    Technisch Ontwerp

    Versie

    Introduction and goals¶

    The Technisch Ontwerp (TO) is the technical design of Gemeenschappelijke Bronontsluiting (GBO). It describes the GBO facilities (voorzieningen) and interfaces (koppelvlakken). The TO goes one level deeper than the Globaal Ontwerp (GO) and stays within the frameworks of the Projectstartarchitectuur (PSA).

    The TO uses the arc42 template. It records how the GBO components are built. For why GBO exists and what it must do, see the PSA introduction and the GO solution direction.

    Baseline: the demo at v0.9.0¶

    The reference implementation gbo-demo is the ground truth for the behavior of GBO. This version of the TO is pinned to demo tag v0.9.0 (November 2, 2026). Every statement about behavior links to code or a test at that tag. Each divergence between the design and the implementation has a record in one of these places:

    • an architecture decision,
    • a finding,
    • an entry in Risks and technical debt.

    Earlier work in the TO¶

    The TO is the standalone reference for the technical design of GBO. It absorbs two earlier bodies of work:

    • The reference architecture v0.6.2 (archived and unpublished). The ADR log holds its decisions. This includes the decisions that the implementation superseded later.
    • The traceability work that ran next to the demo. The TO holds its requirements, findings, open questions, demo increments, and design-to-demo matrix. How to trace explains how the IDs link.

    The IDs did not change (REQ-NN, RL-NN, AV-NN, BSNK-NN, F-NN, Q-NN, SL-NN). A reader who knows an old ID finds it under the same number.

    How this document is organized¶

    The TO has three parts:

    Part Content
    arc42 sections 1 to 12 The design: constraints, context, strategy, building blocks, runtime scenarios, deployment, crosscutting concepts, decisions, quality, risks, and glossary.
    Requirements Testable demands on what GBO builds and on its interfaces (REQ), guidelines for bronhouders (RL), candidate connection conditions (AV), and BSNk preconditions (BSNK).
    Traceability The chain from design to demo: the matrix, demo increments (SL), findings (F), open questions (Q), and feedback to standards bodies (E1 to E10).

    Each arc42 page and each ADR ends with a "Traceability" section. This section lists the requirements, findings, open questions, and demo increments that the page explains or depends on.

    Routes¶

    GBO gives bronhouders one technical backbone for several data flows. A bronhouder is a government organization that holds an authentic source. A bronhouder exposes a GraphQL API behind an FSC Inway. Every request passes the same chain: the FSC Inway as PEP, the PDP of the source, the source gateway, and the source API. The routes differ at the consumer edge and in the evidence that a request carries. The evidence selects the authorization regime (ADR-0031).

    gbo-demo v0.9.0 implements three routes end to end:

    • DvTP (Delen van gegevens via Toestemming met Private dienstverleners). A citizen gives consent, and a private consumer requests source data under that consent. The consumer never holds a citizen identifier. An integrator can call on behalf of the consumer under FSC delegation (ADR-0034). A second consumer pilot runs on the same chain: the Installatie Register asks the LVG source about ownership (rule LVG0001). See DvTP query.
    • EUDI issuance (PuB-EAA route). A citizen discloses a PID from the EUDI wallet and gets an attestation from a government source. The bronhouder is the PuB-EAA provider. GBO operates the technical issuance facility (ADR-0028). The demo proves this route, but the PSA treats wallet support (P-06) as a hook outside version 1. See EUDI issuance.
    • ASI verification (eIDAS Article 45e). A QTSP verifies or retrieves attributes at the Authentic Source Interface, as specified in ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1. The QTSP is an OAuth client and does not take part in FSC. The ASI provider calls the source over FSC (ADR-0037). The route is demo grade: it uses a stub register, development certificates, and a DigiD mock. See ASI verification.

    Three routes exist at design level only (design-level scenarios):

    • Gov-to-Gov: exchange between government parties on a legal basis. The legal-basis regime needs its own positive evidence. No rule set exists for this regime.
    • SDG-OOTS: cross-border evidence exchange through an AS4 bridge (ADR-0020).
    • Relying-party presentation: the citizen presents a wallet attestation to a relying party. This route has no GBO runtime.

    For the interaction patterns (interactiepatronen) behind these routes, see the GO.

    Quality goals¶

    The technical design has five main quality goals, in order of priority. Quality requirements refines them into testable scenarios. Each goal has the following effect on the design:

    Priority Quality goal What it means for the design
    1 Data minimization The query of the consumer is the authorization object. The PDP decides on each requested field. It denies a field that no rule of the active regime covers (REQ-17, REQ-48). See P-02.
    2 Privacy (BSN-free) In DvTP, the consumer gets no BSN and no other citizen identifier. The query names the subject with a placeholder. As a result, the PDP input and the decision logs hold no identity (REQ-20, REQ-79). EUDI and ASI are an exception: the plain BSN is in the PDP input and in both decision logs (REQ-60 not met). ADR-0043 (proposed) records the fix. See P-04.
    3 Verifiable authorization A policy engine decides every data request. Application code does not make this decision. Each decision is allow or deny with a reason code. The consumer and the decision record get a coarse code. The operator gets the rule code per field (REQ-06, ADR-0036). See S05.
    4 Traceability One W3C trace ID links the processing records of all controllers. Next to it, the records hold the FSC transaction ID, which links the transport records (REQ-55, ADR-0035). In demo v0.9.0, the link to the decision record behind the FSC Inway is missing (risk R23). See P-12.
    5 Bronhouder autonomy Sources own their schema, their service description, their decryption keys, and their policy. PAP and PDP are at the bronhouder (ADR-0021). GBO keeps no copy of source data (REQ-11). See P-10.

    Stakeholders¶

    For the parties involved and the impact of GBO on them, see GO chapter 6. The TO has three primary audiences:

    • Engineers who build or integrate GBO components.
    • Bronhouder teams that connect a source.
    • Reviewers who check that the implementation stays within the PSA frameworks.

    Constraints¶

    Four sources set the constraints for this design: the PSA, the law, the GDI standards, and the functional requirements for DvTP. Each constraint links to its normative text, and the TO does not restate that text. If a design element conflicts with a constraint, one of these records the conflict:

    • an entry in Risks and technical debt,
    • a finding,
    • an architecture decision.

    Architecture principles (PSA)¶

    The 16 architecture principles of the PSA bind this design. The PSA page has no anchor per principle. For this reason, each link opens the principles page. The following principles constrain the technical design most directly:

    ID Principle Bearing on the TO
    P-01 Legal basis before exchange Before data flows, the PDP judges every request under a regime. The evidence in the request selects the regime (ADR-0031).
    P-02 Minimal data processing The PDP decides on each field of the GraphQL query (REQ-17).
    P-04 BSN-free for private consumers In DvTP, the consumer holds no citizen identifier. After the allow decision, the source decrypts its own value (ADR-0033). See Pseudonymization.
    P-06 Support for the EUDI wallet The PSA treats this principle as a hook outside version 1. The demo still proves EUDI issuance and ASI verification.
    P-07 Trust through recognized admission and trust anchors (until September 2026: "trust framework based on PKI") Every FSC connection uses mTLS with PKI certificates. Admission comes from a register (REQ-61). The legal identity comes from the certificate (REQ-67). See Identity and trust.
    P-09 Open standards and vendor independence The design uses FSC, AuthZEN, OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP, GraphQL, OPA, LDV, W3C Trace Context, and OAuth 2.0.
    P-10 Data sovereignty: the bronhouder keeps control Sources own their schema, service description, decryption keys, and policy. PAP and PDP are at the bronhouder (ADR-0021).
    P-12 Logging and non-repudiation The design has three authoritative records, one per Logius standard. The ADL holds the authorization decisions (ADR-0036). The LDV logbook of each controller holds the processings (ADR-0026). FSC-Logging holds the transport. The W3C trace ID joins the three records, and the FSC transaction ID is recorded next to it (ADR-0035). See Logging, audit and traceability.
    P-13 Transparency and access for the citizen The citizen views and revokes consents (REQ-38). Each controller can answer an access request from its LDV logbook.
    P-14 Separation of generic and specific functions GBO has one generic chain. Route-specific adapters are at the edge (REQ-44).

    For the full list (P-01 to P-16) and the status of each principle in the demo, see the matrix.

    Design principles (PSA)¶

    The 14 design principles govern how the GBO components are built. Each link opens the design principles page. The following design principles constrain the TO most directly:

    ID Principle Bearing on the TO
    D-01 Decentral where possible, central where necessary Each bronhouder has its own PDP and PAP. Each provider issues its own tokens. GBO has central components only where they are necessary: the consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) and the admission register.
    D-03 Use national generic facilities (GDI) unless GBO reuses FSC, FTV, BSNk PP, DigiD, and PKIoverheid and does not rebuild them. The demo mocks DigiD, BSNk, and MijnOverheid.
    D-07 Open source unless All GBO components and the demo are open source (EUPL).
    D-08 Comply or explain: mandatory open standards A deviation from a mandated standard is an explicit ADR or risk.
    D-09 API-first All interfaces (koppelvlakken) are specified APIs. See Context and scope.
    D-11 Least privilege Authorization is closed-world: without a rule, there is no access. Only the FSC Inway reaches the source gateway (REQ-81).
    D-13 Standardize where possible, make exceptions explicit Exceptions to a standard are visible in the data and in the ADR log. An example is the file metadata transport (AV-08).

    For the full list (D-01 to D-14), see the matrix.

    Requirements¶

    The requirements state testable demands on what GBO builds and on the interfaces between GBO and other parties. Each requirement names its source. The source is a passage in the GO, the PSA, or FR-DvTP, or a principle for which a demo finding showed the need. The arc42 sections explain how the design meets the requirements. The status of each requirement is one of these words: draft, ready for review, approved, covered, or withdrawn.

    The requirements page also lists the guidelines for bronhouders (RL-01 to RL-05). A guideline is a recommendation for bronhouders. It puts no demand on GBO.

    Connection conditions (candidates)¶

    Some demands fall on the parties that connect to GBO, and GBO itself does not carry them. The TO collects these demands as candidate connection conditions (AV-01 to AV-15). They are input for the management organization, which sets the real connection conditions (PSA S04).

    The candidates apply to three types of party:

    Party Candidates
    Consumer AV-01 trace context, AV-02 LDV, AV-03 consent facility and BSNk PP, AV-04 own FSC peer. AV-05 proof sent unchanged, AV-14 contact details for GDPR rights, AV-15 equivalent alternative.
    Integrator AV-06 admitted separately, acts as processor
    Bronhouder AV-07 to AV-13: service description, consent to a taken-over description, old decryption keys, LDV for relation attestations, and validity and revocation policy

    BSNk preconditions¶

    BSNk PP sets preconditions that the DvTP design must respect (BSNK-01 to BSNK-11). These preconditions are facts about an external facility. They are not requirements on GBO. Three of them shape the design most:

    • Transformation is possible only while the citizen is logged in (BSNK-04). As a result, the consent facility makes all values at consent time, and the proof freezes at consent (F-78).
    • Only a recognized party can activate and transform (BSNK-01). It is open whether the consent facility can be such a party (Q-26, Q-49).
    • The interfaces are SOAP with PKIoverheid (BSNK-11). The demo mock offers the same operations as JSON.

    How the register finds a returning citizen is an open design choice. The working assumption is route D (ADR-0040, proposed).

    Functional requirements DvTP (FR-DvTP v0.9)¶

    FR-DvTP v0.9 contains the functional requirements FR-01 to FR-39 for the DvTP route. The document is not public. For this reason, the TO names a criterion without a link, for example "FR-34, criterion 1". The matrix gives the demo status per FR.

    FR-DvTP v0.9 has known contradictions. If the text and a decision conflict, the requirements follow the decision. The known contradictions are:

    • FR-22 to FR-24 name the same consent statuses with different words. The rationale of FR-23 contradicts its criteria (F-97).
    • FR-39 puts policy at a central authority, and FR-26 puts it at a central authorization component. FR-25 ties the GDPR pointer to "revocation no longer possible". FR-35 describes a register content that the design does not use (F-98).

    Legal and regulatory constraints¶

    The PSA groups its principles by legal framework. The following frameworks constrain this design:

    Constraint Source Bearing on the TO
    AVG (GDPR) PSA architecture principles, framework 1 Data minimization, purpose limitation (doelbinding), and legal basis (grondslag). Each controller (Verantwoordelijke) logs its own processing (ADR-0026).
    Digital Government Act (Wdo) and PKIoverheid PSA framework 3 Organization identity through PKI certificates and the OIN.
    eIDAS2 and ARF PSA framework 4 EUDI wallet support. Article 45e: the Authentic Source Interface (ADR-0037).
    eIDAS implementing regulations of 2026 (ASI) CIR (EU) 2025/1569 art. 9, CIR (EU) 2026/1735 Annex IV Art. 9 applies from August 19, 2026. From January 1, 2027, the verify interface follows ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1.1, clause 6.2.3, or both. From that date, every result is sealed. The authorization part stays a national choice (F-80).
    eIDAS implementing regulations of 2026 (PuB-EAA) CIR (EU) 2026/1735 (ETSI TS 119 471), CIR (EU) 2026/1731 (ETSI TS 119 412-6, TS 119 472-3), CIR (EU) 2026/1730, and CIR (EU) 2025/848 PuB-EAA issuance falls under the same standard as QEAA issuance. The issuer needs designation and a registration with entitlement PUB_EAA_Provider. It also needs an access certificate, a registration certificate, and a qualified seal certificate with its own profile (F-81, Q-28).
    BSN legislation (Wabb) PSA framework 6 Private parties must not process the BSN. This rule drives pseudonymization and the BSN exception for the QTSP (F-86).
    Single Digital Gateway Regulation (EU 2018/1724) GO interaction patterns The OOTS connection over AS4 is an obligation under EU law, and GBO has no choice in it (ADR-0020).

    Standards¶

    The capabilities chapter of the PSA lists the agreements, standards, and facilities (voorzieningen) per capability, with their gaps. See capabilities S01 to S11. The design builds directly on the following standards:

    • Connectivity and authorization: OpenFSC, OpenFTV with OpenID AuthZEN 1.0 and the FTV GraphQL profile, OPA/Rego, GraphQL, and PKIoverheid.
    • Pseudonymization: BSNk PP.
    • EUDI issuance: OpenID4VCI, OpenID4VP, and SD-JWT VC.
    • ASI verification: ETSI TS 119 478, OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, DPoP (RFC 9449), and JWT access tokens (RFC 9068). ASI verification also uses dynamic client registration (RFC 7591), authorization server metadata (RFC 8414), resource indicators (RFC 8707), rich authorization requests (RFC 9396), and problem details (RFC 9457).
    • Logging and traceability: LDV 1.0.0 (Logboek Dataverwerkingen), ADL (Authorization Decision Log), FSC-Logging (draft), W3C Trace Context, and OpenTelemetry.

    If the demo deviates from a standard that the PSA names, a risk entry records the deviation. For example, the demo uses Rego instead of ODRL as policy language (R16).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-17, REQ-38, REQ-44, REQ-61, REQ-67, REQ-81, RL-01 to RL-05, AV-01 to AV-15, BSNK-01, BSNK-04, BSNK-11
    • Findings: F-78 (open), F-80 (open), F-81 (open), F-86 (open), F-97 (open), F-98 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-26 (open), Q-28 (open), Q-49 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-28 (done), SL-51 (done)

    Context and scope¶

    The GBO technical system connects to external actors and systems. This chapter lists every interface (koppelvlak) on the system boundary and between GBO components. It covers the technical context only. The GO solution direction and the PSA solution direction give the business context: which parties exchange which data, and why.

    Technical context¶

    GBO has the same shape as in the Globaal Ontwerp: external parties use one of the channels, and every channel reaches the source through GBO Basis. The following figure shows who is on the other side of each interface in gbo-demo v0.9.0. Dashed blocks are designed but not built. Click a block to zoom in.

    The interface inventory lists every interface with its protocol and code. The building block view zooms in per channel.

    Four points in these diagrams are easy to misread:

    • Only the portal backend calls BSNk, at consent time. Neither the PDP nor the source gateway calls BSNk. The source reads its own value with its own decryption component (ADR-0033).
    • The PDP gets the consent status over FSC: from its own Outway (peer …0800) to the register's Inway (peer …0700). Only the public keys come directly from the register (ADR-0032).
    • The QTSP is not an FSC participant. It is an OAuth client of the ASI authorization server and calls the ASIP over HTTPS. The ASIP is the FSC participant toward the source (F-87, ADR-0037).
    • The ASI has four roles. GBO provides the ASIP and the authorization server. The Discover Interface and the QTSP are external. For these two roles, the demo has a stub and a reference client. It is open who operates the ASIP and the authorization server (Q-37).

    Interface inventory¶

    Every interface has a row in one of the tables in the following sections. A row gives the standard that the interface follows and its implementation in gbo-demo. Rows marked designed are not built in demo v0.9.0. Paths in the last column are relative to gbo-demo v0.9.0.

    DvTP consent¶

    The DvTP consent chain uses these interfaces:

    Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in
    Consent initiation Consumer → consent portal (toestemmingsportaal), and back HTTPS redirect with consumer, scopes, purpose, and return URL. The return carries the consent proof in the URL fragment, or status=denied (REQ-37, REQ-119). toestemmingsportaal-frontend
    Citizen login Citizen ↔ consent portal DigiD (mock): the citizen types a test BSN, and the backend signs a portal token with the BSN in sub. Real DigiD gives the identity in an assertion (REQ-24). portalhttp
    Consent registration Portal backend ↔ consent register (toestemmingsregister) REST: POST /consents, GET /consents?subject_ref=…, GET and DELETE /consents/{id}, GET and PUT /subjects/{ref}/polymorphic. No BSN crosses this interface (REQ-23, REQ-39). consent-register/main.go
    BSNk PP Portal backend → BSNk /v2/activate, /v2/transform, and /v2/bsn-authorisation-list. The mock follows the BSNk interface as JSON and does not encrypt. Production BSNk uses SOAP with PKIoverheid (BSNK-11). bsnk-mock
    Consent proof Consumer → Inway → PDP and source gateway Signed JWT gbo-consent+jwt (ES256) in the X-GBO-Consent-Token header, with encrypted_subject per source. The query names the subject with the placeholder consent:identity or consent:pseudonym (REQ-79, AV-05). consent_token.go
    Consent keys PDP → consent register GET /.well-known/jwks.json, cached for 300 s consent.rego
    Consent status PDP Outway (…0800) → register Inway (…0700) FSC service consent-status: GET /consents/{id}/status on a status-only listener, with no cache and a 2 s timeout. The register refuses a call without an FSC peer (REQ-76). status.go, Makefile

    Authorization and FSC¶

    The authorization chain and the FSC group use these interfaces:

    Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in
    Data request Consumer Outway ↔ bronhouder Inway FSC (OpenFSC v2.4.0): mTLS, access token, and grant hash. Grants carry no properties. fsc-infra
    Delegated data request Integrator Outway ↔ bronhouder Inway FSC DelegatedServiceConnectionGrant, signed by the integrator, the represented consumer, and the provider (REQ-106) seed-bri-delegation-int.sh
    Authorization Inway (PEP) ↔ PDP OpenID AuthZEN 1.0, POST /authzen/v1/evaluation over HTTPS. The Inway passes the raw body, and the PDP maps it per the FTV GraphQL profile (REQ-42). openftv-pdp
    Contract decision Provider Manager → PDP AuthZEN autosign request for each submitted contract (REQ-62) autosign.rego
    Participant admission PDP ← admission register OpenFTV PIP pull, GET /internal/openftv/participants, every 5 s, on a network that only the PDP shares (REQ-61) dvtp-onboarding.yaml

    Bronhouder¶

    The bronhouder uses these interfaces:

    Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in
    GraphQL source API Source gateway ↔ source GraphQL over HTTP, POST /graphql. Only the Inway can reach the gateway (REQ-81). graphql-server, brp-graphql-server, lvg-graphql-server
    Source decryption Source gateway → decryption component of the source POST /signed-encrypted-identity and POST /signed-encrypted-pseudonym. The component calls no other service (REQ-21). decryption.go
    Source metadata Reconciler ← source GET /.well-known/gbo over a separate FSC metadata service, per gbo-source-metadata 1.0 or 1.1 (REQ-64) schema, source_metadata.go

    EUDI issuance¶

    EUDI issuance uses these interfaces:

    Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in
    Wallet issuance EUDI wallet ↔ issuance server OpenID4VCI with OpenID4VP disclosure, SD-JWT VC (dc+sd-jwt) eudi-issuance-server (nl-wallet v0.5.0)
    Attestation data Issuance server → EUDI adapter POST /attestations/{source_id}/{type_id} over public HTTPS. In demo v0.9.0, this route has no caller authentication (REQ-45, #133). source_release_runtime.go
    Offer catalog Frontends ← EUDI adapter GET /eudi-offers.json. If a source is stale, the adapter returns 503. source_release_runtime.go
    Type metadata Wallet ecosystem ← EUDI adapter GET /types/{source-id}/{type-id}/v{n}, immutable, vct#integrity type_metadata.go
    Source registry EUDI adapter, issuance init step, ASIP ← source registry PostgreSQL, read-only role on releases and the active pointer source-registry
    QTSP test statement Issuance server → reference QTSP Callback on a secret path over CA-pinned HTTPS (use case qtsp-attestation). Demo scaffolding. qtsp_issuance.go

    Authentic Source Interface¶

    The Authentic Source Interface uses these interfaces:

    Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in
    ASI discovery QTSP ↔ Discover Interface, and Discover Interface ← ASIP records ETSI TS 119 478 clause 5.3 and Annex A. dataService records (clause 5.3.3) at /<ds>/dataservices (REQ-99). asi-discovery-stub (stub), asi-provider
    ASI contract QTSP ← ASIP ETSI Annex B OpenAPI with completions. x-oauth-authorization-server names the authorization server (REQ-100). asi-provider/openapi
    ASI server metadata QTSP, ASIP ← authorization server RFC 8414 metadata and JWKS asi-authorization-server
    QTSP registration QTSP → authorization server RFC 7591 POST /register with a software statement sealed by the QTSP certificate (x5c, registryURI) (REQ-88) asi-authorization-server
    Entitlement lookup Authorization server → register of relying parties Lookup on registryURI for the entitlement QEAA_Provider (CIR 2025/848). The demo reads a stub file (F-85). register.json
    ASI authorization Citizen browser ↔ authorization server ↔ QTSP OAuth 2.0 code flow, PKCE S256, RFC 8707 resource (exactly one data service), optional RFC 9396 authorization_details (REQ-90, REQ-95) asi-authorization-server
    Citizen identification Wallet ↔ wallet verifier ↔ authorization server OpenID4VP, PID urn:eudi:pid:nl:1. A DigiD mock is the second means (REQ-102). asi-wallet-verifier, digidmock
    ASI token Authorization server → QTSP → ASIP RFC 9068 JWT (ES256), DPoP (RFC 9449), private_key_jwt (REQ-86, REQ-87) accesstoken
    ASI verify and retrieve QTSP ↔ ASIP ETSI TS 119 478 clauses 6.1.1 and 6.1.2 at /<ds>/authsrc-api/verify and /retrieve. Errors follow RFC 9457. The seal is in X-JWS-Signature (detached JWS) (REQ-83, REQ-112). handler.go
    ASIP source query ASIP Outway (…1200) ↔ provider Inway FSC and AuthZEN (rule ASI0001). One GraphQL query per request. graphqlsource
    ASI source description Reconciler ← source, and ASIP ← source registry gbo-source-metadata 1.1, capability asi. The ASIP reads a release snapshot. asi-mapping, source-registry

    Logging and audit¶

    Logging and audit use these interfaces:

    Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in
    Decision records PDP → ADL, and reader → ADL Logius ADL in Postgres ftv_adl. Readers use a SELECT-only role (REQ-71). adl-reader.sql, adl.go
    Processing records Component → logbook of its controller LDV v1.0.0 write, POST /logboek/records, over HTTPS with JSON and a bearer write token (REQ-72) ldv-client
    Processing-record read Auditor, portal → logbook LDV read extension, POST /data-processing-operations on trace ID, processing activity, or data subject. A read is possible with a read token only. ldv-logboek
    Transaction logs Auditors ← txlog of each peer FSC txlog API, GET /v1/logs over mTLS. The demo reads the txlog API inside each organization. Access in production is an open question (F-42, Q-08). fsctxlog.go
    Trace context Every component → next hop W3C traceparent. Fsc-Transaction-Id is recorded next to it (REQ-55). tracecontext.go
    Telemetry All services → collector OpenTelemetry OTLP collector-config.yaml

    Designed¶

    Two interfaces are designed but not built in demo v0.9.0:

    Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in
    OOTS evidence exchange EU access points ↔ OOTS adapter AS4/eDelivery and OOTS-EDM. This interface is designed. For more information, see ADR-0020 and Q-79. —
    Government data request Government consumer ↔ bronhouder Inway FSC with its own positive evidence. This interface is designed. For more information, see design-level scenarios. —

    Scope¶

    The demo implements three routes end to end, at demo grade:

    1. The DvTP query under consent, with an integrator variant and the LVG pilot as a second consumer and source.
    2. EUDI issuance of PuB-EAA attestations.
    3. ASI verification and retrieval for QTSPs (ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1).

    Two routes are design-level: SDG-OOTS and Gov-to-Gov. The runtime view has a scenario for each.

    This design covers the following parts of the system:

    • the authorization chain: PEP, PDP, PIPs, policies, and contract decisions
    • the consent chain: portal, register, consent proof, and status service
    • pseudonymization at consent time and decryption at the source
    • the FSC group configuration and the admission register
    • EUDI issuance, source onboarding, and the source registry
    • the Authentic Source Interface: ASIP, authorization server, and discovery records
    • logging, audit, and observability

    The following parts are out of scope:

    • the internal architecture of bronhouder systems behind the GraphQL API
    • the EUDI wallet, DigiD, and BSNk themselves
    • the QTSP, the Discover Interface, and the national register of relying parties
    • the relying-party side of wallet presentations, which touches no GBO infrastructure
    • the EU OOTS common services

    The developer tooling of the demo is scaffolding: the developer portal, the consumer mocks, keyper-mock, and the reference QTSP. This tooling is outside the target architecture. The deployment view marks each unit as target architecture or scaffolding.

    • Requirements: REQ-21, REQ-23, REQ-24, REQ-37, REQ-42, REQ-45, REQ-55, REQ-61, REQ-64, REQ-71, REQ-72, REQ-76, REQ-79, REQ-81, REQ-83, REQ-86 to REQ-88, REQ-99, REQ-100, REQ-102, REQ-106, REQ-112, BSNK-11, AV-05
    • Findings: F-42 (closed), F-85 (open), F-87 (open)

    Solution strategy¶

    The design rests on the pillars in the following tables. Each pillar links to the decisions that record its rationale and to the page that gives the details. The pillars realize the capabilities of the PSA within the solution shape of the GO. gbo-demo v0.9.0 implements every pillar that is marked "built".

    The generic chain¶

    Pillar Approach Decisions Detail
    Data access Each bronhouder has one GraphQL API. The query is the authorization object. ADR-0001, ADR-0025 Building blocks
    Connectivity All domestic traffic uses FSC. Protocol adapters at the edge handle all other traffic. ADR-0003 Deployment view
    Authorization The FSC Inway is the PEP. OPA/Rego in OpenFTV is the PDP, behind AuthZEN with the FTV GraphQL profile. Authorization has five separable concerns and one PDP per bronhouder. There is no central authorization server. Rules are plain Rego, bound by regime, FSC service, and field. ADR-0002, ADR-0004, ADR-0009, ADR-0013 Authorization
    Regime from evidence The evidence that a request carries selects the regime. A consent proof gives the consent regime. Without a consent proof, the PID regime applies. Grants carry no properties. ADR-0031 Regime selection
    Admission A register admits parties. The decision policy does not admit parties. A separate policy decides on FSC contracts. An integrator connects under FSC delegation with a registered mandate. ADR-0015, ADR-0034 Admission and activation
    Policy management Each bronhouder manages and distributes its own policy. GBO supplies a reference policy set and guidelines (RL-01 to RL-05). GBO does not supply a central PAP. ADR-0021 Policy lifecycle
    Source onboarding Sources publish their own service description. A reconciler validates the description, and an operator activates it. A valid contract alone does not activate a source. ADR-0016 Source onboarding

    Consent and pseudonymization (DvTP)¶

    Pillar Approach Decisions Detail
    Consent proof A signed consent proof carries an encrypted value per source. The consumer names the subject with a placeholder. For every request, the policy verifies the proof and asks for the status online over FSC. ADR-0032 Consent, DvTP query
    Pseudonymization The design uses BSNk PP only at consent time. After the allow decision, the source gateway decrypts the value for its own OIN. Only the FSC Inway reaches the gateway. The consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) recognizes the citizen by its own keyed reference (route D, proposed). ADR-0005, ADR-0033, ADR-0040 Pseudonymization

    EUDI routes¶

    Pillar Approach Decisions Detail
    EUDI issuance Issuance is disclosure-based OpenID4VCI on the nl-wallet stack. Sources feed it over FSC under the PID regime. The bronhouder is the PuB-EAA provider, and GBO operates the facility. Built. The PSA treats wallet support (P-06) as a hook outside version 1. ADR-0018, ADR-0017, ADR-0028 EUDI issuance
    ASI verification An OAuth front door as specified in ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1 (verify, retrieve, authorization server). The QTSP is an OAuth client and does not take part in FSC. The design has one data service per authentic source and one token per data service. The source describes its ASI attributes. Built, demo grade. ADR-0037, ADR-0038, ADR-0039 ASI verification

    Audit and traceability¶

    Pillar Approach Decisions Detail
    Audit The design has three authoritative records: the ADL for authorization decisions, the LDV logbook of each controller for processings, and FSC-Logging for transport. Observability tools are not audit records. ADR-0036, ADR-0026 Logging, audit and traceability
    Traceability W3C Trace Context is the correlation key. Each component records the FSC transaction ID next to the trace ID. ADR-0035 Correlation

    Design-level and proposed elements¶

    Two strategy elements exist at design level only. Both reuse the generic chain:

    • The AS4 bridge for SDG-OOTS (ADR-0020) is a protocol adapter in front of the same FSC and authorization chain.
    • Gov-to-Gov needs its own positive evidence for the legal-basis regime (ADR-0031). No rule set exists for this regime (R3).

    Four decisions have the status proposed. Each one waits for an open question or a demo issue:

    • ADR-0040, citizen recognition, waits for Q-49.
    • ADR-0041, seal format of ASI results, waits for Q-32.
    • ADR-0042, per-attribute token binding, waits for Q-33.
    • ADR-0043, identifiers out of the PDP input, waits for demo issue #368.

    Traceability¶

    • Findings: F-70 (open), F-79 (open), F-87 (open), F-89 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-21 (answered), Q-32 (open), Q-33 (open), Q-38 (partly answered), Q-49 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-28 (done), SL-45 (done), SL-46 (done), SL-47 (done), SL-48 (done), SL-50 (done), SL-51 (done)

    Building block view

    Building block view¶

    GBO has one base and three channels. GBO Basis sits at every bronhouder and opens the source in one standard way. The DvTP, EUDI and OOTS channels each serve a different kind of consumer, and GBO Basis feeds all three. This picture is the overview of the Globaal Ontwerp, with the state of gbo-demo v0.9.0 added.

    Each block with a thick border is clickable and zooms in one level. The levels go from this overview, to one page per block, to the component catalog with the code.

    The blocks¶

    The overview has seven GBO blocks. Five of them run in the demo:

    Block What it does In demo v0.9.0 Zoom in
    Generic source access Opens a source over FSC with GraphQL. The PDP of the source decides on every request, field by field. Built GBO Basis
    Source configuration The source describes its own services. GBO validates the description and activates it as a release. Built Source configuration
    GBO tools Help a bronhouder that cannot offer GraphQL, through a translation layer. Design only ADR-0027
    Consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) The citizen gives, views and revokes consent. The register signs a consent proof for the consumer. Built, with a DigiD mock DvTP channel
    PuB-EAA provider Issues an attestation from source data to the wallet of the citizen. Built on the nl-wallet stack PuB-EAA provider
    ASI provider Lets a QTSP verify or retrieve an attribute at the source (eIDAS article 45e). Built, demo grade ASI provider
    OOTS adapter Answers an EU evidence request with source data. Design only OOTS channel

    The pseudonymization facility BSNk PP (pseudonimiseervoorziening) and the QTSP are not GBO components. GBO uses them. The demo runs a mock of BSNk PP.

    How GBO Basis feeds every channel¶

    Every channel reaches the source in the same way. A channel component calls the source through its own FSC Outway. At the source, GBO Basis decides and only then asks the source:

    flowchart LR subgraph ch["Channel (one of three)"] direction TB c1("Consumer backend<br/>DvTP") c2("EUDI adapter<br/>PuB-EAA") c3("ASIP<br/>ASI") end out["Outway of the caller"] subgraph gb["GBO Basis at the source"] direction LR pep("FSC Inway<br/>PEP") pdp("PDP<br/>policy per field") gw("Source gateway") end api[("Source API")] subgraph rec["Records"] direction TB adl[("ADL<br/>decision")] ldv[("LDV<br/>processing")] txl[("FSC txlog<br/>transport")] end c1 & c2 & c3 --> out out -- "1 · mTLS + FSC token" --> pep pep -- "2 · AuthZEN question" --> pdp pdp -- "3 · allow or deny" --> pep pep -- "4 · only after allow" --> gw gw -- "5 · query" --> api pdp -.-> adl api -.-> ldv pep -.-> txl %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class c1 ext class c2,c3 eudi class out,pep,pdp,gw basis class api source class adl,ldv,txl store class pep,pdp,gw zoom style gb fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click pep "gbo-basis/" "GBO Basis" click pdp "gbo-basis/authorization/" "Authorization" click gw "gbo-basis/source-access/" "Source access"

    Figure 2: One path to the source for all channels. Dotted lines: the three audit records.

    The channels differ in the evidence that a request carries. The evidence selects the rules that the PDP applies, and it decides how the source learns who the citizen is:

    Channel Evidence in the request Rules How the source gets the citizen
    DvTP A consent proof, signed by the consent register (toestemmingsregister) DVT0001, LVG0001 The source decrypts its own value from the proof
    PuB-EAA issuance No consent proof: PID regime EUD0001, EUD0002 The adapter puts the BSN from the PID of the wallet in the query
    ASI No consent proof: PID regime ASI0001 The ASIP puts the BSN from its access token in the query

    For the regime rule, see ADR-0031. For the five rules, see Authorization.

    Two ways down¶

    This view goes down by block: from a channel to its components. The crosscutting concepts go down by theme. The following table shows where each theme lives in the blocks:

    Theme GBO Basis DvTP PuB-EAA ASI
    Authorization PEP, PDP and rules DVT0001, LVG0001 EUD0001, EUD0002 ASI0001, and an OAuth server of its own
    Consent Status check per request Consent facility Not used Login is the approval
    Pseudonymization Source gateway decrypts Values made at consent BSN from the PID BSN in the token
    Source onboarding Source description, registry Not used eudi capability asi capability
    Identity and trust FSC certificates, admission Admission register Certificate set per source QTSP register, seal
    Logging and audit ADL, LDV, txlog Logbook of the consent facility Logbook of the adapter ADL and source logbook. The ASIP writes no LDV records

    GBO Basis

    GBO Basis¶

    GBO Basis opens a government source in one standard way, for every channel. It runs at the bronhouder: each source has its own FSC Inway, its own PDP and its own source gateway. No central server decides for all sources (ADR-0004). GBO delivers the components, and the bronhouder runs them (P-10).

    Overview › GBO Basis

    Inside GBO Basis¶

    The Globaal Ontwerp names four parts: a standard interface, generic source access, configurable authorization, and GBO tools. The following figure shows the components that make up these parts in gbo-demo v0.9.0:

"status (DvTP only)" .-> tr inway -- "after allow" --> gw gw --> dec gw --> api meta -. "fetched over FSC" .-> reg pdp -.-> rec api -.-> rec %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class caller ext class inway,mgr,pdp,pol,gw,dec basis class api,meta source class adm,reg,rec store class tools planned class tr dvtp class pdp,pol,gw,mgr,meta,reg,rec zoom style bh fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style fsc fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style authz fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style access fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style shared fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB click pdp "authorization/" "Authorization" click pol "policy/" "Policy rules" click mgr "authorization/#admission-of-parties" "Admission" click gw "source-access/" "Source access" click meta "source-configuration/" "Source configuration" click reg "source-configuration/" "Source configuration" click rec "records/" "Records"

    Figure 1: The parts of GBO Basis. Thick border: click to zoom in.

    The parts have the following roles:

    Part Components Role Zoom in
    Standard interface FSC Inway, FSC Manager, FSC Outway of the caller Every connection to a source runs over FSC, with mTLS and a contract (ADR-0003). The Inway is the PEP. FSC group
    Configurable authorization PDP, policy set, admission register The PDP decides on every request and on every contract proposal. Policy is configuration, not code. Authorization
    Generic source access Source gateway, decryption component, source API The source answers one GraphQL query. Under consent, the gateway first puts the citizen in the query. Source access
    Policy rules Policy set, its tests and its distribution The rules are data for the PDP. Each bronhouder manages its own set. Policy rules
    Records ADL, LDV logbooks, FSC txlog Every decision, processing and transport leaves a record, linked by one trace ID. Records
    Source configuration Source metadata, source registry The source describes its own services. GBO validates and activates that description. Source configuration
    GBO tools Translation layer, onboarding toolkit Help a bronhouder without a GraphQL API. Not built. ADR-0027

    The request path¶

    A request through GBO Basis has the same steps in every channel. The PDP decides before anything reaches the source. The source gateway does its work only after an allow:

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Channel participant C as Caller end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the bronhouder participant IN as FSC Inway (PEP) participant PDP as PDP participant GW as Source gateway end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant API as Source API end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant R as ADL, LDV end C->>IN: GraphQL query over FSC (mTLS, token) IN->>PDP: AuthZEN question with the raw body Note over PDP: field list, regime,<br/>rules per field PDP->>R: decision record (ADL) PDP-->>IN: allow or deny alt deny IN-->>C: deny, nothing reaches the source else allow IN->>GW: the judged request opt consent proof present Note over GW: decrypt own value,<br/>replace the placeholder end GW->>API: query API->>R: processing record (LDV) API-->>C: only the selected fields end

    Figure 2: One request through GBO Basis.

    The steps work as follows:

    1. The caller sends a GraphQL query through its FSC Outway. The Inway checks the certificate and the contract of the caller.
    2. The Inway sends the request, with its raw body, to the PDP as an AuthZEN question. The Inway does not read the query (REQ-42).
    3. The PDP turns the query into a list of fields, selects the regime from the evidence, and decides each field. Authorization shows how.
    4. The PDP writes the decision to the ADL, the audit record of decisions (ADR-0036).
    5. On a deny, the source sees nothing. By design, the caller gets a coarse reason code. The FSC Inway of demo v0.9.0 drops that code on the way back.
    6. On an allow, the Inway passes the request to the source gateway. Only the Inway can reach the gateway (ADR-0033).
    7. Under consent, the gateway decrypts the value that the consent proof holds for this source. It puts the BSN or the source pseudonym in the place of the placeholder. Without a consent proof, it passes the query unchanged.
    8. The source runs the query and returns only the selected fields (REQ-08). It logs the processing in its own LDV logbook.

    What the bronhouder runs¶

    GBO delivers the components as reference components. The bronhouder chooses to run them, or a working equivalent that meets the same interfaces. The following figure shows who owns what at one source:

    flowchart TB subgraph own["Owned by the bronhouder"] direction LR api[("Source API<br/>and schema")] meta[("Service description")] keys[("Decryption keys")] log[("LDV logbook")] pol("Policy set<br/>and its management") end subgraph deliv["Delivered by GBO, run by the bronhouder"] direction LR inway("FSC Inway") pdp("PDP") gw("Source gateway") ldvc("LDV client") end subgraph run["Run by GBO for all sources"] direction LR adm[("Admission register")] reg[("Source registry")] tr[("Consent register")] end own ~~~ deliv ~~~ run %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class api,meta,keys,log source class pol,inway,pdp,gw,ldvc basis class adm,reg store class tr dvtp style own fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style deliv fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style run fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB

    Figure 3: Ownership at one source.

    The PEP, the PDP, policy management and source access are decentral, at the bronhouder. The consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) is central and mandatory for DvTP (Q-10, ADR-0021). The PSA has not decided who operates the central facilities (open decisions B-06 and B-17). The demo runs everything in one stack and shares one PDP between the sources. That is a demo shortcut.

    Open points¶

    The main open points in GBO Basis are these:

    • The PID regime has no positive evidence of its own. A request without a consent proof enters it (F-70).
    • The rule "only after the decision" depends on the network. Only the Inway can be allowed to reach the source gateway (F-79).
    • The ADL record holds only what the consumer also sees (F-72).
    • A broken policy module stops every decision, without a visible fallback (F-52).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-04, REQ-08, REQ-42, REQ-46, REQ-81
    • Findings: F-52 (open), F-70 (open), F-72 (open), F-79 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-02 (answered), Q-10 (answered)
    • Demo increments: SL-42 (done), SL-45 (done), SL-51 (done)

    Authorization in GBO Basis¶

    The Globaal Ontwerp calls this part "configurable authorization". Each source has a PDP that decides on every request, field by field, with rules written as policy. The FSC Inway of the source enforces the decision. This page shows the parts, the order of the checks, and the admission of parties. The Authorization concept page has the detail and the links to the code.

    Overview › GBO Basis › Authorization

    Five questions, five places¶

    Authorization answers five separate questions. Each question has its own place in the chain:

    flowchart LR req(["Request"]) subgraph s1["① Organization"] direction TB a1("Is this a known<br/>organization?") b1["FSC connection<br/>mTLS + PKI certificate"] a1 --- b1 end subgraph s2["② Permission"] direction TB a2("Can it use<br/>this service?") b2["FSC Manager<br/>contract after admission"] a2 --- b2 end subgraph s5["⑤ Validity"] direction TB a5("Is the request complete<br/>and well formed?") b5["Request mapper<br/>field list, limits, pins"] a5 --- b5 end subgraph s3["③ Basis"] direction TB a3("Consent<br/>or PID?") b3["Policy<br/>regime from evidence"] a3 --- b3 end subgraph s4["④ Scope"] direction TB a4("Which fields, whose<br/>data, which years?") b4["Policy<br/>rules per field"] a4 --- b4 end src[("Source")] req --> s1 --> s2 --> s5 --> s3 --> s4 --> src %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class req ext class src source class a1,a2,a5,a3,a4 basis class b1,b2,b5,b3,b4 ext class a2,a5,a3,a4 zoom style s1 fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style s2 fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style s5 fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A style s3 fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A style s4 fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A click a2 "#admission-of-parties" "Admission" click a3 "#regime-from-evidence" "Regime" click a4 "#the-rules" "The rules" click a5 "#from-query-to-decision" "Decision pipeline"

    Figure 1: The five authorization questions and where each one is answered. Grey: FSC, once per connection. Green: the PDP of the source, for every request.

    Questions ① and ② belong to FSC and hold for the whole connection. The PDP answers ③ to ⑤ again for every request (ADR-0004). No central authorization server exists.

    The parts¶

    The PEP, the PDP and two PIPs work together as follows:

    flowchart LR out["Outway of<br/>the caller"] subgraph src["At the bronhouder"] direction LR pep("FSC Inway<br/>PEP") subgraph pdp["PDP: OpenFTV v0.1.0"] direction TB map("FTV GraphQL mapper<br/>query → field list") eng("Rego policy<br/>engine + rules") end pout("Outway<br/>of the PDP") gw("Source gateway") end adm[("PIP: admission register<br/>parties, mandates")] tr[("PIP: consent register<br/>keys, consent status")] adl[("ADL")] out -- "request + raw body" --> pep pep -- "AuthZEN" --> map map --> eng eng -- "status, over FSC" --> pout --> tr tr -. "keys (JWKS), cached 5 min" .-> eng adm -. "pulled every 5 s" .-> eng eng --> adl pep -- "only after allow" --> gw %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class out ext class pep,map,eng,pout,gw basis class adm,adl store class tr dvtp class eng,map,tr,adm zoom style src fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style pdp fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click map "#from-query-to-decision" "Decision pipeline" click eng "#the-rules" "The rules" click tr "../../dvtp/consent-service/" "Consent facility" click adm "#admission-of-parties" "Admission"

    Figure 2: PEP, PDP and PIPs at one source.

    The parts have these roles:

    Part Role
    PEP The FSC Inway. Its AuthZEN plugin sends every request with the raw body to the PDP and forwards the request only on an allow. There is no separate PEP service (ADR-0002).
    Request mapper Turns the GraphQL body into a list of fields with their arguments, following the FTV GraphQL profile. It does nothing else (ADR-0013).
    Policy Rego code that selects the regime, checks the consent proof and decides each field. The policy is data for the PDP, so a bronhouder changes it without a new build.
    PIP: consent register (toestemmingsregister) Gives the status of a consent for every request, over FSC. Gives the keys to check the proof. DvTP only.
    PIP: admission register Lists the admitted parties and the mandates of integrators. OpenFTV pulls it every five seconds.

    From query to decision¶

    The PDP takes a fixed series of steps for each request. The first step that fails decides the outcome:

    flowchart TB in(["AuthZEN question<br/>with raw GraphQL body"]) m{"Mapper: complete<br/>field list?"} r{"Regime: how many<br/>consent tokens?"} cv{"Consent proof:<br/>signature, claims, status OK?"} b["Bind rules to each field:<br/>same regime · same FSC service ·<br/>rule names the field"] f{"Every field granted<br/>by a rule?"} allow(["ALLOW<br/>query goes to the source"]) d1(["DENY<br/>COVERAGE_UNVERIFIABLE"]) d2(["DENY<br/>two tokens"]) d3(["DENY<br/>consent reason"]) d4(["DENY<br/>FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED"]) in --> m m -- "no" --> d1 m -- "yes" --> r r -- "two" --> d2 r -- "one: consent regime" --> cv r -- "none: PID regime" --> b cv -- "no" --> d3 cv -- "yes" --> b b --> f f -- "yes" --> allow f -- "no, or no rule at all" --> d4 %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class in ext class m,r,cv,f,b basis class allow basis class d1,d2,d3,d4 dvtp class cv zoom click cv "../../dvtp/consent-service/#the-consent-proof" "Consent proof"

    Figure 3: The decision pipeline of the PDP. Red: deny.

    Three properties of this pipeline matter for the design:

    • Closed world. A field that no rule names is denied (NO_APPLICABLE_RULE). There is no separate catalog of allowed fields: the rules are the catalog (ADR-0009).
    • All or nothing. The PDP allows the request only if it allows every field. It never removes fields from a query.
    • Two layers of reasons. The consumer gets one coarse code, so it cannot learn the schema by trying field names. The administrator of the source sees the reason per field (REQ-06).

    Regime from evidence¶

    The evidence in the request selects the regime. A declared regime or a contract property plays no part (ADR-0031):

    flowchart LR q{"X-GBO-Consent-Token<br/>in the request?"} c["Consent regime<br/>DVT0001 · LVG0001"] p["PID regime<br/>EUD0001 · EUD0002 · ASI0001"] x(["Deny"]) q -- "one" --> c q -- "none" --> p q -- "two" --> x %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class q basis class c dvtp class p eudi class x dvtp

    Figure 4: Regime selection.

    The regime only selects which rules apply. Each rule still checks its own basis: DVT0001 denies without a verified consent, and the PID rules deny if a consent token is present.

    Only consent is positive evidence. A request enters the PID regime because it carries no token (F-70). For that reason, the PID rules admit only named callers: the EUDI adapter and the ASIP. These lists must never contain a DvTP consumer. The fix in the design is a verified PID as positive evidence (REQ-45).

    The rules¶

    Demo v0.9.0 has five rules. Each rule names its regime, the FSC services it serves, and the fields it can grant:

    Rule Regime Service Grants
    DVT0001 consent bri Income declaration fields, per consented year
    LVG0001 consent lvg The ownership check of the LVG pilot
    EUD0001 PID bri Income statement (inkomensverklaring) to the wallet, years 2024 and 2025
    EUD0002 PID brp Death certificate (akte van overlijden) to the wallet
    ASI0001 PID brp The BRP fields behind the ASI attributes, for the ASIP only

    A rule binds to a field only on its own services. A field name such as Query.ingeschrevenPersoon exists in several schemas. Without this binding, a rule for one source grants the same field at another source (REQ-97, F-90).

    Under consent, two checks look inside the query. The citizen must be the placeholder consent:identity, never a real number. Every requested year must have a consented scope, and a query without a year filter is denied. The PDP checks that the citizen comes from the proof. It never learns who the citizen is (F-77).

    Admission of parties¶

    Before a party can send requests, it needs an FSC contract. The FSC Manager of the source asks the same PDP whether to sign it. The contract policy reads the admission register and stops at the first failed check:

    flowchart LR p(["Contract proposal"]) c1{"Well-formed<br/>request?"} c2{"Grant type 2 or 3?"} c3{"Has a<br/>counterparty?"} c4{"Register<br/>available?"} c5{"Party in<br/>the register?"} c6{"Party<br/>active?"} c7{"Admitted for<br/>this source?"} c8{"Delegation<br/>registered?"} ok(["Manager signs"]) no(["Stays proposed<br/>with a reason code"]) p --> c1 --> c2 --> c3 --> c4 --> c5 --> c6 --> c7 --> c8 --> ok c1 & c2 & c3 & c4 & c5 & c6 & c7 & c8 -. "no" .-> no %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class p ext class c1,c2,c3,c4,c5,c6,c7,c8 basis class ok basis class no dvtp

    Figure 5: The eight checks for a contract, in order (ADR-0015).

    Admission is data in a register, not a rule in the policy (REQ-61). An operator admits, pauses or widens a party without a policy change. A refused contract stays proposed, so the party can try again after admission (REQ-63). The contract decides who can connect. The request rules decide what each request can get (REQ-62).

    Open points¶

    The main open points in authorization are these:

    • The PID regime needs positive evidence of its own (F-70, REQ-45).
    • The ADL record does not hold the consent status that the PDP used, so a decision cannot be replayed from the record (F-72).
    • The FSC Inway of demo v0.9.0 loses the reason code on the way back to the consumer (detail).
    • How to model fields, recursion and arguments for future sources (Q-14).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-06, REQ-17, REQ-18, REQ-45, REQ-61, REQ-62, REQ-63, REQ-74, REQ-97
    • Findings: F-70 (open), F-72 (open), F-77 (open), F-90 (resolved in demo)
    • Open questions: Q-14 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-03a (done), SL-45 (done), SL-48 (done)

    Generic source access¶

    The Globaal Ontwerp calls this part "generieke bronontsluiting", which means generic source access. It is the path behind the PEP: after the PDP allows a request, the source gateway passes it to the source API. Under consent, the gateway first puts the citizen into the query. The source answers one GraphQL query and returns only the fields that the query selects. The Pseudonymization and Authorization concept pages have the detail and the links to the code.

    Overview › GBO Basis › Generic source access

    Components behind the PEP¶

    flowchart LR out["Outway of<br/>the caller"] subgraph bh["At the bronhouder"] direction LR pep("FSC Inway<br/>PEP") subgraph pdpg["PDP"] direction TB pdp("Mapper + policy") copy[("Schema copy<br/>and pins")] end subgraph acc["Generic source access"] direction TB gw("Source gateway<br/>bron-sidecar") dec("Decryption<br/>component") end api[("Source API<br/>GraphQL")] log[("LDV logbook<br/>of the source")] end out -- "request + raw body" --> pep pep -- "AuthZEN" --> pdp pdp --- copy pep -- "only after allow" --> gw gw -- "own value" --> dec gw -- "judged query" --> api gw -.-> log api -.-> log %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class out ext class pep,pdp,gw,dec basis class copy,log store class api source class pdp,copy,gw,dec zoom style bh fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style pdpg fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style acc fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click pdp "../authorization/" "Authorization" click copy "#the-pdp-copy-of-the-schema" "Schema copy" click gw "#placeholder-substitution-under-consent" "Substitution" click dec "../../../concepts/pseudonymization/#where-the-boundary-is-enforced" "Pseudonymization"

    Figure 1: The components of generic source access at one source. Thick border: click to zoom in.

    Each component has one job:

    Component Job Never does
    Source gateway Accepts only the request shape that the PDP judged. Under consent, it replaces the placeholder with the own value of the source. Without consent, it passes the query on unchanged. Verifies the consent proof again, or forwards a literal subject under a consent proof
    Decryption component Reads a VI or a VP with the keys of the source. Calls BSNk or another service at query time (REQ-21)
    Source API Runs the GraphQL query and logs the processing in the LDV logbook of its controller. Returns a field that the query did not select (REQ-08)
    Schema copy and pins One copy of the source schema per FSC service, so the PDP can resolve each field. The policy bundle pins its digest. Changes without a new policy bundle

    The source gateway belongs to the source, and each source has its own instance. It sits between the Inway and the API (ADR-0033). The gateway writes two LDV records: one for the decryption and one for the query that it forwards. The answer goes back to the caller through the Inway. A GBO-delivered channel component calls the source again for each request and does not store the answer (REQ-11).

    The transport subset¶

    The PDP judges one form of request. The source gateway accepts only that form, so a request that the PDP never judged cannot run. In demo v0.9.0, the gateway refuses a request in these cases:

    Request Answer of the gateway
    Path other than /graphql 404
    Method other than POST 405
    A query string 400
    A Content-Type that the mapper does not accept 415
    An Upgrade or Content-Encoding header 400

    The path check compares the raw request target byte for byte. It does not clean or decode the path (transport.go). The PDP refuses the same forms. The second check at the gateway covers a request that reaches the gateway by another route.

    Placeholder substitution under consent¶

    Under consent, the consumer does not know who the citizen is. Its query names the citizen with a fixed placeholder. The gateway fills in the citizen after the allow:

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Consumer participant DV as Service provider end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant IN as FSC Inway (PEP) participant PDP as PDP participant GW as Source gateway participant DEC as Decryption component end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant API as Source API end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant L as LDV logbook end DV->>IN: query with consent:identity + consent proof IN->>PDP: AuthZEN question with the raw body Note over PDP: proof valid, subject is<br/>the placeholder, fields allowed PDP-->>IN: allow IN->>GW: the judged request Note over GW: transport subset,<br/>take encrypted_subject[own OIN] GW->>DEC: VI (identity) or VP (pseudonym) DEC-->>GW: BSN or own pseudonym, with the recipient alt recipient is not the own OIN, value missing, or literal subject GW-->>DV: refused, nothing reaches the source else recipient matches Note over GW: replace the placeholder<br/>in the query variables GW->>L: record: decryption GW->>API: query with the BSN API->>L: record: query API-->>DV: only the selected fields end

    Figure 2: Substitution of the placeholder after the allow. The runtime page DvTP query has every hop.

    The query names the form that the source API takes. Each placeholder maps to one value in the consent proof:

    Placeholder Value in the proof Becomes Who gets the value
    consent:identity VI, encrypted_subject[<OIN>].identity The BSN Only a source on the BSN authorization list
    consent:pseudonym VP, encrypted_subject[<OIN>].pseudonym The own pseudonym of the source Every source

    Under a consent, the subject comes only from the proof (REQ-79). The gateway takes only the value for its own OIN. It accepts the result only if the decrypted value names that OIN as the recipient (REQ-80). The key in the proof is not evidence. The value that BSNk made is the evidence.

    The gateway refuses the request in three cases, and the request goes no further:

    • The proof has no value in the requested form, for example no VI for a source that is not on the BSN authorization list.
    • The decrypted value names another recipient.
    • The query names the subject with a literal value under a consent proof.

    Substitution works only on query variables. If the query text holds a literal placeholder, the PDP allows it, the gateway leaves it, and the query finds nobody. In demo v0.9.0, no rule accepts consent:pseudonym, and no source API answers on a pseudonym (#474).

    Pass-through without consent¶

    The evidence decides what the gateway does, as it decides the regime at the PDP. The gateway reads no grant property:

    Evidence in the request Regime at the PDP Gateway
    Consent proof, subject is a placeholder Consent Decrypts its own value and replaces the placeholder
    Consent proof, subject is a literal value Consent Refuses: the PDP denies this, so it arrives only by another route
    No consent proof PID Passes the query on unchanged

    The EUDI adapter and the ASIP send no consent proof. They put the BSN from the PID or from the access token in the query variables themselves. As a result, the BSN is in the PDP input and in both decision logs (REQ-60). The proposed fix keeps identifiers out of the PDP input (ADR-0043).

    Network isolation is the control¶

    The gateway does not verify the consent proof again. The PDP verified it on the same request, and a consumer holds real proofs. So the rule "only after the decision" depends on one thing: nothing but the Inway reaches the gateway (REQ-81):

    flowchart LR out["Outway of<br/>a consumer"] subgraph sg["Network source-gateways"] direction TB pep("FSC Inway<br/>PEP") gw("Source gateway<br/>no published port") end subgraph src["Network sources"] direction TB dec("Decryption<br/>component") api[("Source API")] log[("Source logbook")] end subgraph other["Networks backend and fsc-infra"] direction TB meta("FSC metadata<br/>service") any["Other<br/>containers"] end out -- "mTLS" --> pep pep -- "after allow" --> gw gw --> dec gw --> api gw -.-> log meta -. "direct, demo limit" .-> api any -. "can reach the API,<br/>demo limit" .-> api %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class out,any ext class pep,gw,dec,meta basis class api source class log store class gw zoom style sg fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A style src fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#6F94B8 style other fill:#FFF1F0,stroke:#E28F80,stroke-dasharray:4 3 click gw "../../../deployment/#deployment-units-and-network-zones" "Network zones"

    Figure 3: Network zones around the source gateway in demo v0.9.0. Red: the limits of the isolation.

    In the demo, the gateways publish no port. They are on two Docker networks only. The source Inways share source-gateways with them. The source APIs, the decryption component, and the source logbooks share sources. No consumer is on either network.

    The isolation has three limits (F-79):

    • The source APIs are also on backend and fsc-infra, because the FSC metadata services point at them directly. A container on those networks can reach a source API without the PDP.
    • The Helm chart has no NetworkPolicy. A Kubernetes deployment needs one, or an equivalent control.
    • A nonce that binds a value to one consent, as a second line, is not built.

    The PDP copy of the schema¶

    The source owns its GraphQL schema. The PDP needs the schema to give each field its parent type. So the PDP keeps its own copy, and three controls keep the judged request equal to the executed request:

    flowchart LR subgraph srcs["Source"] s[("Source schema<br/>owned by the source")] end subgraph bundle["Policy bundle"] direction TB m[("PDP copy<br/>one per FSC service")] p[("Schema pins<br/>graphql_schemas.rego")] end subgraph pdpg["PDP"] direction TB map("Mapper<br/>parent types") eng("Engine<br/>pin check") end no(["Deny<br/>SCHEMA_MISMATCH"]) s -- "CI drift check<br/>check-schema-drift.sh" --- m m -- "gen-graphql-pins.sh" --> p m -- "resolve fields" --> map p -- "pinned digests" --> eng map --> eng eng -- "schema not pinned" --> no %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class s source class m,p store class map,eng basis class no dvtp class map zoom style bundle fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style pdpg fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style srcs fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 click map "../../../concepts/authorization/#query-mapping-ftv-graphql-profile" "Query mapping"

    Figure 4: The PDP copy of the schema, the pins, and the drift check.

    The three controls work as follows:

    Control What it does Where
    Schema pins The policy bundle pins the digest of each copy. An evaluation against a schema that is not pinned gets CONFIG_ERROR SCHEMA_MISMATCH. graphql_schemas.rego
    Drift check A CI job compares each copy with the schema that the source runs. check-schema-drift.sh
    Transport subset The gateway runs only the request form that the PDP judged. The transport subset

    The copy has no directives. In demo v0.9.0, the copies are bd.graphql for bri, eudi/brp.graphql for brp, and lvg.graphql for lvg. The year selector is an argument in the schema. As a result, the PDP can check consent per year. A change to a source schema needs a new copy, new pins, and a new policy bundle.

    Invariants that stay at the source¶

    Some rules depend on data that only the source sees. The PDP cannot check them, so the source holds them and their tests.

    The death certificate (akte van overlijden) is the example in the demo. A surviving partner discloses her own PID and gets an attestation about her deceased partner. The BRP source offers the flat view akteVanOverlijden(bsn). The source picks the marriage and the deceased partner. The PDP sees only the output fields of the view (F-47).

    REQ-57 asks for more. The source records the relation in its service description, and the reference policy denies another entry point. A filter that the schema cannot express stays a tested invariant of the source. The test for the death certificate is not built (#425).

    Three demo sources¶

    Demo v0.9.0 has three sources. Each source has its own API, its own gateway, and its own logbook:

    FSC service Source Offers Rules Logbook
    bri Belastingdienst profile (graphql-server, bron-sidecar) Income declarations per year DVT0001, EUD0001 logboek-bd
    brp BRP profile of RvIG (brp-graphql-server, brp-sidecar) Personal record (persoonslijst) and the death certificate view EUD0002, ASI0001 logboek-brp
    lvg LVG mock (lvg-graphql-server, lvg-sidecar) The ownership check vbo(bsn, vboId) { vboId } LVG0001 logboek-lvg

    The demo takes two shortcuts in this part:

    • The three sources share one decryption component.
    • The three sources share one OIN.

    Production needs one decryption component per source, each with its own OIN. Because of the shortcuts, the demo cannot show that the values of two sources are not linkable.

    Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp¶

    The demo follows the Globaal Ontwerp in the use of GraphQL for selective queries. It differs in three places:

    Topic Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0
    Allowed queries A service catalog (dienstencatalogus) lists the allowed queries per application The rules are the catalog: a field that no rule names is denied (ADR-0009)
    Source without GraphQL A GBO translation layer turns an existing API into a GraphQL source Not built. All three sources run GraphQL (ADR-0027, proposed)
    From proof to BSN BSNk PP keeps the BSN away from the private service provider (dienstverlener) The same, and the source gateway converts its own value after the allow. BSNk is not in the query path

    Open points¶

    The main open points in generic source access are these:

    • The isolation of the gateway outside Docker Compose, and a nonce as a second line (F-79).
    • The PDP checks that the subject comes from the proof. It does not check who the subject is (F-77).
    • A relation to another person stays an invariant of the source that the policy cannot check (F-47).
    • In the PID regime, the BSN is in the PDP input and in both decision logs (F-54).
    • How the PDP models fields, recursion, and arguments for future sources (Q-14).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-08, REQ-11, REQ-21, REQ-57, REQ-60, REQ-79, REQ-80, REQ-81
    • Findings: F-47 (open), F-54 (open), F-77 (open), F-79 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-14 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-22 (done), SL-51 (done)

    Source configuration¶

    The Globaal Ontwerp gives each bronhouder a decentral configuration component ("decentraal configuratiecomponent"): the source configures what the central GBO facilities offer for it. In the demo, the source describes its own services in one document. GBO validates that description and activates it as an immutable release. The EUDI adapter, the issuance server and the ASIP read only the active release. The Source onboarding concept page has the detail and the links to the code.

    Overview › GBO Basis › Source configuration

    Components¶
