"../../../runtime/asi-verification/" "ASI verification"

    Figure 1: The components of source configuration. Thick border: click to zoom in.

    Each component has one job:

    Component Job Never does
    Source document Describes the data service, the query, the offers, the claims and the ASI attributes of the source. Holds the GraphQL schema or an access decision
    Source file Names the transport, the metadata location and the FSC Peer ID of the source. Holds the OIN or the organization name
    Source reconciler Fetches the document, validates it, binds it to the data contract, and writes a candidate. It is the only component that fetches source metadata. Calls the Kubernetes API, or activates a source on a contract alone
    Source registry Stores candidates, states, immutable releases and one active pointer. It has a writer role and a read-only role. Stores private key material
    Readers Build a snapshot from the active release and swap it in memory. Fetch source metadata themselves

    The nl-wallet issuance server reads its configuration only at start. A new release therefore needs a controlled restart of that server.

    Who owns what¶

    Four parties own a part of the description of one source. GBO never adds to the part of the bronhouder (REQ-64):

    flowchart LR subgraph own["Owned by the bronhouder"] direction TB doc[("Source document<br/>service, query, offers,<br/>claims, attributes")] cs[("Certificate set<br/>OIN, organization name,<br/>issuer name")] end subgraph agr["Agreed between bronhouder and GBO"] direction TB fsc[("FSC contracts<br/>and grant hashes")] end subgraph opr["Owned by the GBO operator"] direction TB yaml[("Source file<br/>source_id, transport,<br/>location, Peer ID")] end subgraph gbo["Owned by GBO"] direction TB vs[("value_schema per<br/>ASI attribute")] tm[("Type Metadata<br/>generated")] rel[("Candidates, releases,<br/>active pointer")] end own ~~~ agr ~~~ opr ~~~ gbo %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class doc,cs source class fsc ext class yaml,vs,tm,rel store style own fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style agr fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style opr fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style gbo fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#EA580C

    Figure 2: The owners of the parts that describe one source.

    The source file is small. This is the file for the Belastingdienst in demo v0.9.0:

    metadata_endpoint:
  transport: fsc
  provider_peer_id: "99999999900000000200"
  service_reference: gbo-metadata-bd

    The file name is the stable source_id. The legal identity comes from the certificate set under the same key: the OIN from serialNumber and the name from O. GBO refuses a configured value that differs (REQ-67). The data service and the grant hash come from the document and from the FSC contracts in force.

    A source has a metadata leg and a data leg. Each leg selects one of three transports:

    Transport Metadata leg Data leg Use
    fsc Fixed path /.well-known/gbo, through a separate FSC metadata service The data service in the document, under its contract The intended form
    file A document in the metadata directory of the operator Not possible: a file cannot answer a query A source without its own endpoint, as a temporary exception that needs the agreement of the bronhouder (AV-08)
    unsecured An absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL, without FSC headers or redirects An absolute URL Local demonstrations only

    The reconciler refuses fsc metadata with unsecured data. The registry reports one authentication flag per leg. With one flag for both legs, an FSC data call can hide that its description came over an unauthenticated channel.

    Lifecycle of a source¶

    Every reconcile run takes each configured source through the same states. A source fails or ages on its own, without effect on the other sources:

    stateDiagram-v2 direction LR [*] --> pending: run starts,<br/>certificate set found pending --> active: candidate equals<br/>the active release pending --> rollout_required: new valid candidate rollout_required --> active: operator promotes,<br/>immutable release pending --> stale: refresh fails,<br/>previous candidate in grace pending --> blocked: no usable candidate,<br/>or grace over [*] --> blocked: certificate set<br/>missing or invalid classDef ok fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef wait fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef stop fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B class active ok class pending,rollout_required,stale wait class blocked stop

    Figure 3: The states of a source per reconcile run. The next run starts again at pending.

    The run has these steps:

    1. The reconciler loads the certificate set of the source. Without a valid set, the source is blocked before any network call.
    2. For the fsc transport, the reconciler finds the metadata contract and the data contract of the configured peer in the FSC Manager.
    3. It fetches the document with ETag and If-None-Match. A 304 only extends the freshness. It validates every 200 in full.
    4. A valid result becomes a complete candidate. If the candidate differs from the active release, the state is rollout_required.
    5. Promotion writes one release from the complete candidate set. The SHA-256 of the content identifies the release, and the release never changes.
    6. In the same database transaction, promotion sets the singleton active_release_id. If promotion fails, the previous release stays active.
    7. The readers poll the active pointer and swap the new release in memory.

    In the demo, the reconciler promotes by itself (--auto-promote). Automatic promotion is off by default. Compose and the Helm example turn it on, and then the source file is the management action.

    A contract is not activation¶

    A valid FSC contract does not take a source into use. It also does not put the offer of the source in the wallet (REQ-65, F-58). Transport and mandate are two decisions with two owners. Each situation has a fixed result:

    Situation Result
    Valid metadata contract, no source file Nothing happens
    Source file, no metadata contract blocked: METADATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND
    Source file, no contract for the data service blocked: DATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND
    FSC Manager unreachable FSC_MANAGER_UNAVAILABLE. The candidate stays within grace
    Valid candidate without promotion Not active

    Demo v0.9.0 does not build two things. No control decides who can add a source file. No record keeps the admission decision (REQ-123, PSA B-09 in the decision register).

    Freshness, versions and rollback¶

    Source metadata fails closed for each source, ages within fixed bounds, and can be rolled back (REQ-66). The bounds in demo v0.9.0 are these:

    Bound Value
    Fresh after a successful check 15 minutes at most
    Stale grace after that One hour at most
    Validity left at acceptance At least one hour
    Answer for a source past its grace HTTP 503, for that source only

    The issuance route shows X-GBO-Metadata-Cache: fresh or stale. The versioning rules are these:

    • Activation refuses a lower version than the last validated candidate. It also refuses the same version with other content. This rule has no test (#610).
    • A change to claims or display needs a new type_version, because vct#integrity covers the exact bytes of the Type Metadata. GBO never deletes a published type version automatically.
    • An operator rolls back with activate-source-release --release-id. The command refuses a release that the adapter cannot load. An auto-promoter keeps the rollback until new content arrives.

    Demo v0.9.0 has two deviations from the isolation rule (#606). Promotion needs a valid version of every configured source, so one broken source freezes new releases for all sources. The offer list /eudi-offers.json takes the shortest grace of all sources, so it fails for all sources at the same time.

    Policy bundles do not have this lifecycle of validation, bounded staleness, atomic promotion and rollback (F-59). For the policy side, see Policy rules and their management.

    A certificate set per source¶

    Every source has its own certificate set for issuance: an issuer, a reader and a status-list certificate. GBO never shares a set between sources and never substitutes one (REQ-58). The wallet shows the issuer name and the purpose from these certificates. A fallback to the set of another source made the wallet show the wrong issuer (F-50).

    Missing material fails for that source only. Without a set, the source is blocked with CERTIFICATE_SET_NOT_FOUND. A set without an OIN or an organization name gives CERTIFICATE_SET_INVALID. The reconciler gets only public certificates. Only the issuance init container gets the private keys.

    The source document¶

    The document is closed JSON, validated against gbo-source-metadata-v1. Validation refuses unknown fields:

    flowchart LR doc[("Source document<br/>gbo-source-metadata-v1")] env["Envelope<br/>schema_version 1.0 or 1.1<br/>source_oin · version<br/>issued_at · expires_at"] e["capabilities.eudi<br/>one entry per attestation"] a["capabilities.asi<br/>schema 1.1 only"] t["type_id · type_version"] o["offers<br/>fixed parameters"] q["graphql<br/>one read operation,<br/>subject_variable, result_pointer"] c["display · claims<br/>gbo-simple-v1 rule per claim"] as["authentic_source<br/>legal name, country"] aq["graphql<br/>one query ending in ...Selected"] at["attributes<br/>pointer · join · const · each"] gen("Generated by GBO<br/>Type Metadata, VCT path") doc --> env doc --> e doc --> a e --> t & o & q & c a --> as & aq & at c -. "derives" .-> gen %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class doc,env,e,a,t,o,q,c,as,aq,at source class gen eudi

    Figure 4: The structure of the source document.

    A new attestation type, offer or tax year is a change in the document. It needs no change in GBO code, because the adapter takes its parameters from the source (Q-19).

    The eudi capability defines each claim once. GBO derives the mapping and generates the SD-JWT VC Type Metadata from display and claims. As a result, the schema of an attestation cannot differ from what the mapping fills. The VCT of a type version is /types/{source-id}/{type-id}/v{type-version}.

    The asi capability describes the attributes that the ASIP can verify (ADR-0039). Each identifier must exist in the attribute catalog of GBO. If asi has an error, onboarding refuses the whole source, also when eudi is valid. How many sources the ASIP must connect, and how fast, is open (Q-38).

    The document does not hold the GraphQL schema: the PDP keeps its own copy. It also holds no access decision: the rules decide which fields a channel gets. The source does not sign the document. Its origin rests on the authenticated FSC transport and the OIN in the certificate set.

    Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp¶

    The demo follows the idea of the Globaal Ontwerp: the bronhouder configures, and the central facilities read that configuration. It differs in three places:

    Topic Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0
    Form of the configuration A decentral configuration component at the bronhouder One closed JSON document per source at /.well-known/gbo, a proposal for PSA S10 (ADR-0016)
    Findability A service catalog (dienstencatalogus) with a shared profile and central findability, based on DCAT-AP-NL No central findability and no DCAT-AP-NL reference (F-57)
    Channels Every channel reads the configuration EUDI and ASI read it. DvTP does not: the GBO rules hold the DvTP offer (F-74)

    Open points¶

    The main open points in source configuration are these:

    • The description lacks the read API of the logbook of the source, a DCAT-AP-NL reference and central findability (F-57).
    • The file transport has no recorded agreement of the bronhouder (F-71).
    • DvTP scope comes from the demand side and EUDI scope from the supply side (F-74).
    • The central issuance server holds the private keys of every source (Q-17).
    • The ASI attribute identifiers are placeholders until the EU catalog of attributes exists (Q-31).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-58, REQ-64, REQ-65, REQ-66, REQ-67, REQ-123, AV-08
    • Findings: F-50 (closed), F-57 (open), F-58 (closed), F-59 (closed), F-71 (open), F-74 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-17 (open), Q-19 (answered), Q-31 (open), Q-38 (partly answered)
    • Demo increments: SL-32 (done), SL-46 (done), SL-49 (done)

    Policy rules and their management¶

    The Globaal Ontwerp names policy rules ("Beleidsregels") as a block of GBO Basis: policy rules decide who can get which data. Each bronhouder owns, writes and publishes the policy that its own PDP evaluates. GBO supplies a reference policy set, the engine choice, and five guidelines, but no central policy service (ADR-0021). The Policy lifecycle concept page and the Policy distribution runtime page have the detail and the links to the code.

    Overview › GBO Basis › Policy rules

    The policy set¶

    flowchart LR pep("FSC Inway<br/>PEP") mgr("FSC Manager<br/>of the source") subgraph set["Policy set: policies/"] direction LR entry("authz.rego<br/>entrypoint") subgraph eng["Engine and readers"] direction TB e("engine.rego<br/>regime, binding,<br/>closed world") con("consent.rego<br/>consent PIP") pins("graphql_schemas.rego<br/>schema pins") end subgraph rules["Rules"] direction TB r1("rules/dvtp<br/>DVT0001 · LVG0001") r2("rules/eudi<br/>EUD0001 · EUD0002") r3("rules/asi<br/>ASI0001") end auto("fsc/autosign.rego<br/>contract policy") end tr[("Consent<br/>register")] pep -- "AuthZEN" --> entry --> e e --> r1 & r2 & r3 e --- con e --- pins con -. "status over FSC" .-> tr mgr -- "AuthZEN autosign" --> auto %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class pep,mgr,entry,e,con,pins,r1,r2,r3,auto basis class tr dvtp class r1,r2,r3,auto,con,pins zoom style set fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#16A34A style eng fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style rules fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click r1 "../authorization/#the-rules" "The rules" click r2 "../authorization/#the-rules" "The rules" click r3 "../authorization/#the-rules" "The rules" click auto "../authorization/#admission-of-parties" "Admission" click con "../../dvtp/consent-service/#the-consent-proof" "Consent proof" click pins "../source-access/#the-pdp-copy-of-the-schema" "Schema copy"

    Figure 1: The policy set of demo v0.9.0. Thick border: click to zoom in.

    All policy is Rego in version control, with tests next to the rules. The set has four parts:

    Part Files Role
    Entrypoint authz.rego The package that OpenFTV evaluates. It passes only allow and the coarse reason to OpenFTV. It allows the source-metadata fetch for two known peers on the two metadata services
    Engine and readers gbo/engine.rego, gbo/lib.rego, gbo/consent.rego, gbo/graphql_schemas.rego Generic machinery: regime and service binding, the closed world, reason codes, the consent proof, and the schema pins
    Rules gbo/rules/dvtp/, gbo/rules/eudi/, gbo/rules/asi/ One package per access verdict: DVT0001, LVG0001, EUD0001, EUD0002, ASI0001
    Contract policy fsc/autosign.rego Decides for the FSC Manager of the source whether to sign a contract (ADR-0015)

    A new access verdict is a new rule file with tests. The engine does not change. The policy is data for the PDP, so a bronhouder changes it without a new build. The contract policy is a separate rule set from the request policy, in the same bundle (REQ-62).

    Rules use data with four lifecycles. Some data is in the rule itself, for example the years of EUD0001 and the actor lists of the PID rules. The schema digests are in the bundle. The admission register is a PIP that the PDP pulls every five seconds. The consent proof and its status arrive with each request.

    Ownership¶

    The policy belongs to the source (P-10). The question who can manage and publish the policy of a bronhouder has an answer: the bronhouder itself (Q-21, October 28, 2026). Each party has a fixed role:

    Party Does Never does
    Bronhouder Writes, approves and publishes its own policy. Runs its own PAP and PDP. Hands its policy to a central PAP
    GBO Supplies the reference policy set, the engine choice and the guidelines RL-01 to RL-05. Sets requirements on the policy installation of another party
    Another organization that builds or hosts bundles Signs the bundles. The PDP verifies them. Publishes without a signature across the organization boundary

    PSA S06 sets the norm for publication control. The norm asks for an owner, an approver, an effective date, a change history, tests before publication, and an emergency and rollback procedure. Authority over policy is with competent public parties, so the management practices are guidelines. A guideline becomes a requirement only if GBO delivers the management setup itself.

    From version control to the PDP¶

    A policy change goes through a fixed series of checks before the PDP uses it:

    flowchart LR a(["Author edits<br/>a .rego file"]) g[("policies/<br/>with tests")] c["make policy-check<br/>Rego only, unique names,<br/>opa check"] t["make policy-test<br/>opa fmt, opa test"] ci["CI<br/>same checks, generated<br/>files up to date"] d["Distribution<br/>mount or bundle"] p("PDP compiles<br/>the whole set") ok(["Decides,<br/>writes ADL records"]) stop(["PDP does not start"]) br(["Every decision fails<br/>no visible fallback"]) a --> g --> c --> t --> ci --> d --> p p -- "compiles" --> ok c -- "fails" --> stop p -- "one bad module" --> br %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class a ext class g store class c,t,ci ext class d,p,ok basis class stop,br dvtp class d zoom click d "#two-distribution-modes" "Distribution modes"

    Figure 2: From version control to the PDP. Red: failure.

    The PDP compiles the policy set as a whole. One bad module does not give a deny. It breaks every decision (F-52). The demo had this fault several times:

    • A stale policy declared the same package as an existing rule. Every request got HTTP 500.
    • A non-Rego file under policies/ removed every policy after it in walk order.
    • A second file with the same name replaced the first, because the loader keys policies by file name.
    • At hot reload, the PDP reports a module that does not compile as loaded, while the old policy keeps deciding (#151).

    make policy-check is the local safety net. It refuses non-Rego files and duplicate file names, and then it runs opa check. Every make target that starts the PDP depends on it. make policy-test adds opa fmt --diff and opa test. CI repeats these steps. CI also checks that two generated files are up to date: the schema pins and the rule list of the developer portal.

    The contract policy is in the same set. One broken module therefore also stops the admission of new parties. Its package name is fixed (doelbinding.auto_sign_contract). If someone renames it, every contract stays pending without a signal.

    Two distribution modes¶

    The demo gets the policy set to the PDP in one of two modes:

    flowchart LR git[("policies/<br/>version control")] subgraph mount["Mount mode: default"] direction TB bm["Bind mount<br/>./policies"] pdp1("PDP<br/>hot reload") bm --> pdp1 end subgraph bundle["Bundle mode: opt-in"] direction TB seed["seed-openftv-manager.py<br/>deployment identity"] kc["Keycloak<br/>realm gbo"] mgr("OpenFTV Manager<br/>PAP, Cedar on its API") pg[("postgres-ftv<br/>policy + audit trail")] pdp2("PDP<br/>pulls at start") seed -- "short-lived token" --> kc seed -- "write, retire" --> mgr mgr --> pg pdp2 -- "GET /v1/bundle/gbo-pdp" --> mgr end git --> bm git --> seed %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class git store class bm,seed mock class kc ext class mgr,pdp1,pdp2 basis class pg store class pdp1,mgr zoom style mount fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style bundle fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click pdp1 "../../../runtime/policy-distribution/#mount-mode" "Mount mode" click mgr "../../../runtime/policy-distribution/#bundle-mode" "Bundle mode"

    Figure 3: The two distribution modes. Version control is the source of the content in both.

    The two modes differ as follows:

    Mount mode Bundle mode
    How the PDP gets the policy The image carries policies/, and compose bind-mounts ./policies over it The PDP pulls bundle gbo-pdp from the OpenFTV Manager, because PDP_BUNDLE_MANAGER is set
    When a change takes effect At each edit, by hot reload At the next PDP start. make manager-seed restarts the PDP
    Started by Every make demo* target make demo-manager, then make manager-seed
    Version None The bundle has an ID and a version

    Bundle mode has these properties:

    • The PDP pulls, and nothing pushes. The PDP guards its own management endpoints with the decision policy, which denies every request that is not a data request. A push therefore gets HTTP 403 (F-51).
    • The seed script retires policy and does not delete it. It gives every policy that left version control the tag gbo-retired. A delete fails upstream on a foreign key to the audit trail.
    • Cedar policies authorize the API of the OpenFTV Manager, apart from the Rego decision policy. The PDP shows no identity, so pdp-bundle.cedar allows only GET on the one bundle path.
    • The Manager seeds its Cedar policies only into an empty store. An existing volume does not pick up a changed Cedar file.
    • The realm has the roles admin, author and auditor. Publication uses a non-personal deployment identity with a token of 30 minutes. In demo v0.9.0, no Cedar policy grants author an action, so only admin writes and publishes.
    • The bundle has no signature. Inside one organization, signing is not planned (#426). If a bronhouder lets another organization build or host its bundles, signing and verification become a requirement (F-09).

    Two components have the name Manager. The OpenFTV Manager manages policy. The FSC Manager manages contracts and issues access tokens.

    Guidelines for bronhouders¶

    GBO gives five guidelines for policy management. Each guideline has a status in demo v0.9.0:

    Guideline Demo status
    RL-01 Deliver policy as a versioned bundle. Do not bake it into the PDP Opt-in only. The default mounts the policies. No signature
    RL-02 Authorize the management API with its own policy set. Deny on an empty store Built for the OpenFTV Manager (Cedar). The PDP itself does not follow it (F-51)
    RL-03 Separate writing from publishing. Publish with a non-personal, short-lived identity Deployment identity built. The author role grants no action
    RL-04 Withdraw policy, and do not delete it. Reconcile with version control Built: retire_stale at every seed
    RL-05 Validate a bundle before activation. Fall back visibly to the last valid set Local check built (make policy-check). Visible fallback not built

    Source metadata has the lifecycle that RL-05 asks for: validation before activation, atomic promotion, and rollback (F-59, Source configuration). For policy, this lifecycle is a backlog item.

    Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp¶

    The demo follows the Globaal Ontwerp in the PEP, PDP and PIP chain with AuthZEN and Rego. It differs in the management of the policy:

    Topic Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0
    Place of the PAP A PAP manages the policies and distributes them to the PDPs of the bronhouders A PAP and a PDP at each bronhouder. No central PAP (ADR-0021)
    Bundles Signed policy bundles A bundle with an ID and a version, without a signature. Signing only across an organization boundary
    Policy language ODRL in the PAP Rego for every decision, and Cedar for the API of the OpenFTV Manager (Q-78)

    Open points¶

    The main open points in policy management are these:

    • The PDP guards its own management endpoints with the decision policy (F-51).
    • One broken module stops every decision and the admission of new parties, without a visible fallback (F-52).
    • The decision record does not name the policy version that decided (REQ-59, Records).
    • The actor lists of the PID rules are policy data. They must stay apart from the consent consumers in every environment (F-70).
    • How the reference policy shows that it is not tied to one language or engine (Q-78).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: RL-01, RL-02, RL-03, RL-04, RL-05, REQ-59, REQ-62
    • Findings: F-09 (closed), F-51 (open), F-52 (open), F-59 (closed), F-70 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-21 (answered), Q-78 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-13 (done), SL-44 (done), SL-45 (done)

    Records: decisions, processing, transport¶

    Every data exchange through GBO must be reconstructable afterwards. A reader must see who asked for what, under which basis, with which decision, and who processed which personal data (P-12). GBO keeps three authoritative records, one per Logius standard. One W3C trace ID joins them, and each record stores the FSC transaction ID next to it. This is capability S09 of the Globaal Ontwerp. The Logging, audit and traceability concept page has the detail and the links to the code.

    Overview › GBO Basis › Records

    Three records¶

    flowchart LR subgraph dec["Decision"] direction TB pdp("PDP<br/>OpenFTV") adl[("ADL<br/>ftv_adl")] pdp --> adl end subgraph proc["Processing"] direction TB comp("Gateway, source API,<br/>register, consumer,<br/>EUDI adapter") ldv[("LDV logbook<br/>per controller")] comp --> ldv end subgraph tra["Transport"] direction TB fsc("FSC Inway<br/>and Outway") tx[("FSC txlog<br/>per peer")] fsc --> tx end subgraph obs["Observability, not audit"] direction TB all("All services") jg[("Traces<br/>Jaeger, 7 days")] lk[("Logs<br/>Loki, 7 days")] all --> jg all --> lk end dec ~~~ proc ~~~ tra ~~~ obs %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class pdp,comp,fsc basis class adl,ldv,tx store class all ext class jg,lk mock class adl,ldv,tx zoom style dec fill:#F5F3FF,stroke:#7C3AED style proc fill:#F5F3FF,stroke:#7C3AED style tra fill:#F5F3FF,stroke:#7C3AED style obs fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB,stroke-dasharray:4 3 click adl "../../../concepts/logging/#decision-records-adl" "Decision records" click ldv "../../../concepts/logging/#processing-records-ldv" "Processing records" click tx "../../components/#level-2-fsc-group" "FSC group"

    Figure 1: The three authoritative records and the observability stores. Thick border: click to zoom in.

    Each record answers one question:

    Record Standard Question it answers Writer Store in the demo
    Decision Authorization Decision Log (ADL) Which decision did the PDP take on this request or contract? The PDP Postgres database ftv_adl
    Processing Logboek Dataverwerkingen (LDV) 1.0.0 Which organization processed which personal data, for which activity? Each component, in the logbook of its own controller One logbook per controller
    Transport FSC-Logging (draft) Which FSC transaction took place between which peers? FSC Inway and Outway Transaction log per FSC peer

    A PDP decision is not a processing, so it gets no LDV record. On the DvTP path, the LDV records are at three processings:

    • The consent status lookup at the register.
    • The decryption at the source gateway.
    • The query at the source.

    Traces and logs are for debugging. They are sampled or best effort, and nobody cites them as evidence (REQ-32). The console decision log of the policy engine goes to Loki. It holds the rule per field and the step trace. The developer portal shows it as detail next to the ADL record. The portal sets the color of the PDP from the ADL record alone (ADR-0036).

    One request leaving its trail¶

    For one DvTP query, every component on the path writes its own record. The following figure shows which identifier lands in which record:

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Consumer participant C as Consumer backend participant OW as Consumer Outway end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant IN as FSC Inway (PEP) participant PDP as PDP participant GW as Source gateway end box rgb(254,220,216) DvTP participant CR as Consent register end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant TX as FSC txlogs participant ADL as ADL participant LDV as LDV logbooks end C->>OW: query, traceparent T, Fsc-Transaction-Id X1 OW->>TX: transaction X1 OW->>IN: mTLS, T, X1 IN->>TX: transaction X1 IN->>PDP: AuthZEN on a fresh context (no T, no X1) PDP->>CR: status lookup with T and X1 CR->>LDV: consent logbook: lookup, trace T PDP->>ADL: decision, random trace, request headers stored PDP-->>IN: allow IN->>GW: the judged request, T GW->>LDV: source logbook: decryption, trace T Note over GW: the source API logs<br/>the query under T as well GW-->>C: only the selected fields C->>LDV: consumer logbook: under consent ID, trace T

    Figure 2: The trail of one DvTP query. The runtime page DvTP query has every hop.

    Two identifiers link the records (REQ-55, ADR-0035):

    W3C trace ID Fsc-Transaction-Id
    Made by The application that starts the processing The FSC Outway, or the entry component
    Count per processing One One per FSC transaction
    Recorded in LDV trace_id, ADL trace_id, spans, logs FSC txlog, ADL adl.fsc.transaction_id, span attribute gbo.fsc.transaction_id

    Every component takes the trace ID unchanged from the incoming traceparent and sends it on every outbound call. The transaction ID never replaces an incoming trace. The earlier rule "trace ID equals transaction ID" broke for a caller with its own trace, for one processing over several sources, and at every extra FSC hop (F-67).

    The Inway copies the headers of the request into the AuthZEN context. From there, the policy sends T and X1 on the status lookup. As a result, the record of the register lands in the trace of the request.

    Decision records (ADL)¶

    The PDP writes one ADL record for each evaluation, contract decisions included (REQ-71). The PDP does not start without the database ftv_adl, so the ADL runs in every deployment profile. A reader gets the SELECT-only role adl_reader.

    The record holds the AuthZEN request and the answer {allow, reason}. By design, the Inway returns that reason to the consumer, so per-field detail cannot go into the answer. The record therefore holds only what the consumer can also see. The FSC Inway of demo v0.9.0 drops the reason on the way back (F-72).

    Records per controller (LDV)¶

    Every GBO-delivered component that processes personal data writes one LDV record per processing and per data subject. It writes to the logbook of its own controller (REQ-72, ADR-0026). Only trace metadata crosses an organization boundary, so the demo runs one logbook image as seven logbooks:

    Logbook Controller Writers
    logboek-bd Belastingdienst bron-sidecar, graphql-server
    logboek-brp RvIG brp-sidecar, brp-graphql-server
    logboek-lvg LVG lvg-sidecar, lvg-graphql-server
    logboek-toestemming GBO consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) consent-register, consent-portal-backend
    logboek-eudi-adapter GBO issuance facility eudi-adapter
    logboek-afnemer Hypotheek-BV (demo consumer) dienstverlener-backend, integrator-backend
    logboek-ir Installatie Register (demo consumer) ir-backend

    In production, each controller runs its own logbook, and GBO ships the LDV client. Each record carries the trace context, a versioned processing activity, and the data subject in the own pseudonym space of the controller. If the component calls another party, the record also points to the read API of that party in dpl.read.nextLogbookId.

    Three properties make the records reliable:

    • Durable first, delivered after. A component stores the record in a local outbox, with an fsync, before its response leaves. It delivers the record afterwards with retries. A logbook outage delays records and does not fail requests. If the component cannot store the record locally, it refuses the processing.
    • No BSN. The logbook scans every write for a nine-digit run that passes the BSN check digit test (elfproef), and refuses a match. The check is word-bounded, so a 20-digit OIN passes.
    • Separate tokens. A component that can write cannot read with that token.

    In demo v0.9.0, the ASIP writes no LDV records, although it processes personal data.

    How to read a chain¶

    A read starts at the application that started the processing. From there, a reader follows nextLogbookId. The LDV read extension selects records by trace ID, processing activity, or data subject:

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Reader participant R as Reader end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant LA as Consumer logbook participant LS as Source logbook participant TX as FSC txlogs participant ADL as ADL participant LT as Consent logbook end R->>LA: read trace ID T LA-->>R: record with nextLogbookId = source and X1 R->>LS: read trace ID T LS-->>R: gateway and source records R->>TX: read transaction X1 TX-->>R: transport records R->>ADL: SELECT on X1 in the stored request headers ADL-->>R: decision record Note over R,LT: no record points here (Q-25) R->>LT: read trace ID T LT-->>R: status lookup record

    Figure 3: Reading the chain of one DvTP query.

    Two gaps limit this route (F-68):

    • The chain starts at a party that LDV does not bind. In DvTP, a private consumer starts the processing. Without its records, nobody knows which sources one processing touched. The consumer logs under the consent ID, because it has no citizen identifier (Q-27).
    • No pointer leads from the decision to the consent logbook. The ADL has no field like nextLogbookId. The demo applies option 3 of Q-25: a reader calls the consent logbook by trace ID.

    The register records form a second index over the chain. Every source call leads to a status lookup, and the register logs it with trace ID and consent ID.

    Gaps in demo v0.9.0¶

    The records have these known gaps:

    Gap Effect Link
    ADL behind the Inway is not correlated The Inway sends neither traceparent nor Fsc-Transaction-Id to the PDP. The record gets a random trace and no transaction ID. A reader finds it through the stored request headers. The fix is upstream in open-fsc #369
    No policy version The records carry policies: 0. A reader cannot see which policy decided REQ-59
    Only {allow, reason} The record lacks the consent status answer and the configuration. Nobody can replay a decision from it F-72
    BSN in the decision logs In the EUDI and ASI routes, the ADL and the console log hold the plain BSN. Neither masks it REQ-60, ADR-0043 (proposed)
    A chain reads forward only The read starts at the consumer, and no pointer leads to the consent logbook F-68

    No record type has tamper evidence or a retention period in demo v0.9.0. Who can read which records, and how long they are kept, is open (Q-08).

    Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp¶

    The Globaal Ontwerp names the three standards and leaves their use in GBO open. The demo fills it in as follows:

    Topic Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0
    Standards FSC-Logging, LDV and ADL are available. The GBO use is open One authoritative record per standard (ADR-0036, ADR-0026)
    Chain-wide traceability Agreements still to make The W3C trace ID is the join key, with the transaction ID next to it (ADR-0035)
    Link with the authorization chain Still to make The PDP writes the ADL. The record is not correlated behind the Inway, and it has no pointer to the consent logbook

    Open points¶

    The main open points in the records are these:

    • The decision record holds only what the consumer also sees, so a decision cannot be replayed (F-72).
    • A chain read goes forward only and starts at a party that LDV does not bind (F-68).
    • Masking in the policy engine has no effect, and the BSN is in the decision logs of the EUDI and ASI routes (F-54).
    • How a reader finds the step from the decision to the consent logbook (Q-25).
    • Read access and retention of the records (Q-08).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-32, REQ-55, REQ-59, REQ-60, REQ-71, REQ-72
    • Findings: F-54 (open), F-67 (resolved in demo), F-68 (open), F-72 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-08 (open), Q-25 (open), Q-27 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-38 (done), SL-50 (done), SL-51 (done)

    DvTP channel

    DvTP channel¶

    In the DvTP channel, a private service provider (dienstverlener) gets source data about a citizen, with the consent of that citizen. The channel adds two things to GBO Basis. In the consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening), the citizen gives and revokes consent. The pseudonymization facility (pseudonimiseervoorziening) of BSNk makes sure that the service provider never gets a BSN. This is interaction pattern C of the Globaal Ontwerp.

    Overview › DvTP channel

    Inside the channel¶

    flowchart LR burger(["Citizen"]) subgraph cons["Consumer side"] direction TB dv["Service provider"] int["Integrator<br/><i>optional</i>"] end subgraph tv["Consent facility"] direction LR pf("Portal<br/>frontend") --> pb("Portal<br/>backend") --> tr[("Consent<br/>register")] end subgraph ext["External services"] direction LR digid["DigiD<br/><i>mock</i>"] bsnk["BSNk PP<br/><i>mock</i>"] end subgraph basis["GBO Basis, at each source"] direction LR pdp("PEP + PDP") --> gw("Source<br/>gateway") --> api[("Source<br/>BD · LVG")] end burger -- "uses a service" --> dv dv -- "① redirect" --> pf pf -. "login" .-> digid pb -. "at consent only" .-> bsnk dv <-- "② consent proof" --- tr dv -- "③ query + proof<br/>over FSC" --> pdp int -. "on behalf of" .-> pdp pdp -- "④ status<br/>over FSC" --> tr %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class burger,api source class dv,int,digid,bsnk ext class pf,pb,tr dvtp class pdp,gw basis class pf,pb,tr,pdp,bsnk,int zoom style tv fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#E28F80 style basis fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style cons fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style ext fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB click pf "consent-service/" "Consent facility" click pb "consent-service/" "Consent facility" click tr "consent-service/" "Consent facility" click pdp "../gbo-basis/authorization/" "Authorization" click bsnk "../../concepts/pseudonymization/" "Pseudonymization" click int "../../runtime/dvtp-query/#variant-an-integrator-calls-for-the-consumer" "Integrator variant"

    Figure 1: The DvTP channel. Pink: GBO components of the channel. Green: GBO Basis at the source.

    The channel has these parts:

    Part Role Zoom in
    Consent facility The citizen sees the request, logs in, and gives or refuses consent. Later the citizen views and revokes consents. The register signs a consent proof and answers the status of a consent. Consent facility
    Pseudonymization facility BSNk PP turns the BSN into values that only one party can read. The channel calls it only when a citizen gives consent. Pseudonymization
    Service provider Starts the request, keeps the proof, and sends it with every query. It never gets a BSN or another number for the citizen. DvTP query
    Integrator A software party that calls the source for a service provider, under an FSC delegation and a registered mandate. ADR-0034
    GBO Basis Checks the proof and the consent status for every request, and fills in the citizen only after an allow. GBO Basis

    Two phases¶

    The channel works in two phases, as in the Globaal Ontwerp. In phase 1, the citizen gives consent. In phase 2, the service provider queries a source under that consent, as often as the consent allows:

    sequenceDiagram autonumber actor B as Citizen box rgb(241,239,232) Consumer participant DV as Service provider end box rgb(254,220,216) Consent facility participant P as Portal participant TR as Register end box rgb(241,239,232) External participant BK as BSNk PP end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant PDP as PEP + PDP participant GW as Source gateway end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant S as Source API end rect rgb(255,248,246) Note over B,BK: Phase 1: consent B->>DV: start a service DV->>P: redirect with consumer, service, data sets B->>P: log in (DigiD) and give consent P->>BK: make a value per source BK-->>P: encrypted values (VI, VP) P->>TR: store the consent TR-->>P: signed consent proof P-->>DV: redirect back with the proof end rect rgb(246,252,248) Note over DV,S: Phase 2: query, again for every use DV->>PDP: query with a placeholder + the proof PDP->>TR: status of this consent (over FSC) TR-->>PDP: active Note over PDP: check proof, fields,<br/>years, caller PDP->>GW: allow Note over GW: decrypt own value,<br/>replace the placeholder GW->>S: query with the BSN S-->>DV: only the selected fields end

    Figure 2: The two phases of DvTP. Every step names the essence only. The runtime pages have every hop.

    For every hop, with the data and the error paths, see DvTP consent and DvTP query. Viewing and revoking a consent is a third flow: DvTP citizen access.

    Who sees which identifier¶

    The channel is built so that the BSN appears in as few places as possible. The service provider holds no identifier for the citizen at all:

    flowchart LR subgraph bsn["Sees the BSN"] direction TB pb("Portal backend<br/>at login and consent") bk["BSNk PP"] gw("Source gateway<br/>after the allow") api[("Source API")] end subgraph pseudo["Sees only pseudonymous values"] direction TB tr[("Register<br/>PI, PP under its<br/>own reference")] pdp("PDP<br/>checks the proof,<br/>not the person") end subgraph none["Sees no identifier"] direction TB dv["Service provider<br/>proof + placeholder"] int["Integrator"] end %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class pb,tr dvtp class bk,dv,int ext class gw,pdp basis class api source style bsn fill:#FFF1F0,stroke:#E28F80 style pseudo fill:#FFF7ED,stroke:#EA580C style none fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A

    Figure 3: Where the BSN can appear in the DvTP channel.

    The consent proof carries one encrypted value per source. Only that source can decrypt its value. The value becomes the own pseudonym of the source, or the BSN if the source has the right to process the BSN (ADR-0032, ADR-0033). In its query, the service provider names the citizen with a fixed placeholder.

    This has a cost. The service provider cannot recognize the same citizen across two consents, and it logs under the consent, not under the person (F-76).

    Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp¶

    The demo follows pattern C of the Globaal Ontwerp. It differs in the form of three steps:

    Step Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0
    What the service provider gets A consent ID and an encrypted identity A signed consent proof that holds the consent ID and an encrypted value per source
    What the register stores The encrypted identity, scope, purpose, validity The consent, plus the polymorphic values of the citizen under its own reference. No encrypted values per source
    Who checks the consent The bronhouder asks the register The PDP of the source checks the proof itself, then asks the register for the status over FSC

    The design choice behind these differences is in ADR-0032. Whether the register and the portal backend are one system, and which of them talks to BSNk, is open (Q-49, ADR-0040).

    Open points¶

    The main open points in the DvTP channel are these:

    • Whether a private service provider without a public task can connect to BSNk PP at all (Q-01).
    • Who sets the validity period of a consent (Q-13).
    • Whether the proof must also name the integrator (Q-46).
    • The values in the proof are fixed at consent: a source that joins later needs a new consent (F-78).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-12, REQ-20, REQ-21, REQ-37, REQ-68, REQ-79, REQ-106
    • Findings: F-76 (open), F-78 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-01 (partly answered), Q-13 (open), Q-46 (open), Q-49 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-06a (done), SL-47 (done), SL-51 (done)

    Consent facility¶

    The consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) is where the citizen gives, views and revokes consent. It also tells every source, at every request, whether a consent still holds. It has three components: the consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) frontend and backend (PSA capability S02) and the consent register (toestemmingsregister) (S01). The Consent concept page has the detail and the links to the code.

    Overview › DvTP channel › Consent facility

    Components and interfaces¶

    flowchart LR burger(["Citizen<br/>browser"]) dv["Service provider"] subgraph tv["Consent facility"] direction TB pf("Portal frontend<br/>request, login, choice,<br/>overview, revoke") pb("Portal backend<br/>keeps the BSN away<br/>from the register") subgraph tr["Consent register"] direction TB api("Portal API<br/>create, list, revoke") st("Status listener<br/>status only") jw("JWKS<br/>public keys") db[("Consents,<br/>PI + PP per citizen")] end end digid["DigiD<br/><i>mock</i>"] bsnk["BSNk PP<br/><i>mock</i>"] inw("Register Inway<br/>FSC service consent-status") pdp("PDP of a source") log[("LDV logbook<br/>consent facility")] dv -- "redirect: consumer, service,<br/>data sets, return address" --> pf burger --> pf pf -- "login" --> digid pf --> pb pb -- "activate once,<br/>transform per consent" --> bsnk pb -- "only the backend" --> api api --- db st --- db pf -- "proof in the URL fragment" --> dv pdp -- "over FSC" --> inw --> st pdp -. "keys, cached 5 min" .-> jw api -.-> log st -.-> log %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class burger source class dv,digid,bsnk ext class pf,pb,api,st,jw dvtp class db,log store class inw,pdp basis class pdp,bsnk zoom style tv fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#E28F80 style tr fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#E28F80 click pdp "../../gbo-basis/authorization/" "Authorization" click bsnk "../../../concepts/pseudonymization/" "Pseudonymization"

    Figure 1: The components of the consent facility and their interfaces.

    Each component has one job:

    Component Job Never does
    Portal frontend Shows the request in plain language, one choice per data set. Shows the consents of the citizen and lets the citizen revoke one. Picks fields inside a data set (REQ-10)
    Portal backend Recognizes the citizen with a keyed hash of the BSN. Asks BSNk for the values per source. Talks to the register. Sends a BSN to the register (REQ-23)
    Register: portal API Creates, lists and revokes consents. Signs the consent proof. Only the portal backend can call it. Serves the status to a source
    Register: status listener Answers one question per request: is this consent active? It is reachable only over FSC. Serves anything else
    Register: JWKS Publishes the public keys that the PDP uses to check a proof. —

    The consent proof¶

    The register signs a consent proof when the citizen gives consent. The service provider (dienstverlener) keeps it and sends it unchanged with every query:

    flowchart LR subgraph jwt["Consent proof: ES256 JWT, type gbo-consent+jwt"] direction TB h["Header<br/>algorithm, type, key ID"] subgraph claims["Claims"] direction TB id["consent_id · jti"] sc["scopes · scope_entries<br/>data sets per source"] who["dienstverlener_oin<br/>the party it is for"] t["valid_until = exp<br/>iss · aud · iat · nbf"] subgraph es["encrypted_subject: one entry per source OIN"] direction LR vp["pseudonym (VP)<br/>for every source"] vi["identity (VI)<br/>only for a source that<br/>may process the BSN"] end end end sig["Signature of<br/>the register"] jwt --- sig %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class h,id,sc,who,t dvtp class vp,vi store class sig ext style jwt fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#E28F80 style claims fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style es fill:#F5F3FF,stroke:#7C3AED

    Figure 2: The parts of the consent proof.

    The proof holds no BSN. The service provider can read which data sets it can ask for. It cannot read who the citizen is: each value in encrypted_subject can be decrypted only by the source it was made for (REQ-80). The decision for this form is ADR-0032.

    The proof works as a bearer token. The binding to the service provider stops use by another party, but not replay by the same party within the validity (R4).

    Life of a consent¶

    stateDiagram-v2 direction LR [*] --> Active: citizen gives consent,<br/>register signs the proof Active --> Active: service provider queries<br/>(as often as needed) Active --> Revoked: citizen revokes Active --> Expired: valid_until passes Revoked --> [*] Expired --> [*] classDef active fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef stop fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B class Active active class Revoked,Expired stop

    Figure 3: The states of a consent.

    The register stores ACTIVE or REVOKED. Expired follows from the date in the proof. A consent can be used again within its validity: the design does not require single use (Q-04). A revocation takes effect on the next request, because the PDP asks the status every time (REQ-14).

    Why the status stays online¶

    The proof carries the content of the consent, and the register keeps the status. Each part has its own freshness:

    What How fresh Why
    Content: data sets, party, validity Fixed at consent, checked locally The register signed it. The PDP needs no call for it.
    Public keys At most five minutes old Keys change rarely. An unknown key ID triggers a fetch at once.
    Status Live at every request A revocation must stop the next request.

    The price is a hard dependency: if the register does not answer, the PDP denies every DvTP request (REQ-75). The target values for availability and delay are open (Q-47).

    Open points¶

    The main open points in the consent facility are these:

    • Whether the register and the portal backend are one system, and which one is the BSNk participant (Q-49).
    • Who sets the validity period, and whether the citizen can change it (Q-13).
    • When a consent counts as "retrieved", and how the register learns that (Q-42).
    • Where the signing key lives and how it rotates (Q-55).
    • Whether the register must authenticate the portal backend, or whether network isolation is enough (Q-58).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-10, REQ-14, REQ-23, REQ-68, REQ-75, REQ-76, REQ-80
    • Findings: F-61 (closed), F-78 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-04 (answered), Q-13 (open), Q-42 (open), Q-47 (open), Q-49 (open), Q-55 (open), Q-58 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-11 (done), SL-47 (done), SL-51 (done)

    EUDI wallet channel

    EUDI wallet channel¶

    In the EUDI wallet channel, a citizen gets data from a government source in the EUDI wallet. Interaction pattern (interactiepatroon) A of the Globaal Ontwerp has two flows. In flow A, the source issues an attestation itself, as a PuB-EAA. In flow B, a QTSP verifies or retrieves the data at the source and issues a QEAA. GBO delivers one component for each flow, and both components reach the source through GBO Basis.

    Overview › EUDI wallet channel

    Inside the channel¶

    flowchart LR burger(["Citizen"]) subgraph extp["External parties"] direction TB wallet["NL Wallet<br/>PID, attestations"] qtsp["QTSP<br/><i>reference QTSP in the demo</i>"] end subgraph pub["PuB-EAA provider: flow A"] direction TB is("Issuance server<br/>nl-wallet") ad("EUDI adapter") end subgraph asi["ASI provider: flow B"] direction TB az("Authorization server<br/>login, tokens") asip("ASIP<br/>verify, retrieve") end reg[("Source registry<br/>active release")] subgraph basis["GBO Basis, at each source"] direction LR pdp("PEP + PDP<br/>PID regime") --> gw("Source<br/>gateway") --> api[("Source<br/>BD · BRP")] end burger --- wallet burger -- "B · asks for a statement" --> qtsp wallet -- "A · PID, then<br/>attestation" --> is is -- "callback<br/>with the PID" --> ad wallet -. "B · login with the PID" .-> az qtsp -- "token" --> az qtsp -- "verify, retrieve" --> asip ad -- "query + BSN<br/>over FSC" --> pdp asip -- "query + BSN<br/>over FSC" --> pdp reg -. "eudi" .-> ad reg -. "asi" .-> asip %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class burger,api source class wallet,qtsp ext class is,ad,az,asip eudi class pdp,gw basis class reg store class is,ad,az,asip,pdp,gw,reg zoom style pub fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#EA580C style asi fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#EA580C style basis fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style extp fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB click is "pubeaa/" "PuB-EAA provider" click ad "pubeaa/" "PuB-EAA provider" click az "asi/" "ASI provider" click asip "asi/" "ASI provider" click pdp "../gbo-basis/" "GBO Basis" click gw "../gbo-basis/#the-request-path" "Request path" click reg "../../concepts/source-onboarding/" "Source onboarding"

    Figure 1: The EUDI wallet channel. Orange: the GBO components of the channel, with GBO Basis in green. Thick border: click to zoom in.

    The channel has these parts:

    Part Role Zoom in
    PuB-EAA provider (PubEAA-voorziening) The technical issuance facility. The issuance server asks the wallet for the PID. The EUDI adapter gets the source data and turns it into claims. The bronhouder stays the PuB-EAA provider (ADR-0028, proposed). PuB-EAA provider
    ASI provider Lets a QTSP verify or retrieve attributes at the source (eIDAS article 45e). It has its own OAuth authorization server. The QTSP is an OAuth client there, and not an FSC participant (F-87). ASI provider
    Source registry Holds the active release of every source description. The source describes its attestations (eudi) and its attributes (asi) itself. Source onboarding
    GBO Basis Decides every request of the channel under the PID regime, with the rules EUD0001, EUD0002 and ASI0001. GBO Basis
    NL Wallet and QTSP External parties. The wallet holds the PID of the citizen. The demo runs a reference QTSP, which is not a real QTSP. ASI verification

    Flow A: the source issues a PuB-EAA¶

    In flow A, the citizen shares the PID with the issuance facility and gets an attestation back. The attestation carries the name of the source as the issuer:

    sequenceDiagram autonumber actor B as Citizen box rgb(241,239,232) External participant W as NL Wallet end box rgb(255,237,213) PuB-EAA provider participant IS as Issuance server participant AD as EUDI adapter end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant PDP as PEP + PDP end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant S as Source API end B->>W: scan the QR code of an offer W->>IS: fetch the request IS-->>W: ask for the PID claim bsn, in the name of the source B->>W: share the PID W->>IS: PID as SD-JWT VC Note over IS: check the PID<br/>against the trust anchors IS->>AD: callback with the disclosed PID Note over AD: BSN from the PID,<br/>query from the release AD->>PDP: query with the BSN, over FSC Note over PDP: no consent token,<br/>so PID regime, EUD0001 PDP->>S: allow, query through the gateway S-->>AD: source data Note over AD: claims with gbo-simple-v1 AD-->>IS: claims and type IS-->>W: attestation, signed for the source W-->>B: accept the attestation

    Figure 2: Flow A, at essence level. The runtime page has every hop.

    The facility signs with the certificate set of the source. The wallet shows the source as the issuer. GBO plays no part when the citizen later presents the attestation to a service provider (dienstverlener). For every hop, with the data and the error paths, see EUDI issuance.

    Flow B: a QTSP verifies at the source¶

    In flow B, the QTSP asks the ASI provider to verify or retrieve attributes at the source. The citizen approves the request by logging in at the authorization server:

    sequenceDiagram autonumber actor B as Citizen box rgb(241,239,232) External participant Q as QTSP participant W as NL Wallet end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant AS as Authorization server participant ASIP as ASIP end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant PDP as PEP + PDP end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant S as BRP end B->>Q: ask for a statement Q-->>B: redirect to the authorization server B->>AS: see who asks what at which source W->>AS: log in with the PID (or the DigiD mock) AS-->>Q: code, then a token with the BSN Q->>ASIP: verify or retrieve, with the token Note over ASIP: check the token,<br/>BSN from the token ASIP->>PDP: query with the BSN, over FSC Note over PDP: PID regime, ASI0001 PDP->>S: allow, query through the gateway S-->>ASIP: fields of the person ASIP-->>Q: sealed result per attribute Q->>W: test statement, not a QEAA

    Figure 3: Flow B, at essence level. Discovery and registration of the QTSP happen once, before the first request.

    A token is valid for one data service, and each data service serves one source. The QTSP issues the QEAA itself. In the demo, the reference QTSP issues a test statement through the issuance server of flow A. For every hop, see ASI verification.

    Who sees which identifier¶

    The channel does not use BSNk. The BSN goes into the source query as a plain value:

    flowchart LR subgraph need["Needs the BSN"] direction TB wallet["NL Wallet<br/>PID of the citizen"] is("Issuance server<br/>checks the PID") ad("EUDI adapter<br/>BSN from the PID") az("Authorization server<br/>BSN from the login") asip("ASIP<br/>BSN from the token") api[("Source<br/>after the allow")] end subgraph extra["Holds the BSN without a need"] direction TB qtsp["QTSP<br/>reads the token"] pdp("PDP input") adl[("ADL and console<br/>decision log")] end subgraph none["Holds no BSN"] direction TB ldv[("LDV records<br/>logbook pseudonym")] logs[("ASIP logs<br/>and traces")] stmt["QTSP login and<br/>test statement"] end %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class wallet,qtsp,stmt ext class is,ad,az,asip eudi class api source class pdp basis class adl,ldv,logs store style need fill:#FFF7ED,stroke:#EA580C style extra fill:#FFF1F0,stroke:#E28F80 style none fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A

    Figure 4: Where the BSN can appear in the EUDI wallet channel. Red: the BSN is there without a need.

    In flow A, the EUDI adapter takes the BSN from the disclosed PID. In flow B, the ASIP takes it from the access token. Both components put the BSN in the query variables. As a result, the BSN is in two kinds of places that do not need it:

    • The PDP input, and with it the ADL and the console decision log. This is a known violation of REQ-60. The proposed fix keeps identifiers out of the PDP input (ADR-0043, proposed).
    • The access token of flow B. ETSI requires the identification data in the token, and the QTSP can read the BSN (F-86).

    The LDV records hold no BSN, because the logbook refuses one. For the detail, see Exception: the BSN in the EUDI and ASI routes.

    The PID regime¶

    Neither flow carries a consent proof. The evidence in the request selects the regime, so both flows land in the PID regime (ADR-0031):

    flowchart LR q{"Consent token<br/>in the request?"} c["Consent regime<br/>DvTP"] p["PID regime<br/>EUD0001 · EUD0002 · ASI0001"] a{"Caller on the<br/>actor list?"} s{"BSN in the<br/>root argument?"} f{"Fields and limits<br/>of the rule?"} ok(["Allow"]) no(["Deny"]) ev("Verified PID as<br/>positive evidence<br/><i>design only</i>") q -- "one" --> c q -- "none" --> p p --> a a -- "yes" --> s s -- "yes" --> f f -- "yes" --> ok a -. "ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED" .-> no s -. "PID_NOT_PRESENT" .-> no f -. "FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED" .-> no ev -. "REQ-45" .-> p %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class q,a,s,f,ok basis class c,no dvtp class p eudi class ev planned class p zoom click p "../gbo-basis/authorization/#regime-from-evidence" "Regime from evidence"

    Figure 5: The PID regime. Dashed: the positive evidence that the design asks for. Demo v0.9.0 does not build it.

    Each PID rule admits only named callers: the FSC peer of the EUDI adapter, or the ASIP peer. Only consent is positive evidence. A request enters the PID regime because it carries no token (F-70). For that reason, the actor lists of the PID rules must stay disjoint from the consent consumers. The fix in the design is a verified PID disclosure, bound to the subject of the query (REQ-45).

    In demo v0.9.0, the callback that carries the PID is not authenticated. The callback gap shows what that allows.

    Approval in the wallet is no legal basis¶

    In flow A, the citizen chooses in the wallet to share the PID. In flow B, the citizen approves one request by logging in (REQ-90). The ARF says that approval in the wallet is never a legal basis for the relying party (F-83). The approval of flow B is also not stored, and the citizen cannot revoke it. A DvTP consent and a wallet approval cannot replace each other. For the detail, see Wallet approval is not a legal basis.

    Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp¶

    The demo follows the two flows of pattern A. It differs in six steps:

    Step Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0
    Start of flow A The wallet sends a credential request to the PuB-EAA provider. The citizen scans a QR code. The issuance server first asks for the PID (disclosure-based issuance, ADR-0018).
    Authorization in flow A An authorization facility (autorisatievoorziening) asks the wallet for the PID and authorizes the PuB-EAA provider. No separate service. The nl-wallet issuance server checks the PID and calls the adapter. The adapter does not authenticate that call.
    Authorization in flow B The verify and retrieve service uses the same authorization facility of GBO. The ASI provider has its own OAuth authorization server, with a wallet verifier and a DigiD mock (ADR-0037).
    Approval by the citizen The wallet shows the request and asks for consent. Flow A: the citizen shares the PID. Flow B: the citizen logs in. Neither is a stored consent.
    Format of the attestation SD-JWT VC or mdoc SD-JWT VC (dc+sd-jwt) only
    Result of flow B The QTSP issues a QEAA. The reference QTSP issues a test statement, marked as not qualified.

    The GO also says that a request over ISO 15000 needs no authorization. The demo offers clause 6.1 of ETSI TS 119 478 only (REQ-112). In both the GO and the demo, GBO itself is not a PuB-EAA provider.

    Open points¶

    The main open points in the EUDI wallet channel are these:

    • Nothing binds the BSN in the source query of flow A to a checked PID disclosure (REQ-45, Q-18).
    • The BSN is in the PDP input and in both decision logs (F-54).
    • The QTSP can read the BSN in the access token (F-86).
    • Nothing links the citizen who logs in at the QTSP to the citizen who logs in at the authorization server (F-93).
    • The regulatory frame for PuB-EAA issuance and the designation of the issuer (F-81, Q-28).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-45, REQ-60, REQ-74, REQ-90, REQ-112
    • Findings: F-54 (open), F-70 (open), F-81 (open), F-83 (open), F-86 (open), F-87 (open), F-93 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-18 (open), Q-28 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-19 (done), SL-26 (done), SL-28 (done)

    PuB-EAA provider¶

    The PuB-EAA provider (PubEAA-voorziening) issues an attestation with source data to the EUDI wallet of the citizen. It is flow A of interaction pattern A in the Globaal Ontwerp. GBO operates the technical issuance facility, and each bronhouder stays the PuB-EAA provider of its own attestations (ADR-0028, proposed). The facility runs on the nl-wallet issuance server (ADR-0018). The EUDI issuance runtime page has every hop and the links to the code.

    Overview › EUDI wallet channel › PuB-EAA provider
