    The demo implements three routes end to end: the DvTP query under consent, EUDI issuance, and ASI verification for QTSPs. The SDG-OOTS adapter has no implementation and is not in this view (ADR-0020). The QTSP and the Discover Interface are external roles. The context view shows them.

    The status lookup is one edge in the diagram. It runs from the PDP's own Outway to the register's Inway, as the FSC service consent-status. The dotted LDV edges stand for every component that writes processing records (Level 2: logging and audit).

    Level 2: authorization chain¶

    The authorization chain has the following components:

    Component Responsibility Implementation
    OpenFTV PDP Decides every data request and every FSC contract submission. The build uses OpenFTV tag v0.1.0 and patches in the GBO FTV GraphQL mapper. If a patch step changes nothing, the build fails. The PDP offers AuthZEN 1.0 at POST /authzen/v1/evaluation over HTTPS. It writes one ADL record per evaluation. It does not start without the ADL database. services/openftv-pdp, Dockerfile
    FTV GraphQL mapper Implements the mapping function of the FTV GraphQL profile (ftv-graphql/0.1). It parses the raw body and resolves parent types from the bundled schema of the FSC service in the access token. It returns the field list with arguments as the source executes them, or COVERAGE_UNVERIFIABLE with a subcode. It accepts only queries. For any other operation it returns OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED. It applies fixed limits: body 1 MiB, depth 64, and 1000 field records. It verifies no token, reads no flow, and calls no external service. services/ftv-graphql-mapper, limits, OpenFTV adapter
    Bundled schemas and pins One directive-free schema per FSC service (bri, brp, lvg). The policy bundle pins the digest of each schema. The policy denies an evaluation against another schema (SCHEMA_MISMATCH). A CI job compares the bundled schemas with the source schemas. schemas/pdp-mirror, graphql_schemas.rego, check-schema-drift.sh
    Policy entrypoint Allows the source-metadata fetch for two known peers, on the two metadata services only. It sends every other request to the rule engine. It passes only allow and the consumer's reason code to OpenFTV. policies/authz.rego
    Rule engine Selects the regime from the evidence. If the request carries a consent token, the regime is consent. Without a token, the regime is PID. The engine binds a field to the rules of that regime that serve the FSC service and name the field key. It denies a field that no rule covers (NO_APPLICABLE_RULE). The first bound rule without a reason grants the field. The engine checks the integrator mandate on every delegated call. It returns a coarse reason code to the consumer and keeps the per-field codes for the operator. policies/gbo/engine.rego
    Request reader Reads the field list, the arguments, the caller, the represented party, and the time from the input. It does no checks. policies/gbo/lib.rego
    Consent PIP Verifies the consent token in policy: ES256 signature, issuer, audience, type, validity with 30 s skew, and required claims. It fetches the JWKS directly from the register and caches it for 300 s. It fetches the status for each evaluation over FSC, through the PDP's Outway. The status fetch has no cache and a 2 s timeout. Every failure has its own reason code. The engine copies the resolved consent into its response. policies/gbo/consent.rego
    Authorization rules Five plain-Rego rules, listed in the next table. Each rule names its regime, its FSC services, and its fields. It also states its own reasons to deny. policies/gbo/rules
    Contract acceptance policy Decides whether a provider's FSC Manager signs a submitted contract. It accepts grant types service connection and delegated service connection. It applies eight ordered refusal codes, from NOT_AN_AUTOSIGN_REQUEST to DELEGATION_NOT_REGISTERED. It keeps a missing register (ADMISSION_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE) apart from a missing entry (PARTY_NOT_IN_REGISTRY). policies/fsc/autosign.rego
    Admission register (toelatingsregister) Holds the admitted participants: bronhouders, GBO system participants (EDI issuer, PDP, ASIP), and consumers. Each entry has active and allowed_source_peer_ids. The register also holds integrator mandates (integrations) and serves them as acts_for. OpenFTV pulls it every 5 s over a network that only the PDP shares. The register deactivates an entry and never deletes it. It keeps no change log (REQ-123). It is a SQLite database with an admin UI. services/dvtp-onboarding-register, PIP pull

    The PID regime has no positive evidence of its own. A request without a consent token enters it (F-70). For this reason, the PID rules admit only named actors. These actor lists must stay apart from the consent consumers. The five rules grant these fields:

    Rule Regime Services What it grants Own deny reasons File
    DVT0001 consent bri Income declaration fields under consent consent codes, SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED, CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH, YEAR_NOT_COVERED dvt0001.rego
    LVG0001 consent lvg Ownership check at LVG, scope lvg:vbo:eigendom consent codes, SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED, CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH lvg0001.rego
    EUD0001 pid bri Income statement (inkomensverklaring) to the wallet, years 2024 and 2025 PID_NOT_PRESENT, ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED, YEAR_NOT_ALLOWED eud0001.rego
    EUD0002 pid brp Death certificate ("akte van overlijden") to the wallet PID_NOT_PRESENT, ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED eud0002.rego
    ASI0001 pid brp Fields of the Personal Records Database (BRP) behind the ASI attributes, for the ASIP peer …1200 only PID_NOT_PRESENT, ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED asi0001.rego

    The EUDI rules share one actor list, designated_issuers (eudi_helper.rego). The consent rules share the consent checks in dvtp_helper.rego.

    Rule shape¶

    A rule is plain Rego. It declares what it covers and states its reasons to deny. If a rule has no deny reason for a field, it grants that field. box2Inkomen and box3Inkomen are not in covers_fields, so the engine denies them under consent. This excerpt from DVT0001 shows the shape of a rule:

    rule_id := "DVT0001"
regime := "consent"
services := {"bri"}

covers_types := {"Bedrag"}
covers_fields := {
    "Query.ingeschrevenPersoon",
    "IngeschrevenPersoon.heeftBelastingjaarAangifte",
    "AangifteIH.verzamelinkomen",
    "AangifteIH.box1Inkomen",
    # ... scalar fields of the declaration
}

deny contains helper.consent_invalid_reason if not helper.consent_verified
deny contains "CONSENT_WITHDRAWN" if not helper.consent_active
deny contains "CONSENT_ACTOR_MISMATCH" if not helper.consent_given_to_caller
deny contains "SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED" if not income_scope_granted

# The subject must be the identity placeholder, not a literal BSN.
deny_field[i] contains "CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH" if {
    some i, f in lib.fields
    lib.key(f) == "Query.ingeschrevenPersoon"
    not helper.names_consent_citizen(f, "bsn", {lib.identity_placeholder})
}

    Authorization explains regime selection, rule binding, and the two layers of reason codes. The decisions are in ADR-0002, ADR-0009, ADR-0013, ADR-0015, and ADR-0031.

    Level 2: consent chain¶

    The consent chain has the following components:

    Component Responsibility Implementation
    Consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) frontend The citizen UI. It has a DigiD login (mock), one toggle per data set, a consent overview, and revocation. It shows only the requested data sets and refuses a data set that it cannot describe. It checks the return origin against an allowlist. It returns the consent proof in the URL fragment, or status=denied. toestemmingsportaal-frontend
    Consent portal backend Keeps the BSN away from the register and the consumer. The type system enforces this boundary, and the backend never sends a BSN to the register. It derives subject_ref as a keyed HMAC of the BSN, with a key version. It activates a citizen at BSNk once and stores PI and PP in the register. At each consent, it reads the BSN authorization list and has BSNk transform the values. Every configured source gets a VP. Only a source on the list also gets a VI. services/consent-portal-backend, portal.go, subjectref.go
    Consent register (toestemmingsregister) Stores consent records: subject_ref, consumer, scopes, scope entries per source, purpose (use_case), validity, and status. It also stores the portal's PI and PP per subject_ref (route D, ADR-0040). It stores no BSN, no VI, and no VP. It signs the consent proof and serves the JWKS. A separate listener serves only the status, published as the FSC service consent-status. By default, the register keeps its data in memory. If it uses Postgres, it requires a persistent signing key. services/consent-register, status.go, polymorphic.go
    Consent proof ES256 JWT, type gbo-consent+jwt. Claims: consent_id, encrypted_subject, scopes, scope_entries, dienstverlener_oin, valid_until (equal to exp), iss, aud, iat, nbf, jti. encrypted_subject holds a pseudonym per source OIN. For a source on the BSN authorization list, it also holds an identity. Each value has a key_set_version. dienstverlener_oin holds the consumer's FSC Peer ID (Q-68). The PDP denies a token in the old form with pi. consent_token.go

    The consumer holds no citizen identifier. Its query names the subject with the placeholder consent:identity or consent:pseudonym. The source gateway replaces the placeholder after the allow decision (see the next section). Consent explains the record and its lifecycle. Pseudonymization explains the values. The decision is ADR-0032.

    Level 2: bronhouder¶

    The bronhouder runs the following components:

    Component Responsibility Implementation
    GraphQL source API The query endpoint of the source. Sources identify a citizen by BSN. The demo has three sources. Service bri is a Belastingdienst profile with income declarations per year. Service brp is a BRP profile with the personal record (persoonslijst) and the death certificate view. Service lvg is an LVG mock for the LVG pilot (vbo(bsn, vboId) { vboId }). graphql-server, brp-graphql-server, lvg-graphql-server
    Source gateway (bron-sidecar) Source-owned gateway between the Inway and the API, one instance per source. Its behavior depends on the presence of a consent token. With a token, it takes the value for its own OIN from encrypted_subject and has the decryption component read it. It checks that the value names its own OIN. Then it replaces the placeholder. It refuses a literal subject under a token. Without a token, it passes the request through. It accepts only the transport shape the PDP judged: POST, one path, no query string. services/bron-sidecar, substitution, transport.go
    Decryption component Reads a VI or VP with the source's own keys. It calls no other service, so there is no BSNk call at query time. The demo uses the bsnk-mock image with only the decryption endpoints. The three demo sources share one instance and one OIN. Production needs one instance per source. decryption.go, bsnk-mock README
    Source metadata endpoint Serves the source-owned description at /.well-known/gbo over a separate FSC metadata service. source_metadata.go, BD document

    Only the source Inways can reach the source gateway. Because of this network isolation, every request at the gateway comes after a PDP decision. For this reason, the gateway does not verify the token again (ADR-0033, F-79). The deployment view shows the networks.

    Source metadata document¶

    A source describes its own products in one JSON document. It serves the document at /.well-known/gbo. For a source without an endpoint, an operator supplies it through the file transport. GBO validates the document against gbo-source-metadata-v1 (urn:gov:nl:gbo:schema:gbo-source-metadata:1).

    GBO holds no catalog of sources, years, or schemas. This document is the catalog, and the source owns it (ADR-0016). The document format is a proposal for the open PSA decision on S10.

    The document has the following fields:

    Field Content
    schema_version 1.0 or 1.1. Version 1.1 adds capabilities.asi.
    source_oin, version, issued_at, expires_at Envelope. source_oin must match the OIN in the certificate set. version must increase. GBO refuses a validity of less than one hour.
    capabilities.eudi version and attestations[], one entry per attestation type.
    type_id, type_version Identity of the attestation type. With the source ID they form the VCT path /types/{source-id}/{type-id}/v{n}.
    offers[] Products a wallet can request: id, label, description and fixed parameters (for example {"jaar": 2025}).
    graphql The source-owned query plan: service_reference (the FSC data service), endpoint, document (exactly one read operation), subject_variable, typed parameters, and result_pointer (RFC 6901).
    mapping_profile gbo-simple-v1 (ADR-0017). It applies to the eudi capability only.
    display Per language: name, description, a summary with {{claim}} placeholders, and rendering.
    claims Per claim: source (one gbo-simple-v1 rule: pointer, datatype, optional optional), label, optional description, and sd (always by default, allowed or never). The claim order is the display order in the wallet.
    capabilities.asi version, authentic_source (legal_name, country), a graphql block with one ...Selected fragment, and attributes[]. Each attribute has an identifier, an optional type condition on, and fields built with pointer, join, const or each (ADR-0039).

    GBO generates the SD-JWT VC Type Metadata from display and claims. It publishes the Type Metadata immutably per version, with vct#integrity. A change to claims or display therefore needs a new type_version. The schema has no unit. The reconciler refuses reserved claim names (vct, iss, status, cnf) and nested objects (REQ-78).

    The adapter puts the BSN from the PID into $bsn and the year of the offer into $jaar. It reads the result at result_pointer and copies each source.pointer into its claim. This shortened excerpt from the Belastingdienst document (version 2.4.0) shows how the query plan and the claims relate:

    {
  "type_id": "inkomensverklaring",
  "type_version": "2.4",
  "offers": [
    {"id": "inkomensverklaring_2025", "label": "Inkomensverklaring 2025",
     "description": "Inkomensverklaring over belastingjaar 2025",
     "parameters": {"jaar": 2025}}
  ],
  "graphql": {
    "service_reference": "bri",
    "endpoint": "/graphql",
    "document": "query Inkomensverklaring($bsn: BSN!, $jaar: Int!) { ... }",
    "subject_variable": "bsn",
    "parameters": {"jaar": {"type": "integer", "required": true}},
    "result_pointer": "/data/ingeschrevenPersoon/heeftBelastingjaarAangifte"
  },
  "mapping_profile": "gbo-simple-v1",
  "display": {
    "nl-NL": {"name": "Inkomensverklaring",
              "summary": "€{{verzamelinkomen}} ({{belastingjaar}})"}
  },
  "claims": {
    "belastingjaar": {"source": {"pointer": "/belastingjaar", "datatype": "gYear"},
                      "label": {"nl-NL": "Belastingjaar"}},
    "verzamelinkomen": {"source": {"pointer": "/verzamelinkomen/waarde", "datatype": "integer"},
                        "label": {"nl-NL": "Verzamelinkomen"}}
  }
}

    The BRP document (version 2.6.0, schema 1.1) also publishes the asi capability. This excerpt shows two of its attributes:

    {
  "version": "1.0",
  "authentic_source": {"legal_name": "Basisregistratie Personen (mock)", "country": "NL"},
  "graphql": {
    "service_reference": "brp",
    "endpoint": "/graphql",
    "document": "query Asi($bsn: BSN!) { ingeschrevenPersoon(bsn: $bsn) { ...Selected } }",
    "subject_variable": "bsn",
    "result_pointer": "/data/ingeschrevenPersoon"
  },
  "attributes": [
    {"identifier": "https://gbo.example/attributes/family_name/1",
     "fields": {"family_name": {"join": ["/voorvoegsel", "/geslachtsnaam"], "separator": " "}}},
    {"identifier": "https://gbo.example/attributes/nationality/1",
     "fields": {"nationalities": {"each": "/heeftNationaliteit", "pointer": "/nationaliteit"}}}
  ]
}

    By design, the document leaves out three things:

    • The GraphQL schema. The PDP keeps its own bundled copy. It authorizes the source's query plan field by field, like any other query.
    • Access decisions. The EUD and ASI rules decide which fields a channel can receive. The mapping of the source has no part in that decision.
    • The value_schema of an ASI attribute. GBO keeps it per attribute identifier in schemas/asi-attributes.json until an EU catalog of attributes exists.

    Provenance rests on the authenticated FSC transport and the OIN in the certificate set. The source does not sign the document. The document also has no reference to an LDV read API or a DCAT-AP-NL entry (F-57, AV-07).

    Source configuration on the GBO side¶

    The GBO configuration per source is small: one YAML file, named after the source_id. The file names where the description comes from and how GBO reaches the data. This is sources/configured/belastingdienst.yaml:

    metadata_endpoint:
  transport: fsc
  provider_peer_id: "99999999900000000200"
  service_reference: gbo-metadata-bd

    An optional data_access block (transport, provider_peer_id) gives the data leg a different transport than the metadata leg. The file transport is an exception for a source without its own endpoint. In that case, the operator takes over the description. GBO does not record the agreement of the bronhouder (F-71, AV-08).

    The legal identity of the source comes from the certificate set with the same source_id. The OIN comes from the certificate's serialNumber, and the name comes from its O. GBO refuses a configured value that differs (REQ-67). The configuration holds the FSC Peer ID apart from the OIN. The data service and the grant hash come from the source document and the FSC contracts in force. They never come from this file.

    A valid FSC contract activates nothing. A source becomes active only after three steps: it is configured, its candidate is valid, and an operator promotes a release (REQ-65). If a precondition is missing, the reconciler reports METADATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND, DATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND, or FSC_MANAGER_UNAVAILABLE. Source onboarding and admission and activation explain the lifecycle.

    In demo v0.9.0, the RvIG source (rvig.yaml) uses the Belastingdienst peer …0200 and the OIN of the Belastingdienst. This is a demo shortcut. The demo therefore does not show one OIN per bronhouder.

    Source schema and the PDP copy¶

    The source owns its schema. The PDP holds a directive-free copy per FSC service to resolve parent types. The year selector is in the query, so the PDP can enforce consent per year. This excerpt from the BD copy shows the DvTP part:

    type IngeschrevenPersoon {
  bsn: BSN!
  heeftBelastingjaarAangifte(belastingjaren: [Int!]): [BelastingjaarAangifte!]
}

type Query {
  ingeschrevenPersoon(bsn: BSN!): IngeschrevenPersoon
}

    The BRP source adds a flat view for the death certificate. The selection of the deceased partner from the marriage history is a security-sensitive invariant. The source holds this selection and its tests. The policy does not contain it (REQ-57, F-47). For the view, see the BRP copy and EUD0002:

    type Query {
  ingeschrevenPersoon(bsn: BSN!): IngeschrevenPersoon
  akteVanOverlijden(bsn: BSN!): [AkteVanOverlijden!]!
}

    Level 2: FSC group¶

    The FSC group fsc-demo runs OpenFSC v2.4.0. The deployment view lists the peers. The group has the following components:

    Component Responsibility Implementation
    Directory The registry of the group. It signs service publications automatically. It signs nothing else. fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml
    Manager (per organization) Issues access tokens for contracted connections. The token carries the signed service_name, which binds the PDP rules to a service. The provider Managers of BD, BRP, and the consent register decide contract acceptance through the PDP (AuthZEN autosign). bd-manager
    Inway (per provider) bd-inway and brp-inway are the PEP. Their AuthZEN plugin sends every request with its body to the PDP before the request reaches the source gateway. cr-inway has no AuthZEN hook. Behind cr-inway, the contract authorizes consent-status, and the register reads the calling peer from the Fsc-Authorization token. bd-inway, cr-inway
    Outway (per consumer) Opens mTLS connections to Inways under a grant hash. Grant links give each contracted service a path: /bri, /brp, /lvg, /consent-status. seed-bri-contract.sh
    Grants Service-connection grants carry no properties. The demo removed flow in PR #363 and subject_id_type in #473. The regime follows from the evidence on the request (ADR-0031). seed-bri-contract.sh
    Delegated grants An integrator connects under a DelegatedServiceConnectionGrant. The integrator, the represented consumer and the provider sign it. The provider's Manager admits it only for a registered integration (ADR-0034). seed-bri-delegation-int.sh
    Consent-status service The register peer …0700 publishes consent-status. The PDP peer …0800 connects to it with grant link /consent-status. The register's Manager signs the connection only for peers in the admission register. fsc-seed-consent-status
    ASIP peer The ASIP peer …1200 has an Outway only. It holds a contract for brp on …0200 with grant link /brp. fsc-seed-asip
    Txlog API (per peer) Records each transport transaction (FSC-Logging). It is the authoritative transport record. The ADL records the decisions, and the LDV logbooks record the processings. fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml

    Level 2: EUDI chain¶

    The EUDI chain has the following components:

    Component Responsibility Implementation
    EUDI adapter The bridge between the issuance server and the FSC chain. The issuance server calls POST /attestations/{sourceID}/{typeID}. The adapter takes the BSN from the disclosed PID and builds the query from the source's published graphql block. It calls the source through the EDI Outway with Fsc-Grant-Hash and traceparent. It projects the answer into claims through gbo-simple-v1. It writes two LDV records per issuance: one for the BSN read and one for the assembly of the attestation. It fetches source data per request and stores none (REQ-11). services/eudi-adapter, routes, ldv_issuance.go
    Adapter callback and public endpoints The callback route has no caller authentication (REQ-45, #133). The same listener serves GET /eudi-offers.json (the offer catalog for the frontends) and GET /types/... (Type Metadata). source_release_runtime.go
    Issuance error contract The adapter returns 400 for offer parameters outside the offer, or for a PID without a BSN. It returns 404 if there is no result. If a result does not fit the claims, it returns 502 with GBO_SIMPLE_PATH_MISSING, GBO_SIMPLE_TYPE_MISMATCH, GBO_SIMPLE_RESULT_TYPE, or GBO_SIMPLE_RESULT_AMBIGUOUS. It never issues a partial attestation (REQ-116). internal/gbosimplev1
    Issuance server The nl-wallet issuance server (v0.5.0). It does OpenID4VP disclosure and OpenID4VCI issuance (dc+sd-jwt). It verifies the PID disclosure against issuer_trust_anchors. That list also holds non-PID anchors: the development issuer CA and the issuer CA of every source. An attestation is valid for 365 days. Each type has one status list (REQ-77). A second use case, qtsp-attestation, issues the reference QTSP's test statement. An init step writes the server configuration from the active release. services/eudi-issuance-server, issuance_config.go, qtsp_issuance.go
    Source reconciler Reconciles the configured sources to a desired state. It discovers the FSC contracts. It fetches the source document over FSC, or reads the file for the file transport. It validates the document, and it validates the asi capability against the attribute catalog. Then it writes candidates and statuses. Promotion creates an immutable release and activates it. The --auto-promote flag is for the demo only. reconcile_command.go, source_configuration.go
    Source registry A shared Go module with a PostgreSQL store. The store holds candidates, statuses, immutable releases (content-addressed by SHA-256), and one active-release pointer. It has a writer role and a read-only role. The readers are the adapter, the issuance init step, and the ASIP. The states are pending, active, stale, blocked, and rollout_required. A source is fresh for 15 min and then has a stale grace period of 1 h (REQ-66). services/source-registry, source_metadata_cache.go
    Release runtime Polls the active-release pointer in the adapter. If the release changes, it rebuilds the attestation bindings. If an error occurs, it keeps the previous snapshot. source_release_runtime.go
    gbo-simple-v1 profile A minimal mapping profile that fails closed. It maps one source object to flat claims through RFC 6901 pointers. It allows only scalar data types, with no conversions or expressions. profile, docs/gbo-simple-v1.md
    Certificate set (per source) Issuer, reader, and status-list leaf certificates per source. Sources never share them. A separate privileged command mints the leaves under pre-provisioned CAs. It never mints a CA. Missing or incomplete material blocks only that source (CERTIFICATE_SET_NOT_FOUND, CERTIFICATE_SET_INVALID) (REQ-58). development_ca_provider.go

    The issuance route runs under the PID regime: it carries no consent token. The BSN from the PID is in the PDP input and in both decision logs (REQ-60, ADR-0043). The decision is ADR-0018.

    Level 2: ASI chain¶

    The ASI chain implements the Authentic Source Interface of ETSI TS 119 478, clause 6.1 (ADR-0037). The chain is demo grade. It uses a stub register, development certificates, and a DigiD mock. It has the following components:

    Component Responsibility Implementation
    ASIP Offers clause 6.1.1 verify and 6.1.2 retrieve per data service at /<ds>/authsrc-api. It first verifies the DPoP-bound token. It takes the BSN only from the token (REQ-87). It derives one GraphQL query per request from the source's asi description and sends it through its own Outway (REQ-92). For each attribute, it answers Match, NoMatch, MatchWithVariation, or Unknown. It never returns a source value (REQ-85). It seals every 200 response with a detached JWS in X-JWS-Signature (REQ-83). services/asi-provider, seal.go
    Data services One per authentic source, each with its own base URL, contract, discovery records and token audience (ADR-0038). The demo has one: brp, source rvig. config/dataservices.json
    Source description (asi capability) The source maps its fields onto GBO attribute identifiers. The ASIP reads the active release every 5 s with the reader role. If no current description is available, the data service answers 503. services/asi-mapping, services/source-registry, schemas/asi-attributes.json
    Authorization server Clause 6.1.3. It registers a QTSP with RFC 7591 and a software statement sealed by the QTSP certificate. It verifies the chain and the entitlement QEAA_Provider in the register (REQ-88). It checks the entitlement again every hour (REQ-89). It runs the code flow with PKCE S256 and private_key_jwt. It issues DPoP-bound RFC 9068 tokens (10 min) for exactly one resource (REQ-95). The request page shows who asks for which data at which source (REQ-91). The login is the approval (REQ-90). The token carries the BSN and acr/amr (REQ-86). services/asi-authorization-server
    Register stub Stands in for the national register of relying parties. The server reads it at every lookup. testdata/register.json
    Wallet verifier The nl-wallet verification_server (v0.5.0). It runs the OpenID4VP PID disclosure for the authorization server (use case asi-login, BSN required, REQ-102). As a demo shortcut it also serves the reference QTSP (qtsp-login, no BSN). services/asi-wallet-verifier
    DigiD mock (ASI) A stub means of identification. It accepts nine digits and returns only a BSN. internal/digidmock
    Rule ASI0001 Grants the ASIP peer the BRP fields behind the attributes, on brp only. It does not verify the token or the QTSP. asi0001.rego
    Discover Interface (stub) External role. It answers retrieve from the ASIP's dataService records (REQ-99). For search, it returns 501. services/asi-discovery-stub
    Reference QTSP External role, demo scaffolding. It discovers, registers, gets a token, verifies or retrieves, and accepts a result only with a valid seal. Then it issues a test statement, marked "not qualified", to the wallet. services/qtsp-reference
    Conformance matrix Gives each ETSI requirement ID a status and named tests. If an ID or a test is missing, a CI job fails. conformance

    Trust boundary¶

    The QTSP is not an FSC participant (F-87). It is an OAuth client of the authorization server. Its certificate and its register entitlement admit it. It has no FSC contract.

    The ASIP is an FSC consumer peer of its own. For the PDP, the actor is the ASIP, never the QTSP or the citizen. The ASIP passes nothing about the QTSP into the chain. In demo v0.9.0, the ASIP writes no LDV records.

    ASI verification shows the flow. The ASI requirements give the profile per ETSI clause.

    Level 2: logging and audit¶

    GBO keeps three authoritative records, one per Logius standard (ADR-0036, ADR-0026). One W3C trace ID joins them. The records store the FSC transaction ID next to it (ADR-0035). Logging explains the model. The logging and audit chain has the following components:

    Component Responsibility Implementation
    Authorization Decision Log (ADL) The authoritative record of each PDP decision, contract decisions included. OpenFTV writes it to Postgres ftv_adl. Readers get a SELECT-only role. It holds the request and {allow, reason}. It has no policy version (REQ-59) and no consent-status answer (F-72). For decisions behind the Inway, it has no trace ID and no transaction ID (#369). docker-compose.yml, adl-reader.sql
    LDV logbook Demo stand-in for the logbook of each controller (Verantwoordelijke), one instance per controller. It accepts one record per processing (POST /logboek/records) and serves the read extension (POST /data-processing-operations). It keeps a versioned stand-in register of processing activities. It refuses any record with a run of nine digits that passes the BSN check digit test (elfproef). It uses SQLite with synchronous = FULL. Write and read take separate tokens. services/ldv-logboek
    LDV client A shared Go module. In production, GBO ships this module to chain participants. It does not ship the logbook. The client takes the trace from traceparent. It writes records and waits for the logbook to acknowledge them. It derives the subject in the controller's own pseudonym space. It sets nextLogbookId on outbound calls. A local durable outbox stores each record before delivery. As a result, a logbook outage delays records but does not fail requests. services/ldv-client, outbox.go
    FSC txlog Authoritative transport record per peer (see FSC group). fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml
    Observability stack OpenTelemetry collector, Jaeger, Promtail, Loki and Grafana. The engine's console decision log goes to Loki. These stores are for debugging only. They have no audit function. otel/collector-config.yaml, OBSERVABILITY.md

    The demo runs seven logbooks. Each controller logs its own processings (REQ-72):

    Logbook Controller Writers
    logboek-bd Belastingdienst graphql-server, bron-sidecar
    logboek-brp RvIG brp-graphql-server, brp-sidecar
    logboek-lvg LVG lvg-graphql-server, lvg-sidecar
    logboek-toestemming GBO consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) consent-register, consent-portal-backend
    logboek-eudi-adapter GBO issuance facility eudi-adapter
    logboek-afnemer Hypotheek-BV (consumer) dienstverlener-backend, integrator-backend
    logboek-ir Installatie Register (consumer) ir-backend

    The register logs each status lookup with the verified FSC peer of the PDP as processor (REQ-76). The ASIP writes no records. The consumer logbooks follow candidate condition AV-02.

    Level 2: shared services and mocks¶

    The demo has the following shared services and mocks:

    Component Responsibility Implementation
    BSNk PP mock Follows the BSNk interface as JSON instead of SOAP: /v2/activate, /v2/transform, /v2/provide-dv-keys, /v2/bsn-authorisation-list, and /v2/scheme-keys. It enforces the rules of BSNk. A PI or PP belongs to its requester. A transformation has at most four parties. Only a party on the BSN authorization list gets an identity. It does not encrypt: anyone who holds a value can read it. Only the portal backend calls it, at consent time. services/bsnk-mock, README
    DigiD mocks The consent portal has a DigiD login page. The user types a test BSN, and the portal backend signs a portal token with it. The ASI authorization server has its own stub (see the ASI chain). Demo scaffolding. DigiDAuth.tsx, portalhttp
    Consumer backend and frontend Mock consumer Hypotheek-BV (peer …0300). It starts the consent flow, receives the proof and sends the DvTP query with the placeholder. QUERY_KIND selects the source (bd or lvg) and its placeholder. It writes its own LDV records. Demo scaffolding. services/dienstverlener-backend, dienstverlener-mock
    Installatie Register (LVG pilot) keyper-mock is the IR/Keyper frontend. It has the installer request, the owner approval, and the installer data. ir-backend is the consumer backend with QUERY_KIND=lvg on its own peer …1000. Under one consent, IR calls LVG again at each installer access. IR holds the second consent (citizen to installer). GBO does not hold it. Demo scaffolding. keyper-mock, docs/lvg-ir.md
    Integrator backend Consumer backend on the integrator peer …1100. It calls bri for Hypotheek-BV under a delegated grant. It is opt-in: run make demo-integrator. Demo scaffolding. docs/integrator.md
    Developer portal and backend A cockpit for engineers. It shows the live flow from the trace event stream and a scenario library. It shows the ADL decision next to the engine detail, the LDV chain, the FSC txlogs, and an ASI tab. Rule metadata comes from a generated rules.json. Demo scaffolding. developer-portal, services/dev-portal-backend
    OpenFTV Manager, UI, Keycloak Opt-in policy administration point. It keeps the policies in Postgres and makes a tagged bundle that the PDP pulls. For more information, see policy lifecycle. services/openftv-manager, services/openftv-manager-ui
    Landing page Public explainer with links to the demo UIs. Demo scaffolding. landing-page

    The demo removed the old sector PIP (#378). Admission runs through the admission register and the contract decision. The decision in ADR-0022 is deferred.

    Runtime view

    Runtime view¶

    The runtime view shows how the building blocks work together at runtime. Each page covers one scenario or a small group of scenarios. Each page has these parts:

    • a sequence diagram with numbered steps,
    • the data that each hop carries,
    • the error and failure paths, with links to the tests in gbo-demo v0.9.0,
    • the main observations, with links to requirements, findings, and open questions.

    A built scenario is a scenario that gbo-demo v0.9.0 implements, with the error paths that its page lists. A design-level scenario has no implementation. A design-level page describes the intended sequence and names the open points.

    Two planes¶

    The scenarios fall into two planes:

    • Data plane. A request reads source data about a citizen. Every request takes the same route (ADR-0004, ADR-0002), in this order:

      1. the FSC Outway of the consumer (afnemer),
      2. the FSC Inway of the source, as PEP,
      3. the PDP of the source,
      4. the source gateway,
      5. the source API.

      The scenarios differ in the evidence that the request carries.

    • Management plane. No citizen data travels. The scenarios in this plane admit parties, take sources into use, and bring policy to the PDP. These scenarios come before the first request.

    Scenarios¶

    Scenario Page Route Actor Status Main ADRs

    Consumer requests data under consent, directly or through an integrator DvTP query DvTP Consumer or integrator built 0031, 0032, 0033, 0034, 0013
    Citizen views and revokes consents DvTP citizen access DvTP Citizen built 0032, 0040
    Citizen receives an attestation (PuB-EAA route) EUDI issuance EUDI issuance Citizen with a wallet built 0018, 0016, 0017, 0028
    QTSP verifies or retrieves attributes ASI verification ASI verification QTSP, citizen built 0037, 0038, 0039, 0041
    Contract admission and source activation Admission and activation all (management plane) Consumer, FSC Manager of the provider, operator built 0015, 0034, 0016, 0023
    Policy distribution Policy distribution all (management plane) Operator of the bronhouder built (bundle mode is opt-in) 0021, 0002
    Government consumer requests data under a legal basis Gov-to-Gov Gov-to-Gov Government consumer design-level 0031, 0004
    Cross-border evidence request SDG-OOTS SDG-OOTS Competent authority in another member state design-level 0020, 0031
    Citizen presents an attestation to a relying party Relying-party presentation EUDI presentation Citizen, relying party design-level (no GBO runtime) 0018, 0028, 0023

    Routes¶

    A route is a path from a source to a party that uses the data. The PDP of the source judges each request under one regime. The evidence in the request selects the regime (ADR-0031, Authorization).

    Three routes are built in gbo-demo v0.9.0:

    • DvTP. A private consumer reads source data with the consent of the citizen. The request carries a signed consent proof, so the PDP uses the consent regime. The consumer never gets a BSN (Consent).
    • EUDI issuance. The GBO issuance facility reads source data for a citizen who discloses a PID from the wallet. The request carries no consent proof, so the PDP uses the PID regime. The bronhouder is the PuB-EAA provider. GBO operates the technical facility (ADR-0028).
    • ASI verification. A QTSP verifies or retrieves attributes at the ASI provider (ASIP). The ASIP calls the source over FSC under the PID regime. The QTSP itself is not an FSC participant (F-87).

    Three routes exist only at design level:

    • Gov-to-Gov. A government consumer reads source data under a legal basis. The regime needs its own positive evidence. No rule set for this regime exists.
    • SDG-OOTS. A competent authority in another member state requests evidence through the Once-Only Technical System. AS4 exists only at the edge. No implementation exists.
    • Relying-party presentation. The citizen presents a wallet attestation to a relying party. No GBO decision component and no source take part.

    Data classification¶

    The data-per-hop tables use the tags of the classification table in Consent: what travels where. That table gives each data item (for example the consent proof, VI, VP, subject_ref, and BSN) a meaning, a sensitivity, and the hops where it occurs. The runtime pages add only items that the table does not have, for example contract proposals, admission records, and policy bundles. Those items carry no citizen data.

    The error tables give administrator codes. The consumer gets only a coarse code (REQ-06, Authorization).

    • Requirements: REQ-06, REQ-74

    DvTP: the citizen gives consent¶

    In DvTP, the consumer is a private service provider (dienstverlener). A citizen at the consumer goes to the consent portal (toestemmingsportaal), logs in, and gives consent for one or more data sets. The result is a consent record in the consent register (toestemmingsregister) and a signed consent proof. The proof goes back to the consumer. The consumer uses the proof in DvTP query.

    For the concepts, see Consent and Pseudonymization. For the components, see Level 2: consent chain. The main decisions are ADR-0032 (the consent proof) and ADR-0040 (route D, proposed).

    Sequence¶

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor B as Citizen browser end box rgb(241,239,232) Consumer participant DVF as Consumer frontend end box rgb(254,220,216) Consent facility participant PF as Portal frontend participant PB as Consent portal backend participant CR as Consent register end box rgb(241,239,232) External participant BSNK as BSNk mock end B->>DVF: Start a request, for example a mortgage DVF->>PF: Redirect with service, purpose, scope,<br/>client_oin, client_name, valid_until, return_url Note over PF: The return_url origin must be on the allowlist.<br/>A scope the portal cannot describe stops the request. B->>PF: Log in (DigiD mock) PF->>PB: POST /portal/login {citizen_bsn} PB-->>PF: Portal token (HS256, sub = BSN) B->>PF: Choose data sets (one toggle per set) and give consent PF->>PB: POST /portal/consents<br/>dienstverlener_oin, scopes, validity_seconds, use_case PB->>PB: subject_ref = HMAC of the BSN (SUBJECT_REF_KEY) PB->>CR: GET /subjects/{subject_ref}/polymorphic alt First consent of this citizen CR-->>PB: 404 not found PB->>BSNK: POST /v2/activate {BSN} BSNK-->>PB: PI and PP for the portal PB->>CR: PUT /subjects/{subject_ref}/polymorphic {PI, PP} else Later consent CR-->>PB: PI and PP end PB->>BSNK: GET /v2/bsn-authorisation-list<br/>(copy kept up to BSN_AUTHORISATION_LIST_MAX_AGE) BSNK-->>PB: OINs that can receive the BSN PB->>BSNK: POST /v2/transform PP to VP<br/>every source, at most four per call BSNK-->>PB: VP per source PB->>BSNK: POST /v2/transform PI to VI<br/>listed sources only BSNK-->>PB: VI per listed source PB->>CR: POST /consents<br/>encrypted_subject, subject_ref, dienstverlener_oin,<br/>scopes, use_case, validity_seconds Note over CR: Stores the record and its LDV record in one transaction.<br/>Signs the ES256 proof. Does not store VI or VP. CR-->>PB: 201 consent_id, consent_token PB-->>PF: consent_id, consent_token PF->>DVF: Redirect to return_url with status=ok and consent_id,<br/>consent_token in the URL fragment Note over DVF: Reads the fragment and removes it from the URL

    Data per hop¶

    The tags in the last column are the data classes of What travels where. Each hop carries the following data:

    # From → to Endpoint In Out Data and notes
    1 Citizen → consumer frontend (UI) — — The consumer starts the request. No identity data travels at this hop
    2 Consumer frontend → portal frontend Redirect service, purpose, scope, client_oin, client_name, valid_until, return_url — Low: OIN and scope. All values are unsigned and come from the URL (useRedirectContext.ts#L29-L41). The portal checks only the return origin. REQ-111 asks for the name, the purpose, and the return address from the registration. For more information, see Q-60
    3 Citizen → portal frontend (UI) Login with the DigiD mock — The citizen types the BSN as the password. This shortcut exists only in the demo
    4 Portal frontend → portal backend POST /portal/login citizen_bsn — The BSN is in the browser and on the wire. In production, the identity comes from the MijnOverheid login (REQ-24, Q-50)
    5 Portal backend → portal frontend — — Portal token, HS256, sub = BSN The BSN is inside the token (auth.go#L17-L36). Later calls send this token instead of a raw BSN
    6 Citizen → portal frontend (UI) Data-set choice — One toggle per data set. The citizen cannot choose single fields (REQ-10). The portal shows only the requested sets
    7 Portal frontend → portal backend POST /portal/consents Portal token, dienstverlener_oin, scopes, validity_seconds, use_case — The body holds no BSN. The backend takes the BSN from the verified token. use_case is the redirect purpose (PortaalConsent.tsx#L77-L87). The consumer sets the validity (Q-13)
    8 Portal backend (internal) — BSN subject_ref The portal computes an HMAC of the BSN with its own secret, versioned key (subjectref.go#L40-L52, route D). The portal does not call BSNk
    9 Portal backend → register GET /subjects/{subject_ref}/polymorphic subject_ref — Medium: subject_ref. Only the portal asks for these values
    10 Register → portal backend — — 404 The register has no values, because this is the first consent of this citizen
    11 Portal backend → BSNk POST /v2/activate BSN, requester OIN and key set version of the portal — The portal sends the BSN to BSNk, once per citizen. The mock follows the BSNk interface, but uses JSON instead of SOAP (BSNK-11)
    12 BSNk → portal backend — — PI and PP Medium. Only the portal, as requester, can use them (BSNK-03)
    13 Portal backend → register PUT /subjects/{subject_ref}/polymorphic subject_ref, PI, PP — The register keeps PI and PP under the reference (REQ-69). The register gets no BSN and no per-party value
    14 Register → portal backend — — PI and PP Later consent: the portal finds the values again and does not activate (portal.go#L298-L321)
    15 Portal backend → BSNk GET /v2/bsn-authorisation-list — — The portal reads the list only when its copy is older than BSN_AUTHORISATION_LIST_MAX_AGE (default 1 hour, an assumption)
    16 BSNk → portal backend — — OINs that can receive the BSN The BSN authorization list (BSNK-06). If the copy is too old and BSNk does not answer, the portal gives no consent
    17 Portal backend → BSNk POST /v2/transform PP, per source EntityID (OIN), KeySetVersion, IdentifierType=Pseudonym — The portal makes this call for every source in CONSENT_SOURCES. One call holds at most four parties. More sources give more calls (BSNK-05)
    18 BSNk → portal backend — — VP per source Only its own source can read a VP (BSNK-08). In the demo, anyone can read the values, because the mock does not encrypt
    19 Portal backend → BSNk POST /v2/transform PI, per listed source EntityID, KeySetVersion, IdentifierType=Identity — The portal makes this call only for sources on the list. If no source is on the list, this call does not occur. A party can occur only once per call, so each form takes its own call
    20 BSNk → portal backend — — VI per listed source High at the recipient, and unreadable for others. This call and calls 17 and 18 work only while the citizen is logged in (BSNK-04)
    21 Portal backend → register POST /consents encrypted_subject (per OIN a pseudonym and, if listed, an identity, each with key_set_version), subject_ref, dienstverlener_oin, scopes, use_case, validity_seconds — The register never gets a BSN (REQ-23). Before this call, the portal writes its LDV record dataverwerking.bsn-pseudonimisering under subject_ref (portal.go#L153-L174, REQ-72)
    22 Register → portal backend — — consent_id, consent_token The register signs the proof and stores the record with dataverwerking.toestemming-verlenen in one transaction (main.go#L449-L484). It does not store the per-party values (REQ-80). For the proof claims, see The consent proof
    23 Portal backend → portal frontend — — consent_id, consent_token Medium-high: the proof. The payload holds no BSN
    24 Portal frontend → consumer frontend Redirect to return_url status=ok, consent_id in the query, consent_token in the fragment — The fragment does not reach a server log (PortaalBevestiging.tsx#L56-L64). The consumer cannot read the citizen from the proof (F-76). The question of what the redirect gives back is partly answered (Q-44)

    Error paths¶

    The consent flow has no policy decision. Each failure stops the flow before the register stores a consent. "No consent" means that the citizen stays in the portal and the consumer gets no redirect. If a row states a different result, the row applies. The consent flow has the following error paths:

    Trigger What the consumer sees Administrator reason Pinned by (v0.9.0)
    The return_url origin is not on the allowlist, or a required redirect parameter is missing No redirect. The portal has no request context and cannot send the citizen back validatedRedirectContext returns null redirectValidation.test.mjs#L24
    A requested scope that the portal cannot describe No redirect. The citizen sees an unknown request (shown as "Onbekend verzoek") and cannot consent (REQ-119 gap) The scope is in unknown of requestedScopeGroups scopeGroups.test.mjs#L16, PortaalConsent.tsx#L63-L75
    The citizen cancels the login or refuses consent A redirect with status=denied and no consent_id. The portal does not record the refusal (Q-43) — Code only: PortaalConsent.tsx#L100-L106, DigiDAuth.tsx#L73-L80
    The portal token is missing, expired, or not signed by the portal No consent. The portal answers HTTP 401 invalid token: … Code only: portalhttp.go#L138-L147
    No source configured in CONSENT_SOURCES No consent (HTTP 502) no sources configured: a consent no source can read is not given TestGiveConsentNeedsASource
    BSNk fails, or answers for another party, in another form, or without a value No consent (HTTP 502) activate: … or encrypt the subject for the sources: … TestGiveConsentFailsWhenBSNkFails, TestAnAnswerThatDoesNotMatchIsRefused
    The copy of the BSN authorization list is too old and BSNk does not answer No consent (HTTP 502) read the BSN authorisation list: … TestTheAuthorisationListIsNotUsedOutOfDate
    The portal cannot write its LDV record for the pseudonymization No consent (HTTP 502) log pseudonymisation: … TestGiveConsentThatCannotBeLoggedCreatesNoConsent
    The register gets no encrypted_subject, or a party without a pseudonym No consent. The register answers 400, and the portal answers 502 encrypted_subject is required (no plain BSN accepted) TestCreateRefusesAConsentWithoutAnEncryptedSubject
    The register cannot sign, store, or log the consent No consent. The register answers 500 could not issue consent token, could not store consent, or the refused LDV record Code only: main.go#L449-L484

    Main observations¶

    The consent flow in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

    • The BSN boundary. The BSN occurs only in these places:

      • the browser and the portal token (hops 3 to 5),
      • the portal backend (hop 8),
      • BSNk, at the first consent (hop 11).

      The register and the consumer never see the BSN (REQ-20, REQ-23). The BSN in the browser is a demo shortcut.

    • One activation per citizen. At every later consent, the portal finds PI and PP under its own reference. Then the portal only transforms (TestASecondConsentOnlyTransforms). A new SUBJECT_REF_KEY gives every citizen a new reference. Migration to a new key is not built in demo v0.9.0 (Q-56).

    • No consumer identifier in the proof. The proof carries values that only the sources can read. The consumer does not recognize the citizen across consents (F-76). A VP for the consumer itself is not built in demo v0.9.0 (#478).
    • The proof freezes at consent. BSNk makes the values only while the citizen is present. As a result, the parties, the key versions, and the proof form are fixed for the whole validity (F-78, The proof freezes at consent). The portal configuration (CONSENT_SOURCES) names the sources. No catalogue supplies them (REQ-82).
    • BSNk recognition is open. Only a recognized party can activate and transform (BSNK-01). It is open whether the consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) can be a recognized party. It is also open whether the register and the portal backend are one BSNk participant (F-75, Q-26, Q-49).
    • The initiation is not provable. The consumer name, the purpose, and the return address come unsigned from the redirect URL (REQ-37, REQ-111, #427). The record holds the purpose as use_case. The proof does not hold the purpose (REQ-12, Q-69).

    • Some portal duties are not built. Demo v0.9.0 does not have these portal duties:

      • a step in which the citizen states that they saw the information (REQ-107),
      • a plain-language summary to the norm of REQ-117,
      • a separate confirmation of the choice to the citizen (REQ-122).

      It is open whether the portal must prove what the citizen saw (Q-51).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-10, REQ-12, REQ-20, REQ-23, REQ-24, REQ-37, REQ-69, REQ-72, REQ-80, REQ-82, REQ-107, REQ-111, REQ-117, REQ-119, REQ-122, BSNK-01, BSNK-03, BSNK-04, BSNK-05, BSNK-06, BSNK-08, BSNK-11
    • Findings: F-75 (open), F-76 (open), F-78 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-13 (open), Q-26 (open), Q-43 (partly answered), Q-44 (partly answered), Q-49 (open), Q-50 (open), Q-51 (open), Q-56 (open), Q-60 (open), Q-69 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-06a (done), SL-11 (done), SL-47 (done), SL-51 (done)

    DvTP: the consumer queries a source under consent¶

    A consumer (afnemer) asks a source for data about a citizen who gave consent. The consumer sends a GraphQL query and the consent proof through FSC. The PDP of the source decides before any data reaches the source. After an allow, the source fills in the citizen. Besides the direct call, the flow has two variants: a call by an integrator, and a call by the Installatie Register to LVG.

    For the concepts, see Authorization, Consent, and Pseudonymization. For the components, see Level 2: authorization chain and Level 2: bronhouder. The main decisions are ADR-0031, ADR-0032, and ADR-0033.

    The precondition is that the consumer has an FSC contract with the source. The Manager of the source signed the contract after a positive admission decision of the same PDP (REQ-61, REQ-62). For that scenario, see Admission and activation.

    Sequence¶

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Consumer participant DV as Consumer backend end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis: FSC and PDP participant HVO as HV Outway participant BDM as BD Manager participant BDI as BD Inway (PEP) participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP<br/>mapper and Rego policy participant POUT as PDP Outway participant CRIN as Register Inway end box rgb(254,220,216) DvTP participant CR as Consent register end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant SC as bron-sidecar participant DEC as Decryption component end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant SRC as graphql-server end Note over DV: Holds the consent proof.<br/>Holds no identifier of the citizen. DV->>HVO: POST /bri/graphql with variables.bsn = consent:identity<br/>X-GBO-Consent-Token, Fsc-Transaction-Id, traceparent HVO->>BDM: Request an access token for the bri grant (mTLS) BDM-->>HVO: Access token without grant properties HVO->>BDI: Body and headers unchanged, Fsc-Authorization (mTLS) BDI->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation<br/>subject = HV peer, body, headers PDP->>PDP: Mapper builds the FTV field list.<br/>A consent token is present, so the consent regime applies. opt JWKS not cached, older than 300 s, or unknown kid PDP->>CR: GET /.well-known/jwks.json CR-->>PDP: ES256 public keys end PDP->>PDP: Verify the signature, then the claims (30 s skew) PDP->>POUT: GET /consent-status/consents/{id}/status<br/>no cache, 2 s timeout POUT->>CRIN: FSC (mTLS and access token) CRIN->>CR: GET /consents/{id}/status (port 4012) CR-->>PDP: ACTIVE, REVOKED or 404, back over FSC PDP->>PDP: Rules: actor, placeholder, scope, years, fields PDP-->>BDI: Allow with the granted fields BDI->>SC: POST /graphql, body and X-GBO-Consent-Token unchanged SC->>SC: Take the VI for its own OIN from the proof SC->>DEC: POST /signed-encrypted-identity (VI, own keys) DEC-->>SC: BSN and recipient OIN SC->>SC: Recipient is the own OIN, so replace the placeholder with the BSN SC->>SRC: POST /graphql with variables.bsn = BSN SRC-->>SC: Data, selected fields only SC-->>BDI: Data BDI-->>HVO: Data HVO-->>DV: Data

    Data per hop¶

    The tags (for example Medium and Low) are the data classes of What travels where. The hop numbers refer to the steps of the sequence:

    # From → to Endpoint In Out Data and notes
    1 Consumer backend → HV Outway POST /bri/graphql Body {query, variables} with variables.bsn = "consent:identity". Headers X-GBO-Consent-Token, Fsc-Transaction-Id, and traceparent — Plain GraphQL, no envelope. The placeholder names the citizen (REQ-79). The consumer reads only consent_id and scopes from the proof (token.go#L32-L52). It sends the proof unchanged (AV-05, outway.go#L34-L51). The year filter travels inside the query (kind.go#L75-L95)
    2 HV Outway → BD Manager Token request Grant hash of the bri contract — The Manager of the providing peer issues the access token
    3 BD Manager → HV Outway — — Access token (certificate-bound JWT) Medium. The token carries sub, service_name, grant_hash, and service_peer_id. It has no grant properties, so flow and subject_id_type are not in it (REQ-74)
    4 HV Outway → BD Inway FSC transport Body 1:1, Fsc-Authorization, X-GBO-Consent-Token, and Fsc-Transaction-Id — FSC native transport over mTLS (ADR-0003)
    5 BD Inway → PDP POST /authzen/v1/evaluation subject (HV peer, token attributes), action.properties.body, resource, and context.headers — The AuthZEN plugin of the Inway is the PEP. It passes the request unchanged (REQ-42). The Inway sends no traceparent. It correlates with X-Request-ID = Fsc-Transaction-Id (ftv-graphql-profile.md#L105-L106)
    6 PDP (internal) Mapper, then policy AuthZEN request FTV field list The mapper only maps (Query mapping). The policy reads the token from the headers and selects the regime (engine.rego#L173-L181, Regime selection)
    7 PDP → register GET /.well-known/jwks.json — — Direct, without FSC. Only if the cache is empty or older than 300 seconds, or if the kid is unknown
    8 Register → PDP — — ES256 public keys Low. No stale-key fallback
    9 PDP (internal) Proof verification X-GBO-Consent-Token consent_id, scopes, dienstverlener_oin, and valid_until The policy verifies the proof. The mapper does not (REQ-68, REQ-18, consent.rego#L174-L186). The policy does not read encrypted_subject. It only requires a pseudonym per party
    10 PDP → PDP Outway GET /consent-status/consents/{id}/status consent_id, traceparent, and Fsc-Transaction-Id — Medium: consent_id. Per evaluation, no cache, 2-second timeout, and raise_error: false (consent.rego#L194-L200)
    11 PDP Outway → Register Inway FSC service consent-status Same as hop 10 — From the PDP peer …0800 to the register peer …0700 (FSC peers, REQ-76)
    12 Register Inway → register Status listener, port 4012 consent_id — The listener serves only the status. If the request has no FSC peer, the listener answers 401. The register logs the lookup with the calling peer as processor
    13 Register → PDP — — {status} or 404 Only the status is online. The content of the consent comes from the proof (F-61)
    14 PDP (internal) Rules Resolved consent, field list, and subject Decision per field DVT0001 binds the fields of service bri. It checks actor binding, placeholder, scope, years, and fields (REQ-48, REQ-97, dvt0001.rego#L72-L80). The PDP input holds no BSN and no pseudonym
    15 PDP → BD Inway AuthZEN decision — decision: true, granted fields The engine adds the resolved consent to its response for the console log (engine.rego#L25-L29). The ADL records the request and the decision (ADR-0036)
    16 BD Inway → bron-sidecar POST /graphql Body 1:1, X-GBO-Consent-Token, and Fsc-Authorization — The Inway forwards only after the allow. Only the source Inways reach the source gateway (REQ-81, Network isolation)
    17 Source gateway (internal) Substitution Proof, body VI for OWN_PEER_OIN If the request carries a consent token, the source gateway takes the subject from that token. The source gateway does not verify the token again (substitution.go#L105-L107)
    18 Source gateway → decryption component POST /signed-encrypted-identity VI, own decryption keys, and scheme keys — For consent:pseudonym, the source gateway sends the VP to /signed-encrypted-pseudonym. No BSNk call in the query path (REQ-21, BSNK-09)
    19 Decryption component → source gateway — — BSN, recipient OIN BSN, inside the source boundary. In the demo, the three sources share one decryption component and one OIN
    20 Source gateway (internal) Recipient check and substitution BSN, recipient Body with the BSN The value must name the own OIN as recipient (REQ-80, substitution.go#L213-L232). The source gateway logs the decryption in the LDV logbook of the source
    21 Source gateway → source POST /graphql variables.bsn = BSN — BSN only at the source. The query and operationName stay the same
    22 Source → source gateway — — {data} Only the selected fields (REQ-08). The source gateway logs the forward
    23 to 25 Source gateway → BD Inway → HV Outway → consumer — — {data} No BSN in the response. The consumer logs its processing under the consent_id (F-76, Q-27)

    Variant: an integrator calls for the consumer¶

    An integrator is a software party that calls the source for a consumer under FSC delegation (ADR-0034, integrator.md). The demo runs this variant opt-in with make demo-integrator. The consent stays a consent to the consumer (Hypotheek-BV, peer …0300).

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Integrator participant INT as integrator-backend end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant IO as Integrator Outway participant BDM as BD Manager participant BDI as BD Inway (PEP) participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP end box rgb(237,233,254) Admission register participant REG as Admission register end REG-->>PDP: acts_for of the integrator (PIP pull, every 5 s) INT->>IO: POST /bri/graphql with the proof of Hypotheek-BV IO->>BDM: Request an access token for the delegated grant BDM-->>IO: Access token, sub = integrator, act.sub = Hypotheek-BV IO->>BDI: Body, headers and token BDI->>PDP: AuthZEN, subject.id = integrator,<br/>outway_delegator_peer_id = Hypotheek-BV PDP->>PDP: Proof names Hypotheek-BV?<br/>Integrator active and mandated for Hypotheek-BV in DVT0001? PDP-->>BDI: Allow or deny Note over BDI: After an allow, hops 16 to 25 of the main sequence follow

    The integrator variant differs from the direct call in these hops:

    # What differs from the direct call
    1 The admission register (dvtp-onboarding-register) supplies integrations as acts_for on the entry of the integrator. A mandate names the represented party and the rules (REQ-106, AV-06)
    2 integrator-backend is the consumer backend behind the own Outway of the integrator (peer …1100). The proof is the proof that the portal gave to Hypotheek-BV
    3 to 4 The contract is a DelegatedServiceConnectionGrant between the integrator, Hypotheek-BV, and the source. The OpenFSC Manager puts the delegator in act.sub. This is the reverse of RFC 8693 (integrator.md#L61-L67)
    6 The Inway maps the delegator to subject.attributes.outway_delegator_peer_id. The policy reads that field and does not read the claim
    7 The consent binds the represented party. This is the delegator, or else subject.id (lib.rego#L62-L72). Every delegated call also needs a mandate for that party and the granting rule (engine.rego#L253-L266)

    At the source, the source gateway and the source log the integrator as foreignOperation.processor. The LDV record has no field for "on behalf of". The FSC transaction log of the source records both peers (integrator.md#L132-L152). It is open whether the proof must name the integrator (Q-46).

    Variant: the Installatie Register asks LVG about ownership¶

    The LVG pilot uses the same consent pattern with a different consumer and a different source (lvg-ir.md). The Installatie Register (IR) asks the national buildings facility (LVG) whether a building unit belongs to the citizen. The citizen gives two consents:

    • One consent to IR in the consent portal (toestemmingsportaal), with scope lvg:vbo:eigendom. This consent is in GBO.
    • One consent to the installer inside IR. This consent is not in GBO.
    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor B as Citizen end box rgb(241,239,232) IR participant K as keyper-mock (IR) participant IRB as ir-backend end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant IRO as IR Outway participant BDI as BD Inway (PEP) participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP participant LS as lvg-sidecar end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant LVG as lvg-graphql-server end Note over K: Holds the proof of the consent<br/>citizen to IR, scope lvg:vbo:eigendom B->>K: Approve the installer (IR consent, outside GBO) K->>IRB: Ownership check for a vboId, with the proof IRB->>IRO: POST /lvg/graphql<br/>vbo(bsn = consent:identity, vboId) IRO->>BDI: FSC, service lvg on peer …0200 BDI->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation PDP->>PDP: LVG0001 with the consent checks of DVT0001,<br/>scope pinned to lvg:vbo:eigendom PDP-->>BDI: Allow BDI->>LS: Body and proof unchanged LS->>LS: Decrypt the VI, replace the placeholder with the BSN LS->>LVG: vbo(bsn, vboId) LVG-->>IRB: vboId or null, back through LS, BDI and IRO IRB-->>K: Ownership confirmed or not

    The LVG variant differs from the direct call in these hops:

    # What differs from the direct call
    2 to 3 ir-backend is the consumer backend with QUERY_KIND=lvg (kind.go#L47-L53). The query is vbo(bsn: $bsn, vboId: $vboId) { vboId } with the placeholder in $bsn
    4 IR has its own peer …1000, so the actor binding tells IR apart from Hypotheek-BV. LVG is a logical source behind bd-inway on the shared provider peer
    5 to 6 Hops 6 to 14 of the main sequence apply: proof verification and the online status lookup. If a consent does not have the LVG scope, LVG0001 denies with SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED
    9 lvg-sidecar logs lvg-identiteit-ontsleuteling and lvg-bronquery-doorgifte in the LVG logbook. lvg-graphql-server logs lvg-vbo-eigendom, also for null
    11 to 12 Three outcomes are possible: the vboId (the citizen is the owner), null (not the owner), or a deny (no valid consent). Only if the citizen is the owner does IR record the access of the installer (lvg-ir.md#L64-L70)

    IR keeps the proof. At every access of an installer, IR asks again under the same consent. After a revocation, the next question fails (lvg-ir.md#L60-L62, Repeated use). With one consent, IR can ask about any vboId. The pilot must answer whether the vboId belongs in the consent (lvg-ir.md#L113-L114).

    Error paths¶

    A deny carries two layers of reason (Reason codes, REQ-06):

    • Consumer code: the PDP puts this code in reason_user, and the ADL stores it. It never names the field or the failed check.
    • Administrator codes: these codes are per field. They reach only the OPA console decision log. For a server fault, the request code is PIP_UNAVAILABLE, and the trace keeps the cause.

    In demo v0.9.0, the FSC Inway removes the consumer code. The Inway reads reasonUser, but the PDP sends reason_user (ftv-graphql-profile.md#L93-L96). As a result, the consumer gets a deny without a code. The consumer backend then shows UNAVAILABLE to the citizen (denial.go#L12-L56).

    On every PDP deny, no request reaches the source gateway or the source. If one field has more than one reason, the administrator code is the first reason in a fixed order (engine.rego#L321-L339). The error paths have these triggers and codes:

    Trigger Consumer code Administrator code Pinned by (v0.9.0)
    The citizen revoked the consent FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_WITHDRAWN consent_test.rego#L197-L207, dvt0001_test.rego#L72
    valid_until passed, within the 30-second skew FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_EXPIRED dvt0001_test.rego#L76
    exp passed by more than 30 seconds FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_TOKEN_EXPIRED consent_test.rego#L347
    Forged or tampered proof, unknown kid, an algorithm other than ES256, no signature, or no JWT FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_SIGNATURE_INVALID consent_test.rego#L318-L345, scenario use-bogus-consent-deny
    The request has two tokens. Or the token has a wrong type, issuer, or audience, or misses a claim. Or it has no encrypted_subject, a party without a pseudonym, or a valid_until other than exp FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_CONTEXT_INVALID consent_test.rego#L380-L424, #L438
    The PDP cannot fetch the JWKS ACCESS_DENIED PIP_UNAVAILABLE, trace CONSENT_KEYS_UNAVAILABLE consent_test.rego#L297
    The status lookup fails, times out, or gives an unexpected answer ACCESS_DENIED PIP_UNAVAILABLE, trace CONSENT_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE consent_test.rego#L303-L314
    The register does not know the consent FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_NOT_FOUND consent_test.rego#L291
    The proof names a party other than the represented party of the call FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_ACTOR_MISMATCH dvt0001_test.rego#L84, lvg0001_test.rego#L44
    The proof has no scope of this rule, for example an LVG consent on income fields FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED dvt0001_test.rego#L92-L102, lvg0001_test.rego#L38
    A year without bd:ib:<year> in the proof, or no year filter in the query FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED YEAR_NOT_COVERED dvt0001_test.rego#L167-L176, scenarios use-hypotheek-2023-deny, use-jaar-niet-geconsenteerd-deny
    The subject is a literal BSN, consent:pseudonym, a different string, or a schema default FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH dvt0001_test.rego#L131-L154, lvg0001_test.rego#L48-L55
    A field that no consent rule covers, for example box2Inkomen FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED NO_APPLICABLE_RULE engine_test.rego#L210-L220, scenario use-veld-buiten-scope-deny
    The consumer omits the proof FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED PID regime: PID_NOT_PRESENT (placeholder) or ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED (literal BSN) engine_test.rego#L341-L355, disjoint actors #L371
    The mapper cannot build a complete field list COVERAGE_UNVERIFIABLE <subcode> (INVALID_QUERY gives FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED) The same code and subcode engine_test.rego#L117-L129, appendix_a_test.rego#L214-L219
    A mutation or a subscription OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED appendix_a_test.rego#L221-L225
    A delegated call without a mandate for this party and rule, or from a suspended integrator FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED engine_test.rego#L621-L629, #L692-L711
    A delegated call while the admission register is not available ACCESS_DENIED PIP_UNAVAILABLE, trace INTEGRATOR_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE engine_test.rego#L631-L642
    After the allow: the proof has no value of the asked form for this source (a source not on the BSN authorization list has no VI) HTTP 400 the subject of the consent could not be filled in Source gateway log subject substitution failed (ErrNoValue), LDV decryption record with an error status substitution_test.go#L186
    After the allow: BSNk made the value for a different party HTTP 400, with the message of the preceding row ErrRecipient substitution_test.go#L112, #L234
    A request with a literal subject under a proof reaches the source gateway (so it did not pass the PDP) HTTP 400, with the same message ErrLiteralSubject substitution_test.go#L141
    The source gateway cannot log the decryption HTTP 500 the decryption could not be logged; refusing the request Code only: main.go#L236-L244
    A request outside the transport subset reaches the source gateway HTTP 404, 405, 400, or 415, before any decryption The transport reason transport_test.go#L14, #L83

    The code CONSENT_SCOPE_MISMATCH does not exist. A consent without a matching scope gives SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED. A year outside the consent gives YEAR_NOT_COVERED.

    Observations¶

    The DvTP run in demo v0.9.0 shows these facts:

    • The evidence selects the regime. A consent token, verified or not, puts the request in the consent regime. If the request has no consent token, only PID-regime rules apply. No header, grant property, or default decides the regime (REQ-74, ADR-0031). The PID regime starts when a proof is absent. As a result, its actor lists must stay disjoint from consent consumers (F-70).
    • The legal basis travels as a proof, and the status stays online. The PDP verifies the proof locally. It asks only for the status, per request and fail-closed (REQ-68, F-61). As a result, every DvTP request depends on the register (REQ-75, Q-05). The status answer is not in the PDP input, so the ADL cannot replay the decision (F-72).
    • The subject comes from the proof. The consumer names the citizen only with a placeholder (REQ-79, Subject binding). The PDP does not check who the subject is. It checks only that the subject comes from the proof. One request is about one citizen (F-77).
    • The rule "after the decision" depends on network isolation. The source gateway does not verify the token again. A consumer holds real proofs, so a second verification gives no protection. Only the source Inways reach the source gateway (REQ-81, F-79, ADR-0033). In Kubernetes, this isolation needs a NetworkPolicy (Deployment units and network zones).
    • BSNk is not in the query path. The source reads its own value with its own keys (REQ-21, BSNK-04). A source keeps older keys while proofs for that key version are valid (AV-09). In demo v0.9.0, no demo rule accepts consent:pseudonym, because no demo source takes a pseudonym (#474).
    • The PDP gives a clean deny instead of an HTTP error. For an unknown consent or an unreachable register, the PDP makes a policy decision with a reason in the decision record. The consumer does not get an upstream error (F-24).
    • The records correlate. The consumer sends traceparent and Fsc-Transaction-Id (REQ-55, AV-01, ADR-0035). The Inway does not pass traceparent to the PDP. The policy puts both on the status lookup. For how the records join, see Logging.
    • A suspended consumer keeps access. A consumer with an existing contract can still send queries, also with a valid consent (REQ-110, Q-53).
