    DvTP: the citizen views and revokes consents¶

    A logged-in citizen opens the page My consents (shown as "Mijn toestemmingen") in the consent portal (toestemmingsportaal). The portal shows the consents of the citizen with their status, and the citizen revokes one consent. The portal finds the consents through its own reference to the citizen, without a BSNk call. A revocation takes effect at the next request of the consumer.

    For the concepts, see Revocation and Citizen recognition: route D. For the components, see Level 2: consent chain. For the requirements, see Citizen access.

    Sequence¶

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor B as Citizen browser end box rgb(254,220,216) Consent facility participant PF as Portal frontend participant PB as Consent portal backend participant CR as Consent register end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant LB as logboek-toestemming end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP end B->>PF: Log in (DigiD mock) and open My consents PF->>PB: GET /portal/consents (portal token) PB->>PB: subject_ref = HMAC of the BSN (SUBJECT_REF_KEY) PB->>LB: LDV record bsn-pseudonimisering,<br/>reason toestemmingen-inzien PB->>CR: GET /consents?subject_ref={subject_ref} CR-->>PB: Consents of this subject_ref PB-->>PF: List with effective_status per consent PF-->>B: Overview with active, expired, and revoked B->>PF: Revoke consent {id} PF->>PB: DELETE /portal/consents/{id} (portal token) PB->>PB: subject_ref = HMAC of the BSN PB->>LB: LDV record bsn-pseudonimisering,<br/>reason toestemming-intrekken PB->>CR: GET /consents/{id} CR-->>PB: Consent with its subject_ref PB->>PB: Ownership check, consent.subject_ref equals subject_ref PB->>CR: DELETE /consents/{id} Note over CR: Sets REVOKED and keeps the record.<br/>Writes the LDV record in the same transaction. CR-->>PB: Consent with status REVOKED PB-->>PF: status REVOKED PF-->>B: Revoked badge Note over PDP: Next query of the consumer on this proof PDP->>CR: Status lookup over FSC CR-->>PDP: REVOKED PDP->>PDP: Deny with CONSENT_WITHDRAWN

    Data per hop¶

    The tags are the data classes of What travels where. Each hop carries the following data:

    # From → to Endpoint In Out Data and notes
    1 Citizen → portal frontend (UI) DigiD mock login Portal token, sub = BSN The same as hops 3 to 5 of DvTP consent. In production, the identity comes from the MijnOverheid login (REQ-24, Q-50)
    2 Portal frontend → portal backend GET /portal/consents Portal token in Authorization — The BSN travels only inside the signed portal token. The citizen sends no reference and no BSN as a parameter (REQ-40)
    3 Portal backend (internal) — BSN subject_ref The portal computes an HMAC with its own secret, versioned key (route D). The portal does not call BSNk (TestListingAndRevokingDoNotCallBSNk)
    4 Portal backend → logbook LDV write dataverwerking.bsn-pseudonimisering under subject_ref, with attribute dpl.gbo.pseudonimiseringAanleiding = toestemmingen-inzien — The derivation is a separate processing (REQ-72, portal.go#L323-L340). The record holds no BSN
    5 Portal backend → register GET /consents?subject_ref={subject_ref} subject_ref — Medium. The register refuses a listing without subject_ref (TestAnUnscopedListingIsRefused). Only the network keeps other callers out (REQ-39, Q-58)
    6 Register → portal backend — — Records with consent_id, subject_ref, dienstverlener_oin, scopes, use_case, status, valid_until The records hold no BSN, no PI or PP, and no proof values (REQ-69, TestNoConsentAnswerCarriesThePolymorphicValues). The register logs dataverwerking.toestemming-inzage
    7 Portal backend → portal frontend — — Records plus effective_status The backend derives Revoked from the register status, Expired from valid_until, and otherwise Active (consent.go#L135-L146). The payload holds no BSN (REQ-20)
    8 Portal frontend → citizen (UI) — Overview The overview shows the statuses active (shown as "Actief"), expired (shown as "Verlopen"), and revoked (shown as "Ingetrokken") (REQ-38). The status retrieved (shown as "Opgehaald") is not built in demo v0.9.0 (Q-42, F-97). The overview has no export (REQ-108, Q-52)
    9 Citizen → portal frontend (UI) Revoke on consent_id — The UI shows the button only for an active consent (MijnToestemmingenDetail.tsx#L127)
    10 Portal frontend → portal backend DELETE /portal/consents/{id} consent_id, portal token — Revocation changes the status of the record. The register keeps the record
    11 Portal backend (internal) — BSN subject_ref As hop 3
    12 Portal backend → logbook LDV write As hop 4, with dpl.gbo.pseudonimiseringAanleiding = toestemming-intrekken — TestListAndRevokeLogTheirPseudonymisation
    13 Portal backend → register GET /consents/{id} consent_id — The backend reads the record to compare the owner. The register logs this read as dataverwerking.toestemming-inzage
    14 Register → portal backend — — Record with subject_ref —
    15 Portal backend (internal) Ownership check consent.subject_ref, subject_ref Allow or ErrNotOwned The check runs on the server side. The register cannot see who calls, so the portal backend does the check (portal.go#L268-L296)
    16 Portal backend → register DELETE /consents/{id} consent_id — The register sets REVOKED, keeps the record, and stores dataverwerking.toestemming-intrekken in the same transaction (main.go#L585-L596). It stores no revocation time (Q-48)
    17 Register → portal backend — — Record with status REVOKED —
    18 to 19 Portal backend → portal frontend → citizen — — {"status": "REVOKED"}, badge The answer holds no pointer to the rights of the citizen at the consumer (REQ-120)
    20 PDP → register Status lookup over FSC consent_id from the proof — Only at the next request of the consumer, as hops 10 to 12 of DvTP query. The consumer gets no message at revocation
    21 Register → PDP — — REVOKED The PDP does not cache the status, so the revocation takes effect at the next request (REQ-14)
    22 PDP (internal) Rules Resolved consent Deny Administrator code CONSENT_WITHDRAWN, consumer code FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED. Another active consent of the same citizen cannot replace the revoked one: the PDP checks only the consent_id from the proof

    Error paths¶

    Each error path shows the citizen an HTTP status and gives the administrator a reason, as follows:

    Trigger What the citizen sees Administrator reason Pinned by (v0.9.0)
    No portal token, or an invalid one The portal shows and changes nothing. HTTP 401 invalid token: … Code only: portalhttp.go#L138-L147
    The consent belongs to another citizen HTTP 403 with reason: consent_not_owned_by_caller. The consent does not change. REQ-40 asks for 404 CONSENT_NOT_FOUND, the same answer as for an unknown consent consent does not belong to authenticated citizen TestRevokeDeniedForOtherCitizen
    The consent does not exist HTTP 404 consent not found TestRevokeUnknownConsentIsNotFound
    A direct backend call revokes an expired or already revoked consent HTTP 200, status REVOKED again, with a new LDV record. REQ-109 asks for a refusal with CONSENT_NOT_REVOCABLE (#600) None: the backend checks only ownership Code only: main.go#L282-L299
    The portal cannot write its LDV record for the derivation The portal shows and changes nothing. HTTP 502 log pseudonymisation: … Code only: portal.go#L323-L340
    The register cannot build its LDV record for the listing or the read The portal shows nothing. The register answers 500, and the portal answers 502 the operation could not be logged; refusing it Code only: ldv_consent.go#L176-L180
    The register is unreachable The portal shows and changes nothing. HTTP 502 list consents: … or revoke: … Code only: portalhttp.go#L94-L106
    The operator replaced SUBJECT_REF_KEY An empty overview, because older consents have the old reference. These consents stay valid for the consumer None Code only: subjectref.go#L40-L52

    Main observations¶

    The citizen-access flow in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

    • The server derives the reference. The portal derives subject_ref from the BSN in the signed portal token. As a result, a citizen cannot list or revoke the consents of another citizen (REQ-40, TestListIsolatesByCitizen).
    • Viewing and revoking need no BSNk. The reference is an HMAC that the portal computes itself (route D, ADR-0040, proposed). A new key gives every citizen a new reference. Migration to a new key is not built (Q-56). It is open whether the register and the portal backend are one system (Q-49).
    • Revocation keeps the record. The status becomes REVOKED and the record stays. The effect reaches the consumer at its next request, through the online status lookup (REQ-14, DvTP query). The demo has no status cache, so the propagation time is one request. The norm for the propagation time is open (REQ-75, Q-47).
    • Every step is a logged processing. The portal logs each derivation of the reference with its reason. The register logs each read and the revocation under subject_ref. No record holds a BSN (TestNoBSNInAnyRecordedProcessing, Logging).
    • The demo does not meet all requirements. A revocation of the consent of another citizen gives 403, where REQ-40 asks for 404. The demo accepts a second revocation (REQ-109). The demo has no export (REQ-108), no rights notice (REQ-120), no "retrieved" status (Q-42), and no revocation time (Q-48).
    • The register trusts its caller. The register serves list, read, and revoke to every caller on its network. Only network placement limits this to the portal backend (REQ-39, Q-58).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-14, REQ-20, REQ-24, REQ-38, REQ-39, REQ-40, REQ-69, REQ-72, REQ-75, REQ-108, REQ-109, REQ-120
    • Findings: F-97 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-42 (open), Q-47 (open), Q-48 (open), Q-49 (open), Q-50 (open), Q-52 (open), Q-56 (open), Q-58 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-06b (done), SL-11 (done), SL-51 (done)

    EUDI issuance: the PuB-EAA route¶

    A citizen scans a QR code, shares the PID from the NL Wallet, and gets an attestation with data from an authentic source. The bronhouder is the PuB-EAA provider. GBO operates the technical issuance facility (ADR-0028, PSA S11). The decision for this route is ADR-0018.

    One issuance in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has hops, data on each hop, and error paths. The following sections give these details and do not explain the concepts again. For the concepts, see these pages:

    • The components: Level 2: EUDI chain.
    • The regime: Regime selection.
    • The source description and its release: Source onboarding.
    • The certificates: EUDI trust roles.
    • The BSN in this route: Exception: the BSN in the EUDI and ASI routes.

    Before the first QR code¶

    The route runs only from an active source release. For each source, the release holds these items:

    • The offers.
    • The GraphQL query and its parameters.
    • The claims.
    • The display texts.
    • A reference to the certificate set.

    GBO generates the issuance configuration and the Type Metadata from the release (REQ-64, ADR-0016, ADR-0017). A valid FSC contract does not activate a source (REQ-65). For that run, see Admission and activation. If no release is active, no offer exists and the portal shows no QR code.

    The demo has two attestation types:

    Type Source (source_id) FSC service Rule Offers Subject of the data
    Income statement (inkomensverklaring) belastingdienst bri EUD0001 Year (jaar) 2024 and 2025 The PID holder
    Death certificate (akte van overlijden) rvig brp EUD0002 One, without parameters The deceased partner of the PID holder (related-person attestation)

    The offers come from the source documents (BD, BRP). In the default demo, both sources are on the Belastingdienst peer …0200 (FSC peers).

    Sequence¶

    The sequence shows the income statement for 2024, cross-device.

    Data per hop¶

    The table marks personal data in bold. The hop numbers refer to the steps of the sequence:

    # From → To Endpoint Data Notes
    1 to 2 Portal → adapter GET /eudi-offers.json (through the portal proxy) Per offer: key, label, source_id, type_id, and parameters No personal data. The adapter serves the offers of the active release (source_release_runtime.go#L95-L104, nginx.conf#L43-L49).
    3 to 4 Citizen ↔ portal — In: the chosen offer. Out: a universal link with request_uri The portal builds the link in the browser (eudi.ts#L42-L51). The QR code is public, so any person can scan it. This is the only initiation route in the demo.
    5 to 7 Wallet ↔ issuance server POST /disclosure/<offer>/request_uri The disclosure request The request asks for one PID claim, bsn (issuance_config.go#L162). The reader certificate of the source names the issuer and the purpose (REQ-58).
    8 to 10 Wallet → issuance server OpenID4VP PID with the BSN The issuance server checks the presentation against issuer_trust_anchors (issuance_server.toml.example#L3-L9). That list also holds non-PID anchors (REQ-45). The approval in the wallet is no legal basis (F-83).
    11 Issuance server → adapter POST /attestations/{sourceID}/{typeID}?<offer parameters> Disclosed attributes, urn:eudi:pid:nl:1 with the BSN Public HTTPS (an ISRG-rooted certificate, through a tunnel). The route has no caller authentication (source_release_runtime.go#L69-L81, #133). For more information, see The callback gap.
    12 Adapter (internal) Active release In: path and body. Out: the BSN The binding of sourceID and typeID must exist in the active release. The adapter takes the BSN from the PID and does not check a signature (main.go#L143-L162, #L23-L26).
    13 Adapter → logbook LDV write Record dataverwerking.pid-bsn-extractie The record names the data subject by a pseudonym that is local to the logbook. It does not hold the BSN. If the logbook does not acknowledge the record, the adapter does not call the source (main.go#L256-L262, ldv_issuance.go#L101-L147, REQ-72).
    14 Adapter (internal) Query plan In: the offer parameters and the query of the release. Out: {query, variables: {bsn, jaar}} The parameters must match a published offer exactly (source_metadata.go#L272-L298). The adapter has no query or mapping of its own (REQ-44).
    15 Adapter → edi-outway POST {outway}/graphql {query, variables} with the BSN, and the headers Fsc-Grant-Hash, Fsc-Transaction-Id, and traceparent The adapter checks that the source document names the contracted service (main.go#L466-L503). No X-GBO-Scope and no flow. The txlog and the trace carry the transaction ID. The ADL record behind the Inway gets its own trace and no transaction ID (#369, REQ-55, ADR-0035).
    16 to 17 edi-outway ↔ edi-manager FSC access token In: the grant hash. Out: a certificate-bound token The Outway caches the token. The grant carries no properties.
    18 edi-outway → bd-inway FSC, mTLS Body 1:1 with the BSN Every channel goes through FSC with a valid certificate (REQ-46).
    19 bd-inway → PDP POST /authzen/v1/evaluation AuthZEN envelope: Outway peer …0100, service bri, and the body with the BSN The Inway is the PEP. The mapper parses the GraphQL and does not call BSNk (Regime selection).
    20 PDP → bd-inway AuthZEN response Allow or deny, per field The request has no consent token, so the PID regime applies. EUD0001 checks the designated issuer, the BSN in the root argument, and allowed_years (eud0001.rego#L45-L75, REQ-74, REQ-97). The PDP writes the BSN to the ADL and the console decision log (REQ-60).
    21 to 22 bd-inway → gateway → source POST /graphql The judged query with the BSN The request has no consent token, so the gateway passes it through unchanged (Level 2: bronhouder). The source logs its own processing.
    23 Source → adapter GraphQL response Income data for the year Back through the same FSC chain, 1:1.
    24 Adapter (internal) gbo-simple-v1 In: the response at result_pointer. Out: flat claims Exactly one result gives claims. Zero results is no_data. Any error gives no attestation (REQ-116). Only scalar claims (REQ-78).
    25 Adapter → logbook LDV write Record dataverwerking.attestatie-samenstellen The record names the number of claims without their values. It points at the logbook of the source. The adapter writes it for every outcome after the call to the source. If the logbook does not acknowledge the record, the adapter withholds the answer (main.go#L283-L292).
    26 Adapter → issuance server Response to hop 11 [{attestation_type: <VCT>, attributes, format: "dc+sd-jwt", id}] with the claims The VCT is the URL of the generated Type Metadata (main.go#L319-L334).
    27 to 28 Issuance server → wallet OpenID4VCI Attestation (SD-JWT VC) Signed with the issuer certificate of the source. Valid 365 days, with one status list per type (issuance_config.go#L166-L180, REQ-77). The wallet shows the issuer from the certificate.

    Public endpoints of the adapter¶

    The adapter serves three routes on one listener (source_release_runtime.go#L59-L106):

    Route Caller Content When the release is not available
    GET /eudi-offers.json Developer portal, consumer frontends The offer catalog 503 for all sources, also when only one source is past its grace period
    GET /types/{sourceID}/{typeID}/v{version} Wallet, relying parties The SD-JWT VC Type Metadata that GBO generates from the claims. Its URL is the VCT. 503
    POST /attestations/{sourceID}/{typeID} Issuance server The attestation callback 503

    The issuance server installs the same Type Metadata bytes and computes vct#integrity over them. A change to the claims or the display needs a different type_version (type_metadata.go#L17-L40, The eudi capability).

    The callback gap¶

    The issuance server checks the PID. The adapter does not know that the request comes from the issuance server. No mechanism binds the BSN in hop 11 to a checked disclosure (REQ-45, Q-18, #133). The demo uses this gap itself. The developer portal has a playground that posts a typed BSN to the adapter (EudiQrPanel.tsx#L36-L51, nginx.conf#L36-L42).

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Caller participant X as Any caller<br/>that reaches the adapter end box rgb(255,237,213) EUDI participant AD as EUDI adapter end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant OW as edi-outway<br/>(designated issuer) participant PDP as PDP<br/>(EUD0001) end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant SRC as Source end X->>AD: POST /attestations/belastingdienst/inkomensverklaring?jaar=2024<br/>body with any BSN, no wallet AD->>OW: Query with that BSN OW->>PDP: Actor …0100, no consent token PDP-->>OW: Allow: designated issuer, BSN present SRC-->>AD: Income data of that person AD-->>X: Claims, without any wallet

    The data on each hop of this gap is as follows:

    # Data Notes
    1 Any BSN No caller authentication, and no proof of a checked disclosure.
    2 to 4 BSN The request has no consent token, so it enters the PID regime. The only gate of this regime is the list of designated issuers (F-70, eudi_helper.rego#L13-L30).
    5 to 6 Income data The caller gets the projected claims.

    SL-25 removed the PID check from the adapter, because the issuance server checks the PID. The issuance server checks the signature, so the gap is in the callback. REQ-45 names two fixes:

    • The adapter checks the SD-JWT itself.
    • The issuance server authenticates the callback and delivers signed evidence.

    Both fixes need the binding of the disclosure to the request. The reference QTSP callback on the same issuance server uses a secret path over CA-pinned HTTPS (qtsp_issuance.go#L134-L152, ASI verification).

    Error paths¶

    The consumer of the adapter is the issuance server. The issuance server gets only the HTTP status. The details are in the adapter log (stage). For a PDP deny, the details are also in the ADL.

    The FSC Inway removes the reason of a deny (ftv-graphql-profile.md#L93-L95). In every error path, no attestation reaches the wallet. The error paths have these triggers and outcomes:

    Trigger Outcome Pinned by (v0.9.0)
    The release is past its grace period for one source GET /eudi-offers.json gives 503 for every source. The portal shows no QR code. source_release_runtime.go#L95-L100
    The adapter cannot load a release 503 source activations unavailable source_release_runtime.go#L70-L74
    sourceID or typeID not in the active release 404 source_release_runtime.go#L75-L79
    Source metadata missing, expired, or past the stale grace (15 min fresh, 1 h grace) 503 source metadata unavailable, for this source only (REQ-66) main.go#L221-L225, source_metadata_cache.go#L10-L14
    Body unreadable, or no disclosed attestation in it 400 main.go#L234-L246
    PID without a BSN 400 no BSN in disclosed PID. The adapter logs nothing and does not call the source. main.go#L249-L253, ldv_test.go#L402
    The logbook does not acknowledge the LDV record of hop 13 500. The adapter does not call the source. main.go#L256-L262, ldv_test.go#L354
    Offer parameters outside the published offer (for example jaar=2023) 400 invalid attestation parameters main.go#L263-L268, main_test.go#L434
    PDP deny: the caller is not a designated issuer ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED in the ADL. The adapter answers 502. eud0001_test.rego#L65, eud0002_test.rego#L36
    PDP deny: no BSN, or a placeholder, in the root argument PID_NOT_PRESENT. The adapter answers 502. eud0001_test.rego#L71-L80, eud0002_test.rego#L42
    PDP deny: the request carries a consent token PID_NOT_PRESENT. The adapter answers 502. eud0001_test.rego#L83
    PDP deny: a year outside allowed_years, or no year filter YEAR_NOT_ALLOWED. The adapter answers 502. eud0001_test.rego#L39-L58
    PDP deny: a field outside the rule (closed world) FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED or NO_APPLICABLE_RULE. The adapter answers 502. engine.rego#L282, Rule model
    Chain unreachable, non-200 answer, or GraphQL errors 502 source request failed. The adapter does not pass on the upstream body. The assembly record has status ERROR. main.go#L294-L300, main_test.go#L444, ldv_test.go#L267
    Result does not fit the claims: GBO_SIMPLE_PATH_MISSING, GBO_SIMPLE_TYPE_MISMATCH, GBO_SIMPLE_RESULT_TYPE 502 source response could not be projected. No partial attestation. The code is only in the adapter log. main.go#L302-L308, profile.go#L33-L37, cases.json#L96-L125
    More than one result 502 with GBO_SIMPLE_RESULT_AMBIGUOUS cases.json#L89-L93
    No result (no_data) 404 source has no data for this subject and parameters. The adapter still writes the assembly record, with zero claims. main.go#L310-L315, cases.json#L82-L86, ldv_test.go#L505
    The logbook does not acknowledge the LDV record of hop 25 500. The adapter withholds the attestation. main.go#L284-L292
    Missing or incomplete certificate set of a source The issuance facility blocks the source (CERTIFICATE_SET_NOT_FOUND, CERTIFICATE_SET_INVALID). Other sources continue to work. REQ-58, A certificate set per source
    A caller posts a body with any BSN directly to the adapter Allowed in demo v0.9.0. The source answers, and the caller gets the claims. Not built: #133, REQ-45

    Related-person attestation: death certificate¶

    The death certificate holds data about the deceased partner of the citizen who shares the PID. The subject of the claims differs from the person who discloses the PID (F-47, REQ-57, SL-43). The run is the same as the run in the preceding sections, with these differences per hop:

    # Difference
    11 POST /attestations/rvig/akte-van-overlijden, without parameters.
    14 to 15 The query is akteVanOverlijden(bsn: $bsn) with the BSN of the PID holder, on service brp.
    19 to 20 EUD0002 decides. It grants a closed list of output fields and checks the BSN in the root argument. It has no year check (eud0002.rego#L20-L66).
    21 to 22 The gateway is brp-sidecar, and the source is brp-graphql-server.
    22 to 23 The source resolves the relation itself. It selects the marriage that ended by the death of the partner. If the partner died on a different date than the dissolution, the source returns nothing. Then the adapter answers 404 (main_test.go#L183).
    25 The deceased is not a data subject under the GDPR. The source logs the requester and the living parents (AV-10).

    The PDP sees only the flat output of the source view. It does not see the relation. The relation depends on the source and on the subject from the PID. Because of the callback gap, a caller can ask for the death certificate for any BSN.

    The preferred design puts the relation in filter arguments of the published schema. The policy then requires these arguments with fixed values (#425, Q-14). In demo v0.9.0, the source description does not mark the relation.

    Observations¶

    The run of an issuance in demo v0.9.0 shows these facts:

    • The regime follows from the evidence. A request without a consent token goes into the PID regime. That regime has no positive evidence of its own. Its only gate is the list of designated issuers. This list must stay disjoint from the consent consumers (REQ-74, F-70, ADR-0031). A test pins the disjointness only for the seeded consumers (engine_test.rego#L366-L376).
    • The PID check and the source query have no link. The issuance server checks the PID. The adapter callback has no authentication (REQ-45, Q-18). The PID trust list also trusts the GBO development CA and the issuer CA of every source.
    • The BSN is in the decision logs. The adapter puts the plain BSN in the query variables. As a result, the BSN is in the PDP input, the ADL, and the console decision log (REQ-60, F-54, ADR-0043, #368). The LDV records of the adapter hold no BSN.
    • The offer and the policy are independent limits. The source offers 2024 and 2025. EUD0001 allows 2024 and 2025. A request for 2023 fails at the adapter (no offer). The PDP also denies it (YEAR_NOT_ALLOWED). Publication by a source does not authorize the published data (F-74).
    • The adapter holds no knowledge of a source. The query, the parameters, the claims, the display, and the Type Metadata come from the release (REQ-64, F-57). The source decides through its own PDP (REQ-44).
    • No partial attestation exists. Any projection error gives 502 and no attestation (REQ-116). The issuance server sees no reason code.
    • The validity is fixed. Every source attestation is valid 365 days. GBO has no change feed from the source. As a result, GBO cannot revoke an attestation when the source data changes (REQ-77, F-82).
    • Correlation works, with one gap. The adapter sends one Fsc-Transaction-Id and a traceparent. The txlog, the LDV records of the adapter and the source, and the trace share them. The ADL record behind the Inway has its own trace and no transaction ID (#369) (REQ-55, Reading a chain).

    Not built in demo v0.9.0¶

    Demo v0.9.0 does not have these items:

    • An authenticated callback, and the binding of the disclosure to the source query (#133, REQ-45).
    • A PID trust list with PID-provider anchors only.
    • The BSN out of the PDP input (#368, ADR-0043, proposed).
    • Validity and revocation per type, set by the bronhouder, with revocation on instruction or on a change in the source (REQ-77, AV-12, AV-13).
    • Nested claims (REQ-78), and traceability of the mapping version per attestation (REQ-124).
    • The relation as filter arguments, and its marking in the source description (#425, REQ-57).

    • The regulatory frame for PuB-EAA issuance (F-81, Q-28). This frame has these parts:

      • Designation.
      • A registration certificate.
      • A qualified seal in a QSCD.
      • Conformity with ETSI TS 119 471 and TS 119 472-3.

      The trust list for PuB-EAA providers is open (Q-30). Key custody is open (Q-17).

    • A second initiation route next to the QR code in the developer portal.

    • Cross-route items from the ASI work (ASI verification):
      • The BRP document also publishes the asi capability. An error in asi refuses the whole source, and this includes its EUDI issuance (#592, source-onboarding.md#L400-L401).
      • The issuance server also issues the test statement of the reference QTSP. That use case runs only in the local stack. A deployment in the simulation environment is #594.
      • #595 (BSN in the ASI token) and #596 (same-device wallet login on a phone) concern only the ASI route.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-44, REQ-45, REQ-46, REQ-55, REQ-57, REQ-58, REQ-60, REQ-64, REQ-65, REQ-66, REQ-72, REQ-74, REQ-77, REQ-78, REQ-97, REQ-116, REQ-124, AV-10, AV-12, AV-13
    • Findings: F-47 (open), F-54 (open), F-57 (open), F-70 (open), F-74 (open), F-81 (open), F-82 (open), F-83 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-14, Q-17, Q-18, Q-28, Q-30
    • Demo increments: SL-19, SL-25, SL-26, SL-31, SL-33, SL-39, SL-40, SL-43, SL-46, SL-48, SL-49

    ASI verification: a QTSP verifies or retrieves an attribute¶

    A qualified trust service provider (QTSP) asks the Authentic Source Interface Provider (ASIP) to verify or retrieve attributes of a citizen at the authentic source. This exchange follows eIDAS Article 45e and ETSI TS 119 478, clause 6.1 (ADR-0037, GO: ASI provider). The citizen approves each request by logging in at the authorization server of the ASIP.

    The ASI route in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has four runs:

    1. Discovery and registration
    2. Authorization and login
    3. Verify through the chain
    4. Test statement to the wallet

    For the concepts, see these pages:

    • The components and the trust boundary: Level 2: ASI chain.
    • The profile per ETSI clause: ASI requirements.
    • The trust roles: ASI trust roles.
    • The source description: The asi capability.
    • What is real, stub, or interpretation in the demo: docs/asi-route.md.

    The demo runs one data service, brp, for the authentic source rvig (BRP mock). Its base URL is /brp/authsrc-api (ADR-0038, dataservices.json). The QTSP is the reference QTSP of the demo. It is not a real QTSP. The route runs only in the local stack (make demo-asi).

    Discovery and registration¶

    A QTSP finds the data service for an attribute without addresses in its configuration (REQ-99, REQ-100). The QTSP registers once per authorization server (REQ-88).

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) External roles participant Q as QTSP<br/>(qtsp-reference) participant DIP as Discover Interface<br/>(asi-discovery-stub) end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant ASIP as ASIP<br/>(asi-provider) participant AS as Authorization server<br/>(asi-authorization-server) end box rgb(237,233,254) Register participant REG as Register of relying parties<br/>(stub file) end Q->>DIP: GET /retrieve, queryType dataServices,<br/>attributeIdentifier, conformsTo DIP->>ASIP: GET /brp/dataservices ASIP-->>DIP: dataService records of the active description DIP-->>Q: Records: endpointURI, endpointDescription,<br/>provider, country Q->>Q: One data service for all attributes? Q->>ASIP: GET /brp/openapi.json ASIP-->>Q: Contract: servers, x-oauth-authorization-server Q->>AS: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server AS-->>Q: Metadata: issuer, endpoints, jwks_uri Q->>Q: Metadata URL belongs to the issuer? Q->>AS: POST /register: redirect_uris, scope,<br/>software_statement with x5c and registryURI AS->>AS: Chain to a trust anchor, certificate valid,<br/>organizationIdentifier, iss, iat, exp AS->>REG: Look up registryURI REG-->>AS: Identifiers, entitlements, legal name AS-->>Q: 201: client_id, jwks with the certificate key Note over AS,REG: Every hour, for each registered client AS->>REG: Look up registryURI again AS->>AS: No QEAA_Provider: deactivate.<br/>Register unreachable: keep active.

    Each hop of discovery and registration carries the following data:

    # From → To Data Notes
    1 to 4 QTSP → Discover Interface → ASIP In: an attribute identifier. Out: one record per attribute and data service No personal data travels. The stub holds no records. It reads them per query from the ASIP and checks them against the ETSI schema (directory.go#L35-L40). The ASIP lists the attributes of the active source description. If no description is active, the ASIP answers 503 (handler.go#L139-L165).
    5 QTSP (internal) The records A token is for one data service. If no data service provides all attributes, the QTSP stops before the authorization server (qtsp.go#L124-L162, F-89).
    6 to 7 QTSP → ASIP The contract (ETSI Annex B OpenAPI) servers must equal the endpointURI. x-oauth-authorization-server is a GBO extension: ETSI requires the reference but gives no field (F-91, Q-39, E1).
    8 to 10 QTSP → authorization server RFC 8414 metadata The QTSP checks that the metadata URL is the RFC 8414 location for the issuer (qtsp.go#L190-L214).
    11 to 12 QTSP → authorization server RFC 7591 request with a software statement, sealed with the QTSP certificate (x5c, registryURI) No personal data travels. The certificate must chain to a trust anchor and carry an organizationIdentifier. In the demo, the certificate comes from the development reader CA. It is not an access certificate per ETSI TS 119 411-8 (F-85).
    13 to 15 Authorization server ↔ register registryURI. Out: identifiers, entitlements, legal name The entry must carry QEAA_Provider and the organizationIdentifier of the certificate (registration.go#L199-L215). It is open which identifier links the two (Q-35). The client key is the certificate key. The authorization server keeps clients in memory.
    16 to 17 Authorization server ↔ register The same lookup The re-check runs every AZSP_ENTITLEMENT_RECHECK_INTERVAL (1 h) (REQ-89, registration.go#L221-L245). If the register is unreachable, the client stays active (Q-34). Tokens already issued stay valid (Q-41).

    Authorization and login¶

    The citizen starts at the QTSP and logs in there first. The QTSP then sends the browser to the authorization server. One request page shows who asks what at which source (REQ-91). The citizen approves by logging in, or refuses (REQ-90). The diagram shows three alternatives: the cross-device wallet login, the DigiD mock, and a refusal.

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor C as Citizen<br/>(browser) end box rgb(241,239,232) QTSP participant Q as QTSP end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant AS as Authorization server participant V as Wallet verifier<br/>(nl-wallet) end box rgb(241,239,232) Wallet participant W as NL Wallet<br/>(phone) end C->>Q: Log in at the QTSP: NL Wallet without BSN,<br/>or test data C->>Q: POST /start: product and values Q-->>C: 302 to /authorize: code, PKCE S256, state,<br/>scope, resource, authorization_details C->>AS: GET /authorize AS-->>C: Request page and transaction cookie C->>AS: POST /authorize/decision alt NL Wallet, cross-device AS->>V: POST /disclosure/sessions: asi-login,<br/>PID with five claims V-->>AS: session_token, kept with the transaction AS-->>C: Wallet page with QR code, refreshes itself W->>V: Fetch the request, signed with the<br/>reader certificate of asi-login W->>V: Presentation: PID as SD-JWT VC V->>V: Issuer signature, trusted issuer,<br/>wallet binding C->>AS: GET /authorize/wallet: status DONE AS->>V: GET disclosed attributes, API key V-->>AS: bsn, family_name, given_name,<br/>birthdate, nationalities else DigiD mock AS-->>C: DigiD mock page C->>AS: POST /authorize/digid: BSN as password else Refuse AS-->>C: 302 to redirect_uri: error access_denied end AS-->>C: 302 to redirect_uri: code and state C->>Q: GET /callback: code, state Q->>AS: POST /token: code, code_verifier,<br/>client_assertion, DPoP proof AS-->>Q: Access token, at+jwt, 10 min

    Each hop of authorization and login carries the following data:

    # From → To Data Notes
    1 Citizen → QTSP name, birth date, nationalities (no BSN) The QTSP uses use case qtsp-login on the same verifier, with its own reader certificate. This shared verifier is a demo shortcut. The test-data login is a stub. The QTSP keeps the login in memory for 30 minutes.
    2 to 3 Citizen → QTSP → browser The product and the values to check (address) The redirect carries PKCE S256, state, the operation as scope, resource = the endpointURI, and authorization_details with the attribute identifiers (REQ-103, ADR-0042). The values stay at the QTSP.
    4 to 5 Browser → authorization server The authorization request. Out: the request page If resource does not name exactly one data service, the answer is invalid_target (REQ-95). The page names the QTSP by its legal name from the register, the operation, the source, and the attributes. The transaction lives 5 minutes and is used once. A cookie binds the transaction to the browser.
    6 Browser → authorization server The choice: wallet, digid, or deny The choice of a means starts the approval. The code comes only after a successful login.
    7 to 9 Authorization server → verifier → browser DCQL: urn:eudi:pid:nl:1 with bsn, family_name, given_name, birthdate, nationalities The authorization server keeps the session with the transaction and never takes one from the browser (provision.go#L33-L49).
    10 to 12 Wallet ↔ verifier PID with the BSN The reader certificate names the authorization server. It does not name the QTSP. Any phone can scan the QR code (F-93). The verifier verifies the issuer signature, the trusted issuer, and the wallet binding. The trusted issuers come from a fixed list. They do not come from a trusted list (REQ-102, Q-36).
    13 to 15 Authorization server ↔ verifier BSN, names, birth date, nationalities Only a PID of the right type with a BSN identifies the citizen. The NL PID has no place of birth (F-94).
    16 to 17 Browser → DigiD mock BSN The DigiD mock is a stub. It checks only for nine digits and gives only the BSN (F-88).
    18 Authorization server → browser error=access_denied No login takes place, and the source gets no request.
    19 to 20 Browser → QTSP code, state The code is single use and valid for 60 s. Before the QTSP asks for a token, it checks its session and state.
    21 QTSP → authorization server POST /token: code, code_verifier, private_key_jwt client assertion, DPoP proof From each pair of mechanisms that ETSI offers, the demo uses one: private_key_jwt and DPoP. The demo uses no mTLS and no PAR (F-84, Q-66).
    22 Authorization server → QTSP RFC 9068 access token, ES256: aud = data service, scope, authorization_details, cnf.jkt, opaque sub, BSN claim, acr/amr, PID claims (wallet only) The QTSP can read the BSN in the token (F-86, E7, #595). The token carries the means used (REQ-86, tokens.go#L53-L85).

    Same-device wallet login¶

    If the browser and the wallet are on one phone, a button opens the wallet. The wallet returns the browser with a nonce (#548, PR #573). This flow needs an HTTPS issuer, because nl-wallet accepts only an HTTPS return URL. Over local HTTP, the button is disabled, and only the QR code works. A run on a real phone waits for the simulation environment (#596, #594).

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor C as Citizen<br/>(browser on the phone) end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant AS as Authorization server participant V as Wallet verifier end box rgb(241,239,232) Wallet participant W as NL Wallet<br/>(same phone) end C->>AS: POST /authorize/decision: wallet AS->>V: POST /disclosure/sessions with a return<br/>template to /authorize/wallet/return V-->>AS: session_token, kept with the transaction AS-->>C: Button Open NL Wallet and QR code C->>W: Universal link opens the wallet W->>V: Fetch the request, presentation W-->>C: Back to the website: return URL with nonce C->>AS: GET /authorize/wallet/return:<br/>transaction, session_token, nonce AS->>AS: Session of this transaction<br/>in this browser? AS->>V: GET disclosed attributes with the nonce V-->>AS: PID, only for the right nonce AS-->>C: 302 to redirect_uri: code and state

    These hops carry the data that is specific to the same-device login:

    # From → To Data Notes
    2 Authorization server → verifier The return template The verifier returns only after a same-device session (session_type_return_url = "same_device", only for asi-login).
    7 to 9 Wallet → browser → authorization server transaction, session_token, nonce The authorization server refuses another browser or another session before it calls the verifier. The browser also comes back after a refusal in the wallet (identification.go#L322-L356).
    10 to 11 Authorization server ↔ verifier nonce. Out: PID with the BSN The nonce binds the disclosure to the browser that the wallet returned. Another phone cannot finish this session (F-93).

    Verify through the chain¶

    The QTSP calls the ASIP with the token. The ASIP verifies the token, takes the BSN from it, and calls the source once, through its own FSC Outway. The generic GBO chain starts behind the ASIP (F-87).

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) QTSP participant Q as QTSP end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant ASIP as ASIP<br/>(data service brp) participant AS as Authorization server end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant OW as asip-outway<br/>(peer …1200) participant IW as bd-inway<br/>(PEP, peer …0200) participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP<br/>(ASI0001) participant GW as Source gateway<br/>(brp-sidecar) end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant SRC as BRP mock<br/>(brp-graphql-server) end Q->>ASIP: POST /brp/authsrc-api/verify: DPoP token,<br/>DPoP proof, traceparent, attributes ASIP->>AS: Metadata and JWKS, once, cached AS-->>ASIP: Signing keys ASIP->>ASIP: Token, proof and scope.<br/>BSN from the token. ASIP->>ASIP: Contract schema, approved attributes,<br/>mandate, attributes described ASIP->>ASIP: One query from the active<br/>description, only the needed fields ASIP->>OW: POST /brp/graphql: query, BSN as variable,<br/>Fsc-Transaction-Id, traceparent OW->>IW: mTLS, Fsc-Authorization, same body IW->>PDP: POST /authzen/v1/evaluation with the body PDP-->>IW: Allow per field, ADL record IW->>GW: Query GW->>SRC: Query unchanged, no consent token SRC-->>ASIP: Fields of the person, or no person ASIP->>ASIP: Build the attributes and compare ASIP-->>Q: 200: attributeVerificationResults,<br/>X-JWS-Signature Q->>Q: Seal valid? Else not accepted.

    Each hop of the verification carries the following data:

    # From → To Data Notes
    1 QTSP → ASIP Authorization: DPoP <token>, DPoP proof with ath, attribute values to check The values are personal data that the QTSP already has. insufficient_scope and every other token error give 401, as ETSI lists.
    2 to 3 ASIP → authorization server jwks_uri from the metadata If the kid is unknown, the ASIP fetches the keys again. If the keys are not available, the ASIP answers 503 (REQ-87).
    4 ASIP (internal) Token, proof. Out: the BSN The ASIP first verifies the token: signature, issuer, aud, expiry, DPoP binding and replay, and scope (handler.go#L222-L258). The BSN comes only from the token. No log line holds the BSN.
    5 ASIP (internal) The request Schema against the contract: 400. Attributes outside authorization_details: 401. mandate: 501. An attribute the source does not describe: 404 (handler.go#L260-L356, service.go#L129-L139).
    6 ASIP (internal) The asi description from the active release The ASIP reads the active release every 5 s with the reader role. It derives one query with only the fields of the requested attributes (REQ-92, ADR-0039).
    7 ASIP → asip-outway POST /brp/graphql (grant link /brp): {query, variables: {bsn}} with the BSN, Fsc-Transaction-Id, traceparent One FSC transaction per request. The span names the source, the transaction ID and the attribute identifiers, never the BSN or a value (source.go#L75-L104, REQ-55).
    8 asip-outway → bd-inway FSC, mTLS, with the body and the BSN The hop uses the contract of the ASIP peer …1200 for service brp on …0200 (FSC peers).
    9 to 10 bd-inway ↔ PDP AuthZEN: actor …1200, service brp, the query with the BSN ASI0001 grants the ASIP peer the BRP fields behind the attributes, on brp only. It does not check the token or the QTSP (asi0001.rego#L1-L72, REQ-97). The PDP never sees the QTSP or the citizen. The ADL holds the BSN (REQ-60, ADR-0043).
    11 to 12 bd-inway → gateway → BRP mock The judged query If the query has no consent token, the gateway passes it through. The BRP logs its own processing. In demo v0.9.0, the ASIP writes no LDV records.
    13 BRP mock → ASIP fields of the person, or null The answer goes back through the same FSC chain.
    14 ASIP (internal) Fields. Out: a result per attribute pointer, join, const, and each build the attribute from the fields. The result is Match, MatchWithVariation, NoMatch, or Unknown. Unknown means only that the source holds no value (REQ-84). Fuzzy matching applies only to strings without a format (REQ-113).
    15 ASIP → QTSP results, provider, authenticSource (legal name from the description), header X-JWS-Signature A verify response holds no source value (REQ-85). One authentic source per response (REQ-94). The seal is a detached JWS, ES256, with x5c, over the exact body. The ASIP does not seal errors (REQ-83, ADR-0041, handler.go#L402-L417).
    16 QTSP (internal) The seal The chain must lead to QTSP_SEAL_TRUST_ANCHORS. If it does not, the QTSP does not accept the result.

    The retrieve operation runs the same way at POST /brp/authsrc-api/retrieve with scope retrieve. The request names attribute identifiers, without values. The sealed 200 carries the values of every requested attribute. If the source holds no value for one of them, the answer is 404. Retrieve gives no partial result (REQ-101).

    Test statement to the wallet¶

    After an accepted result, the reference QTSP issues a test statement to the wallet of the citizen who logged in at the QTSP. The QTSP uses the central issuance server of the EUDI route, with its own use case and its own certificates (qtsp_issuance.go#L19-L27, EUDI issuance).

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor C as Citizen<br/>(browser) end box rgb(241,239,232) QTSP participant Q as QTSP end box rgb(255,237,213) EUDI participant IS as Issuance server<br/>(nl-wallet) end box rgb(241,239,232) Wallet participant W as NL Wallet<br/>(phone) end Q->>Q: Accepted result: pending statement<br/>with the login identity Q-->>C: Result page with a QR code<br/>for use case qtsp-attestation W->>IS: Fetch the request, signed with<br/>the reader certificate of the QTSP W->>IS: PID: family_name, given_name,<br/>birthdate, nationalities, no BSN IS->>Q: Callback over internal HTTPS,<br/>secret path, the shared attributes Q->>Q: Same as the login identity? Q-->>IS: Statement: subject, outcome per attribute,<br/>source, date, test and not qualified IS-->>W: SD-JWT VC over OpenID4VCI, signed<br/>with the issuer certificate of the QTSP

    Each hop of the test statement carries the following data:

    # From → To Data Notes
    1 to 2 QTSP → browser The result and a fixed link per use case This hop occurs only after Match, MatchWithVariation, or a retrieved value. The pending statement lives 10 minutes in memory and is used once. A later request of the same citizen replaces it.
    3 to 4 Wallet → issuance server PID without the BSN A QTSP is not allowed to process the BSN.
    5 Issuance server → QTSP name, birth date, nationalities The QTSP gets no session, only the shared attributes. The callback uses a secret path over CA-pinned HTTPS, without client authentication (qtsp_issuance.go#L134-L152).
    6 QTSP (internal) The identity The link to the login uses only these personal data. This link is a demo binding and does not check a unique identity (F-93).
    7 to 8 QTSP → issuance server → wallet statement The statement is valid for 30 days, has attestation_qualification = "EAA", and carries a clear test marking. It is not a QEAA. For MatchWithVariation, the statement records the value that the QTSP sent. It does not record a source value.

    Error paths¶

    The ASI route has the following error paths:

    Trigger Outcome Pinned by (v0.9.0)
    No data service provides all requested attributes The QTSP stops before the authorization server. Request API: 422. api_e2e_test.go#L201
    No active source description Records, verify, and retrieve answer 503. The contract stays published. source_test.go#L168, graphqlsource/source_test.go#L148
    Software statement invalid: signature, chain, expiry, or no organizationIdentifier invalid_software_statement registration_test.go#L105
    No QEAA_Provider, or the identifier is not in the register entry unapproved_software_statement (REQ-88) registration_test.go#L152
    Register unreachable at registration 503 temporarily_unavailable registration_test.go#L324
    Entitlement withdrawn in the register The next re-check deactivates the client: invalid_client. Issued tokens stay valid for up to 10 min (Q-41). registration_test.go#L224, #L276
    Register unreachable at re-check The client stays active (demo choice, Q-34) registration_test.go#L306
    Unknown client or redirect_uri Error page, no redirect handler_test.go#L211
    resource missing or not exactly one data service invalid_target (REQ-95) handler_test.go#L153
    The citizen refuses access_denied, without login login_test.go#L61
    DigiD mock: BSN is not nine digits The page stays open with an error login_test.go#L110
    Wallet declines or the session expires Back to the request page. The transaction stays. wallet_test.go#L205
    Verifier unreachable, also after DONE 503 page. The transaction stays for the DigiD mock. wallet_test.go#L299
    Same-device return in another browser or for another session Refused before the authorization server calls the verifier wallet_test.go#L123, #L148
    Same-device return without the right nonce Back to the request page with a message wallet_test.go#L177
    Wrong code_verifier, or a code that is used twice, expired, or of another client invalid_grant handler_test.go#L239, #L246
    Client assertion missing, wrong, or replayed invalid_client handler_test.go#L293, #L347
    No valid DPoP proof at the token endpoint invalid_dpop_proof handler_test.go#L374
    No token, an invalid token, or a DPoP proof that is missing, invalid, or replayed 401 with WWW-Authenticate: DPoP token_test.go#L46-L216
    Scope does not cover the operation 401 insufficient_scope token_test.go#L217
    Attribute outside the approved authorization_details 401 insufficient_scope (REQ-103) token_test.go#L233
    Token for another data service 401 (REQ-95) dataservices_test.go#L16
    Keys of the authorization server not available 503 token_test.go#L289
    Body not valid against the contract 400, after the token check and before other checks handler_test.go#L220, token_test.go#L262
    mandate present 501 (REQ-114) handler_test.go#L186, #L194
    Attribute the source does not describe, also one of another data service 404. The ASIP does not call the source. handler_test.go#L151, #L157
    Source holds no value, or the BSN is unknown to the source Unknown (REQ-84) handler_test.go#L140, token_test.go#L254
    Retrieve, and the source holds no value for one attribute 404, no partial result (REQ-101) handler_test.go#L291
    Chain unreachable, or the Outway answers 5xx 503, never Unknown (REQ-93) graphqlsource/source_test.go#L157, source_test.go#L141
    PDP deny (the Inway answers 401), GraphQL errors, or an answer of another shape 500, never Unknown The same tests
    PDP: the caller is not the ASIP peer ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED asi0001_test.rego#L29
    PDP: a consent token, or no BSN in the root argument PID_NOT_PRESENT asi0001_test.rego#L37-L49
    PDP: another service than brp, or another BRP field Rule not bound, or the field falls to the closed world asi0001_test.rego#L56-L61
    Seal from an unknown anchor The QTSP does not accept the result e2e_test.go#L285
    Test statement: NoMatch or Unknown No pending statement issuance_test.go#L97
    Test statement: another PID, or a statement that is expired or used Empty document list, nothing issued issuance_test.go#L53, callback_test.go#L38

    The conformance matrix gives each ETSI requirement ID a status and named tests. At v0.9.0, the matrix has 55 passed, 4 stub, 21 not applicable, and 1 failing. If an ID or a test is missing, a CI job fails (etsi-ts-119478.yaml, ci.yml#L72-L73).

    Main observations¶

    The ASI route in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

    • The QTSP is outside FSC. Its admission is a certificate and a register entitlement at the authorization server. The source and the PDP see only the ASIP peer …1200. The ASIP passes nothing about the QTSP into the chain (F-87, Trust boundary).
    • Two logins, no link. The citizen logs in at the QTSP and at the authorization server. Nothing proves that it is the same person. In the cross-device route, another phone can scan the QR code (F-93, Q-40, E6).
    • The BSN travels in two places where it is not needed. The QTSP can read the BSN in the token (F-86, #595). The PDP input and the ADL also hold the BSN (REQ-60, ADR-0043).
    • The wallet may not show why. The wallet shows the authorization server as relying party. Until wallets must validate the registration certificate, the request page alone tells the citizen who asks what and why (F-99).
    • Approval is a login, not a consent. The citizen approves one request. The demo stores no approval, and the citizen cannot revoke one (REQ-90, Wallet approval is not a legal basis).
    • One token per source. A QTSP that needs attributes of two sources authorizes twice. The citizen sees each source by name (ADR-0038, F-89, E3).
    • Per-attribute binding is optional. If the request has no authorization_details, the token binds only per operation, as in ETSI. A configuration option makes the detail required (ADR-0042, F-95, Q-33).
    • No value with a variation. MatchWithVariation returns no value. The conformance matrix records that row as failing (F-92, Q-29, E2).
    • The seal format is a GBO choice. ETSI defines no seal format (Q-32, E4). The demo seals with a development certificate.
    • Identification data is incomplete. The NL PID has no place of birth. The DigiD mock gives only the BSN (F-88, F-94, Q-36).

    Not built in demo v0.9.0¶

    Demo v0.9.0 does not build these parts of the ASI route:

    • A resource list from the source descriptions. The authorization server takes its resource list from AZSP_RESOURCES. The rest of the asi capability is built (#592, Q-38).
    • A deployment in the simulation environment, and a connection of an external QTSP (#594).
    • Protection of the BSN in the access token (#595, F-86).
    • A same-device wallet login on a real phone. It is built and tested, and waits for #594 (#596).
    • iss in the authorization response, RFC 9207 (F-96, E9). The effect of a withdrawn entitlement on issued tokens (Q-41, E10).
    • LDV records by the ASIP and the authorization server (REQ-72).
    • Clause 6.2 (ISO 15000) and deferred answers (REQ-112, Q-64). Requests on behalf of another person (Q-65).
    • A production register, access certificates per ETSI TS 119 411-8, real DigiD, and a qualified seal certificate (F-80, F-85, Q-28, Q-37).
    • Registration of the data services in the Discover Interface (Q-31, Q-67).
