    Admission and activation¶

    Two management-plane scenarios come before the first request:

    1. Contract admission: a party asks for an FSC contract. The FSC Manager of the provider asks the PDP whether that party is admitted.
    2. Source activation: the operator of a GBO component takes a source into use. The component fetches the service description of the source, validates it, and activates it as an immutable release.

    Both scenarios carry no citizen data. They share one principle: a valid contract is necessary, but it is not enough. Admission comes from a register and does not follow from the contract (REQ-61). Activation is an explicit management action and does not follow from the contract either (REQ-65).

    For the concepts, see Authorization: admission and contract acceptance and Source onboarding. The decisions are ADR-0015 and ADR-0016.

    Scenario 1: contract admission¶

    A consumer, an integrator, or a GBO component (the issuance facility, the ASIP, the PDP itself) wants to connect to an FSC service of a bronhouder. The party creates a contract proposal in its own FSC Manager. The FSC Manager of the provider does not sign on a flag. It sends every proposal to the OpenFTV PDP as an AuthZEN evaluation and signs only on allow (fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml#L701-L702). The FSC Managers of the BRP peer and the consent register (toestemmingsregister) peer use the same policy (#L892-L893, #L1079-L1080).

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Administrator actor ADM as Register administrator end box rgb(237,233,254) Admission register participant REG as Admission register<br/>(dvtp-onboarding-register) end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP<br/>(autosign.rego) participant CM as FSC Manager<br/>of the consumer participant PM as FSC Manager<br/>of the provider end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant ADL as ADL<br/>(postgres-ftv) end ADM->>REG: Admit party: Peer ID, name, active, admitted sources loop Every 5 s (PIP pull) PDP->>REG: GET /internal/openftv/participants REG-->>PDP: Participants with acts_for end CM->>CM: POST /v1/contracts (grant), signed by the consumer CM->>PM: Contract proposal (FSC, mTLS) PM->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation<br/>context.doelbinding = auto_sign_contract PDP->>PDP: Eight ordered checks on the register data PDP->>ADL: Decision record alt Allow PDP-->>PM: decision true, rule FSC_AUTOSIGN_ADMITTED_PARTY PM->>PM: Countersign PM-->>CM: Signature: the contract becomes valid else Deny PDP-->>PM: decision false, reason_admin.code Note over PM: The proposal stays proposed.<br/>No signature, no rejection. end

    Data per hop¶

    Each hop of contract admission carries the following data:

    # From → to Interface Data Notes
    1 Administrator → register Register UI (localhost:9415), CSRF-protected forms FSC Peer ID (20 characters), display name, active, Peer IDs of the admitted bronhouders The register has no accounts. Anyone who reaches the UI locally is administrator (README). Integrations (acts_for) and technical participants are part of the deployment configuration. The UI does not manage them
    2 to 3 PDP → register GET /internal/openftv/participants (handler.go#L63), interval 5 s, timeout 2 s data.entities.dvtp_participant, keyed by Peer ID: name, active, allowed_source_peer_ids, acts_for (dvtp-onboarding.yaml) The pull uses a network that only the register and the PDP share. Every entry carries acts_for. If the party acts for nobody, acts_for is empty. As a result, a withdrawn mandate replaces the old entity
    4 Consumer → own FSC Manager POST /v1/contracts, internal API, mTLS (seed-bri-connection-hv.sh#L113-L135) Contract content: grant (type and service), validity, the peers FSC grants carry no properties (ADR-0031)
    5 Consumer Manager → provider Manager FSC Manager interface, mTLS with the organization certificate (demo CA) Signed contract proposal The contract hash identifies the proposal. A new submission is a new proposal with a new hash
    6 Provider Manager → PDP AuthZEN, https://openftv-pdp:8443/authzen/v1, the Manager pins the PDP CA subject (self_peer_id, peer_ids), action autosign_contract, resource (contract hash, grant_types), context.doelbinding = auto_sign_contract (autosign.rego#L12-L15) The input has no service name and no delegation direction. The PDP judges who connects. It does not judge to which service (F-56)
    7 to 8 PDP Package doelbinding.auto_sign_contract, separate from the request policy (REQ-62) Decision record in the ADL, next to the request decisions The purpose limitation (doelbinding) selects the package. A renamed package resolves to nothing (autosign.rego#L8-L10)
    9 to 11 PDP → provider Manager → consumer Manager AuthZEN response, then FSC signature Allow: FSC_AUTOSIGN_ADMITTED_PARTY, counterparties, source Peer ID. Deny: first failing code, counterparties, grant types (autosign.rego#L184-L202) The response holds only Peer IDs and no personal data

    Ordered refusal codes¶

    The policy runs eight checks in a fixed order. The first check that fails names the refusal (autosign.rego#L165-L175). Each check defaults to false, so malformed input leads to a refusal instead of an undefined check. The policy refuses a contract for one of eight reasons, in this order:

    # Code Refuses when Tests (v0.9.0)
    1 NOT_AN_AUTOSIGN_REQUEST The action is not autosign_contract, the resource is not a contract, or attributes are missing autosign_test.rego#L223, #L230, #L239
    2 GRANT_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED The grants are not all type 2 (service connection) and not all type 3 (delegated service connection): a publication, a mix, or no grant #L149, #L205, #L209, #L213
    3 NO_COUNTERPARTY The contract names no party other than the provider #L219
    4 ADMISSION_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE The PIP pull supplied no register #L86, #L91
    5 PARTY_NOT_IN_REGISTRY A counterparty is not in the register. This also applies when the register is empty #L130, #L96, #L190
    6 PARTY_NOT_ACTIVE A counterparty is suspended (active is not true) #L138, #L185, #L195
    7 SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED A counterparty is not admitted for the Peer ID of this source #L109, #L113
    8 DELEGATION_NOT_REGISTERED The contract has a delegated grant, but no integration between the two counterparties is registered #L176, #L180, #L201

    The tests #L74, #L117, and #L171 cover the allow paths. If the policy refuses one party among several, it refuses the whole contract (#L143).

    A refusal leaves the proposal at proposed. The party can correct its admission and submit again. The new submission gets a new assessment (REQ-63). This behavior is product behavior of the FSC Manager. No automated test covers it. If a setup configures an automatic refusal, the setup breaks the requirement.

    Delegated grant (integrator)¶

    An integrator connects on behalf of a consumer (the represented party). The integrator uses one contract that holds a delegated service connection grant (type 3). The contract has three signatures (seed-bri-delegation-int.sh#L1-L17):

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis: FSC and PDP participant IM as FSC Manager<br/>of the integrator participant DM as FSC Manager<br/>of the represented party participant PM as FSC Manager<br/>of the provider participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP end IM->>IM: Create contract: delegated grant,<br/>integrator, represented party, service IM->>DM: Contract proposal DM->>DM: Accept (operator action) IM->>PM: Contract proposal PM->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation, grant_types [3] Note over PDP: Checks 1–7 for both counterparties,<br/>then check 8: one acts_for the other PDP-->>PM: Allow, or DELEGATION_NOT_REGISTERED PM-->>IM: Countersignature: contract valid

    Each hop of the delegated grant carries the following data:

    # Data Notes
    1 to 2 Delegated grant with the Peer IDs of the integrator, the represented party, and the provider The FSC Manager of the represented party has no autosign. In the demo, the seed script accepts on its behalf. The script does what the operator does in the Controller UI (#L147-L167)
    4 to 6 peer_ids with the two counterparties, grant_types [3] The integrator must be admitted in its own right. A mandate does not replace the admission of either party

    The contract check admits the pair of counterparties. It does not check the direction (autosign.rego#L119-L139). The input does not say which party delegates. The check refuses a third counterparty. A contract that is signed the wrong way round passes this check, but the request policy denies it on every call.

    At request time, the provider Manager puts the represented party in the act claim of the access token. The engine then requires a mandate for the represented party and for the granting rule (engine.rego#L246-L267, ADR-0034). The engine decides as follows:

    Situation at request time Code Tests (v0.9.0)
    Registered integrator, mandate for the represented party and the rule allow engine_test.rego#L613
    No mandate for the represented party or the rule INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED #L621
    The integrator is suspended INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED #L706
    The register is missing from the PDP data INTEGRATOR_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE in the trace, request code PIP_UNAVAILABLE. The consumer sees ACCESS_DENIED #L631

    The register attaches the mandates to the entry of the integrator (service_test.go#L245). The consent binds the represented party. It does not bind the integrator (REQ-106). For the DvTP query with an integrator, see DvTP query.

    Register missing against register empty¶

    The PDP data can be in two states that look the same but have a different meaning (autosign.rego#L43-L59, PR #579):

    PDP data Meaning Code
    No data.entities, or no dvtp_participant document The PIP pull supplied no register: an outage or a wrong mapping ADMISSION_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE
    dvtp_participant is {} The register is available and admits nobody PARTY_NOT_IN_REGISTRY

    Both states lead to a refusal. The two codes tell the operator whether the pull or the admission needs a repair. The readiness script of the demo waits for the first successful pull before it seeds contracts (wait-openftv-admission.sh).

    The OpenFTV pull adds and replaces entities. If an entity disappears from a later response, the pull does not remove it. For this reason, the register deactivates a participant and never deletes it. A deleted record leaves the old admission in the PDP (REQ-61).

    Main observations¶

    Contract admission in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

    • Admission is register data (F-55). No policy rule holds the admission. Adding, suspending, or withdrawing a party changes register data. The PDP sees the change within one pull interval of 5 s, without a policy change or a restart.
    • Contract and request rules are separate (REQ-62). The two rule sets share no rules and no reason codes. They do share one policy set and one availability object. As a result, one broken module stops both (F-52).
    • A suspended consumer keeps its access. A suspension stops only new contracts. At request time, the policy checks the status of an integrator. It does not check the status of a direct consumer. A suspended consumer with an existing contract can still request data, also with a valid consent (REQ-110, Q-53).
    • Changes are not traceable. The register has no accounts and no change log (REQ-123). The task to run the register is assigned to the management organization (Q-22). It is open who builds the facility (Q-74).
    • The register key is the FSC Peer ID. It is open whether policy can read the Peer ID as the OIN of the consumer (Q-68).

    Scenario 2: source activation¶

    For each source, the issuance facility and the ASIP need to know the data service, the query, the mapping, and the offer. The source publishes that description itself (REQ-64, F-57). The source reconciler of the EUDI adapter fetches the description, validates it, and writes it to the Source Registry. The runtime readers read only activated releases.

    First, the metadata contract and the data contract of the source must be valid. They pass contract admission like every other contract, because the issuance facility is a technical participant in the admission register (toelatingsregister).

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Operator actor OP as Operator end box rgb(237,233,254) Certificates participant CS as Certificate store end box rgb(255,237,213) Issuance facility participant REC as Source reconciler end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis: FSC participant FM as FSC Manager<br/>of the issuance facility participant OUT as FSC Outway<br/>of the issuance facility end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant SRC as Source<br/>(Inway, PDP, /.well-known/gbo) end box rgb(237,233,254) Source Registry participant SR as Source Registry<br/>(PostgreSQL) end box rgb(255,237,213) EUDI channel participant AD as EUDI adapter participant ASIP as ASIP participant ISS as Issuance server end OP->>REC: Add sources/configured/{source_id} OP->>CS: Place the certificate set of source_id REC->>CS: Load the certificate set Note over REC: OIN from serialNumber,<br/>name from O REC->>FM: List contracts (internal API, mTLS) FM-->>REC: Valid grants with grant hashes alt Transport fsc REC->>OUT: GET /.well-known/gbo<br/>Fsc-Grant-Hash, If-None-Match OUT->>SRC: FSC request Note over SRC: PDP rule SOURCE_METADATA_FSC SRC-->>REC: 200 document + ETag, or 304 else Transport file REC->>REC: Read the document from --metadata-dir end REC->>REC: Validate, and bind to the data contract REC->>SR: Write candidate, state rollout_required alt Demo: --auto-promote REC->>SR: Promote: immutable release + active_release_id else Production: explicit promotion OP->>SR: Promote, or activate-source-release --release-id end loop Every 5 s AD->>SR: Read the active release (reader role) AD->>AD: Swap the in-memory snapshot end loop Every 5 s ASIP->>SR: Read the active release (reader role) end OP->>ISS: make eudi-config: write issuance_server.toml, restart

    Data per hop¶

    Each hop of source activation carries the following data:

    # From → to Interface Data Notes
    1 Operator → reconciler One file per source in sources/configured/ (source_configuration.go#L16-L28) source_id (file name), transport per leg, metadata locator, provider_peer_id The file holds no OIN and no organization name. Those values come from the certificate
    2 to 4 Operator → store → reconciler Public certificate store (--certificate-store=public-filesystem) Issuer, reader and status-list leaf certificates of the source The reconciler gets only public leaves. Only the issuance init container gets the private keys (REQ-58)
    5 to 6 Reconciler → FSC Manager Internal Manager API, mTLS (docker-compose.yml#L1846-L1865) Contract snapshot: per provider Peer ID and service, the grant hash A contract without a source file activates nothing
    7 to 9 Reconciler → Outway → source GET /.well-known/gbo with Fsc-Grant-Hash and If-None-Match Source metadata document (gbo-source-metadata-v1, version 1.0 or 1.1), ETag The PDP of the source allows only known peers, on the metadata services, on exactly this path (authz.rego#L14-L36). The document is public and holds no citizen data. A 304 extends only the freshness
    10 Reconciler Validation (service.go#L399-L416) Schema, source_oin against the certificate, version, validity window, one read operation, mapping, offers, claims, the asi capability The data service that the document names must have a valid data contract
    11 Reconciler → registry Writer role Candidate per source, with state The registry refuses private key material
    12 Reconciler or operator → registry One database transaction (store.go#L300-L390) Release (identified by the SHA-256 of its content) and the singleton active_release_id A release never changes. Automatic promotion is off by default (reconcile_command.go#L197). Compose turns it on
    13 to 14 Adapter → registry Reader role, every 5 s (source_release_runtime.go#L59-L63) Source snapshots, Type Metadata, offer catalog The adapter loads the full material only when the release ID changes
    15 ASIP → registry Reader role, ASIP_SOURCE_REGISTRY_REFRESH = 5 s (asi-provider/main.go#L101) Per data service: query, attribute mapping, legal name of the authentic source, discovery records
    16 Operator → issuance server Init container writes issuance_server.toml Offers, disclosure, certificates, trust anchors The issuance server reads its configuration only at start, so a new release needs a controlled restart

    For the document structure, the transports, and the release readers, see Source onboarding.

    Failure per source¶

    A source that fails gets the state stale or blocked. The other sources keep their state (REQ-66). For the reason codes, see service.go#L141-L152. Source activation handles each failure as follows:

    Trigger Result Tests (v0.9.0)
    Valid metadata contract, no source file Nothing is activated fsc_contract_discovery_test.go#L143, #L89
    Certificate set missing That source gets blocked: CERTIFICATE_SET_NOT_FOUND. The reconciler checks this before any network call. The other sources continue #L172, #L278, service_test.go#L130
    Certificate without OIN or organization name blocked: CERTIFICATE_SET_INVALID code (service.go#L283-L297)
    FSC Manager unreachable FSC sources get FSC_MANAGER_UNAVAILABLE, and the candidate stays within grace. Sources without FSC continue service_test.go#L159, #L319, fsc_contract_discovery_test.go#L599
    Source file, no metadata contract blocked: METADATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND #L201
    Fetch fails, previous candidate within grace stale. Issuance continues on the previous version #L549, #L519
    Fetch fails, no candidate, or file missing blocked: METADATA_FETCH_FAILED #L851
    Document invalid: schema error, OIN differs from the certificate, more or less than one read operation, or valid for less than one hour METADATA_INVALID. The last complete candidate stays main_test.go#L628
    asi capability invalid, or a document with only asi The whole source gets METADATA_INVALID asi_onboarding_test.go#L152
    GBO attribute catalogue unreadable Only sources with asi are refused asi_onboarding_test.go#L227
    No contract for the data service in the document DATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND service_test.go#L295
    Lower version, or the same version with other content Not activated none, code only (source_registry_backend.go#L163-L175, #610)
    Registry write fails blocked: ACTIVATION_FAILED code (service.go#L418-L421)
    Promotion fails The previous release stays active store_test.go#L94
    One configured source without a valid version No new release for any source. The active release stays (deviation, #606) registry_test.go#L91
    Operator rolls back to a stored release The stored release becomes active. Automatic promotion keeps the rollback until new content arrives registry_test.go#L116, store_test.go#L147, source_registry_command_test.go#L47
    Rollback to a release the adapter cannot load Refused. The pointer does not change source_registry_command_test.go#L72
    Active version of a source past grace Issuance for that source answers HTTP 503. The offer list /eudi-offers.json answers 503 for all sources (deviation, #606) code only (main.go#L221-L225)
    Adapter refresh fails The previous complete snapshot stays in use source_release_runtime_test.go#L125, #L89
    ASIP reads the release The ASIP reads per data service from the active release asi_onboarding_test.go#L323

    Main observations¶

    Source activation in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

    • A valid contract is not activation (F-58). The source file is the management action. Transport and mandate are two decisions with two owners. Two parts are not built: the rule for who can take the action, and the way GBO records the admission decision. These parts are PSA B-09 in the decision register and REQ-123.
    • The source owns its description (F-57). GBO validates and activates the description. Its origin is the authenticated FSC transport plus the OIN from the certificate. The document itself has no signature. The file transport is a visible, temporary exception for a source without an endpoint. The demo does not record the agreement of the bronhouder (F-71, AV-08).
    • Releases have a full lifecycle (F-59). The lifecycle has validation before activation, bounded staleness, atomic promotion, and rollback. Policy bundles do not have this lifecycle. For a comparison, see Policy distribution.
    • Isolation is incomplete. One failing source freezes new releases for all sources, and the offer list fails for all sources at the same time (#606).
    • DvTP is not covered. For DvTP, the GBO rules hold the offer of a source. A publication of the source does not hold it (REQ-64). The question of how a source connects to the ASIP is partly answered (Q-38).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-61, REQ-62, REQ-63, REQ-110, REQ-123, REQ-106, REQ-64, REQ-65, REQ-66, REQ-58, AV-06, AV-08
    • Findings: F-55 (closed), F-56 (closed), F-52 (open), F-73 (closed), F-57 (open), F-58 (closed), F-59 (closed), F-71 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-22 (answered), Q-53 (open), Q-68 (open), Q-74 (open), Q-38 (partly answered)
    • Demo increments: SL-45 (done), SL-46 (done), SL-09 (partly covered)

    Policy distribution¶

    Policy distribution is a management-plane scenario. Policy travels in this scenario, and no citizen data travels. The management plane decides who changes the rules. The decision plane decides who gets which data. The two planes are separate (F-51).

    The scenario takes place at the bronhouder. The PDP is behind the FSC Inway of the bronhouder, and the OpenFTV Manager serves exactly that PDP. Policy management stays with each bronhouder (Q-21, ADR-0021). In the demo, everything runs in one compose stack. This setup is a demo artifact and makes no statement about the architecture.

    For the concept, see Policy lifecycle.

    Two components have the name Manager. The OpenFTV Manager manages policy (PAP). The FSC Manager manages contracts and issues access tokens. This page covers only the OpenFTV Manager.

    Two modes¶

    The PDP gets its policy in one of two modes:

    Mode Where the PDP gets its policy Started by
    Mount (default) The PDP image carries policies/ (Dockerfile#L62-L67). Compose bind-mounts ./policies over that copy (docker-compose.yml#L157). The PDP hot-reloads at each edit every make demo* target
    Bundle (opt-in) The PDP pulls bundle gbo-pdp from the OpenFTV Manager at start, because PDP_BUNDLE_MANAGER is set (docker-compose.yml#L145-L149) make demo-manager, then make manager-seed after each change (Makefile#L151-L177)

    The demo runs OpenFTV release v0.1.0. The PDP builds from the tag with the FTV GraphQL mapper patched in. The Manager and its management interface are the published v0.1.0 images (docker-compose.yml#L245). If the three versions differ, or if the version is not a release tag, CI fails (ci.yml#L355-L373).

    Scenario 1: mount mode (default)¶

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Author actor DEV as Policy author end box rgb(237,233,254) Version control participant GIT as policies/ in version control end box rgb(241,239,232) Build participant MK as make policy-check end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant ADL as ADL (postgres-ftv) end DEV->>GIT: Edit a .rego file DEV->>MK: Any make target that starts the PDP MK->>GIT: Refuse non-Rego files and duplicate file names MK->>MK: opa check policies MK-->>DEV: Pass, or stop before the PDP starts PDP->>GIT: Load /policies (bind mount), recursive Note over PDP: Hot reload on every edit PDP->>ADL: Decision records

    Each hop in mount mode carries the following data:

    # From → to Data Notes
    1 Author → version control Rego source with tests next to the rules Version control is the source of the content
    2 to 5 make → policies/ File list, compile result policy-check runs before every target that starts the PDP (Makefile#L92-L106). make policy-test adds opa fmt --diff and opa test (#L115-L117)
    6 to 7 PDP → mount Every file under /policies as a Rego module (PDP_POLICIES_LANGUAGE=rego, PDP_POLICIES_STORE_RECURSE=true) The reload log line policy added/replaced does not prove that the new rules decide (#151)
    8 PDP → ADL Decision records The PDP does not start without the ADL database (docker-compose.yml#L117-L125)

    Scenario 2: bundle mode (OpenFTV Manager)¶

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(237,233,254) Version control participant GIT as policies/ in version control end box rgb(241,239,232) Deployment participant SEED as seed-openftv-manager.py<br/>(deployment identity) participant IDP as Keycloak (realm gbo) end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant MGR as OpenFTV Manager v0.1.0<br/>(PAP) participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP v0.1.0 end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant PG as postgres-ftv<br/>(ftv_manager, ftv_adl) end SEED->>IDP: POST /protocol/openid-connect/token<br/>(password grant, user deployment) IDP-->>SEED: Access token, role admin (30 min) SEED->>GIT: Read policies/**/*.rego (not *_test.rego) SEED->>MGR: POST or PUT /v1/policy/{uuid5(path)}<br/>tag gbo-authz, Bearer token MGR->>MGR: Cedar: may this principal write? MGR->>PG: Store the policy and the audit trail SEED->>MGR: GET /v1/policies: which policy left version control? SEED->>MGR: PUT /v1/policy/{id}, tag gbo-retired Note over SEED,PDP: make demo-manager and make manager-seed restart the PDP PDP->>MGR: GET /v1/bundle/gbo-pdp (internal port 9443) MGR->>MGR: Cedar: pdp-bundle.cedar permits GET on this path MGR-->>PDP: Gzipped bundle {version, policies with tag gbo-authz, data} PDP->>PDP: Compile the whole set and activate it PDP->>PG: Decision records to the ADL (ftv_adl)

    Data per hop¶

    Each hop in bundle mode carries the following data:

    # From → to Interface Data Notes
    1 to 2 Seed → Keycloak POST /realms/gbo/protocol/openid-connect/token (seed-openftv-manager.py#L83-L113) Client openftv-manager-ui, user deployment, password from FTV_MANAGER_DEPLOY_PASSWORD Publishing token: non-personal deployment identity, role admin, token lifespan 1800 s, and no long-lived API key (RL-03)
    3 Seed → version control File system policies/**/*.rego without tests, repo-relative path Version control is canonical for the content. The Manager is the distribution mechanism (RL-01)
    4 to 6 Seed → Manager → Postgres POST /v1/policy/{id}, on conflict PUT (#L171-L211) Rego source, title, tag gbo-authz id is uuid5 of the repo-relative path, so a new run updates the policy instead of making a duplicate. The Manager has no file store: policy enters only through the API, the same path as the management interface
    7 to 8 Seed → Manager GET /v1/policies, then PUT /v1/policy/{id} (#L116-L168) Policies with gbo-authz that are not in version control get tag gbo-retired and title prefix RETIRED Reconciliation (RL-04). DELETE fails upstream on a foreign key to the audit trail, so the script retires policies and never deletes them
    9 to 11 PDP → Manager GET /v1/bundle/gbo-pdp on the internal port (gbo-pdp.yaml) Gzipped bundle: version, the policies with tag gbo-authz, design-time data The PDP pulls the bundle. The Manager has no push targets (targets: []). The PDP presents no identity. pdp-bundle.cedar permits only can_read on this one path (RL-02)
    12 PDP — The active policy set The PDP compiles the set as a whole. If one package is duplicated, every request fails (F-52, RL-05)
    13 PDP → Postgres ADL Decision records for data requests and contract proposals The ADL is the authoritative record (ADR-0036). The ADL records no policy version (REQ-59). The ADL can hold OINs. In the EUDI and ASI routes, it can also hold the BSN (REQ-60)

    Components and ports¶

    The Ports column gives each port as host:container. The host ports are the compose defaults. Policy distribution uses the following components:

    Component Ports Role
    openftv-manager 9280:8443 management API · 9281:9443 internal (bundle) · 9282:8080 health PAP. The Manager stores policy and builds bundles. Cedar policies from /authz authorize its own API (admin.cedar, auditor.cedar, pdp-bundle.cedar). The Manager fails closed on an empty store (docker-compose.yml#L266-L269)
    openftv-manager-ui 9283:8080 Management interface: policies, deployments, and the ADL (shown as "Logboek")
    keycloak 9284:8080 Demo identity provider of the management plane. Realm gbo with roles admin, author, and auditor. The Manager reads the roles from the roles claim (MANAGER_OIDC_ROLES_CLAIM)
    postgres-ftv internal Two databases: ftv_manager (policy and audit trail) and ftv_adl (decision log). They are separate because their migration bookkeeping conflicts. The component runs in every profile
    openftv-pdp 9181:8443 AuthZEN · 9180:8080 health Decides. The PDP gets its policy set from the mount. If PDP_BUNDLE_MANAGER is set, the PDP gets the set as a bundle

    Only the Manager, its interface, and Keycloak are opt-in (profile manager).

    Failures¶

    Each fault in the following table has an effect and a guard in v0.9.0:

    Fault Effect Guard in v0.9.0 Evidence
    A non-Rego file under policies/ The loader reads every file as Rego. A file that does not parse drops every policy after it in walk order. The paths of those policies answer HTTP 500 make policy-check, CI step Makefile#L93-L98, ci.yml#L143-L154
    The same file name twice The loader keys policies by file name, so the second file replaces the first. Every decision fails, while opa test passes make policy-check, CI step Makefile#L99-L104, ci.yml#L155-L162
    A module that does not compile, at hot reload The PDP reports the module as loaded. The previous rules keep deciding opa check before start. No runtime signal: a visible fallback is not built in demo v0.9.0 (RL-05) #151, docker-compose.yml#L234-L238
    A policy renamed or removed in version control (bundle mode) The store is cumulative: the old policy stays in the bundle. A duplicate package breaks the whole set, and every request gets HTTP 500 instead of a deny retire_stale at every seed. A failed retirement fails the seed seed-openftv-manager.py#L116-L168, test_seed_openftv_manager.py#L63
    Delete a policy The delete fails upstream on a foreign key to the audit trail Retire (tag gbo-retired) #L119-L123
    Push a bundle from the Manager The PDP authorizes its own management endpoints with the decision policy. That policy denies every request that is not a data request, with HTTP 403 (F-51) No push targets. The PDP pulls at start. The make targets restart the PDP after a seed gbo-pdp.yaml#L18-L32, Makefile#L164-L165
    Bundle pull without a Cedar permit Since v0.1.0, the bundle endpoint uses the same authorizer as the API. Cedar denies by default. Every pull gets HTTP 403, and the PDP gets no bundle pdp-bundle.cedar pdp-bundle.cedar, CHANGELOG
    A changed Cedar file on an existing volume The Manager seeds /authz only into an empty store, then treats the store as the truth. The change does not arrive Add the policy through the API, or recreate the volume CHANGELOG
    MANAGER_POLICIES_LANGUAGE=rego Then the GBO package authz governs the Manager API. From the next restart, the API answers HTTP 403 Not set. The compose file explains why docker-compose.yml#L254-L263
    PDP_POLICIES_LANGUAGE=OPA (the documented value) OpenFTV skips every policy file without a signal Set to rego docker-compose.yml#L106-L114
    No deployment password, or the token request fails The seed stops. The Manager does not change Required variable seed-openftv-manager.py#L236-L250, test_seed_openftv_manager.py#L44
    PDP, Manager, and interface on different OpenFTV versions The bundle format and the API differ CI check ci.yml#L355-L373
    The contract policy package is renamed The FSC Manager finds no policy. Every contract stays pending, without a signal None (comment only) autosign.rego#L8-L10
    The ADL database is missing The PDP exits at start postgres-ftv in every profile docker-compose.yml#L117-L125

    Main observations¶

    Policy distribution in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

    • Two planes, two policy sets. Cedar policies authorize the Manager API. These policies are separate from the Rego decision policy. On the PDP side, this separation is missing. The PDP guards its own management endpoints with the decision policy. As a result, push works only if that policy opens up. The demo pulls instead (F-51, RL-02).
    • Write and publish are not separate. The realm defines author, but no Cedar policy in v0.9.0 grants it an action. Only admin writes and publishes. The deployment identity is that non-personal admin (RL-03).
    • Version control is canonical. The PAP distributes the policy. Manual API changes are possible. As a result, reconciliation at every publication is the only guard against drift (RL-04).
    • The policy set fails as a whole. The policy set is one availability object. If one rule is faulty, the whole set fails, and every request gets HTTP 500 instead of a deny. Since SL-45, the same set also holds the contract policy (policies/fsc/). As a result, one broken module stops the data exchange and also the admission of new participants (F-52, REQ-62).
    • No signing, by decision. The bundle has an ID and a version, but no signature. A bundle gets a signature only when it crosses an organization boundary. Inside one organization, signing is not planned (#426, closed as not planned, F-09, ADR-0021).
    • Source metadata has a fuller lifecycle. Source releases get validation before activation, atomic promotion of immutable releases, and rollback (REQ-66, Source activation). The policy bundle has none of these steps. For this reason, RL-05 is a backlog item and more than a wish (F-59).
    • Read access to the ADL is open. Read access to the decision log is an authorization question. The auditor role reads the ADL through the management interface. The ADL can hold OINs, and in the EUDI and ASI routes also the BSN. It is open who can read the ADL (Q-08, F-53).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: RL-01, RL-02, RL-03, RL-04, RL-05, REQ-59, REQ-60, REQ-62, REQ-66
    • Findings: F-09 (open), F-51 (open), F-52 (open), F-53 (resolved in demo), F-59 (closed)
    • Open questions: Q-21 (answered), Q-02 (answered), Q-08 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-44 (done), SL-45 (done)

    Design-level scenarios¶

    The scenarios on this page have no implementation in gbo-demo v0.9.0. Each section gives the intended sequence, the behavior of v0.9.0 for such a request, and the open points. The first two scenarios go through the same chain as every built data-plane scenario, in this order:

    1. the Outway,
    2. the Inway of the source, as PEP,
    3. the PDP of the source,
    4. the source gateway,
    5. the source API.

    The third scenario uses no GBO runtime.

    Gov-to-Gov¶

    A government consumer reads source data under a legal basis (grondslag). The request has no consent and no pseudonymization, because both parties can process the BSN. The design makes two decisions:

    • The regime follows from the evidence that the request carries. A Gov-to-Gov regime needs its own positive evidence. It cannot be a third regime that the PDP selects because something is absent (ADR-0031, F-70).
    • The PDP evaluates the legal basis locally from policy data, with no PIP call (ADR-0004).

    Demo v0.9.0 has no rule set, no evidence format, and no legal-basis data. This gap is risk R3 in Risks and technical debt.

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Consumer participant GOV as Government consumer<br/>backend end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant OUT as FSC Outway<br/>of the consumer participant MGR as FSC Manager<br/>of the provider participant IN as FSC Inway (PEP) participant PDP as PDP of the source participant GW as Source gateway end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant API as Source API end GOV->>OUT: GraphQL query, subject = BSN,<br/>legal-basis evidence (form open) OUT->>MGR: Access token request (mTLS, grant hash) MGR-->>OUT: Access token, no grant properties OUT->>IN: mTLS + access token + body IN->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation (raw body) Note over PDP: Regime from the legal-basis evidence.<br/>Legal basis from policy data, no PIP call.<br/>Per-field rules as in every regime. PDP-->>IN: Allow or deny IN->>GW: Forward (no consent token: pass-through) GW->>API: Query with the BSN API-->>GOV: Requested fields (through Inway and Outway)

    Data per hop¶

    Each hop of the Gov-to-Gov request carries the following data:

    # From → to Data Notes
    1 Consumer → Outway Query and variables, the BSN as subject, the legal-basis evidence The form of the evidence is open. ADR-0031 rules out declarations, such as a header, a grant property, or a default
    2 to 3 Outway ↔ provider Manager FSC token The contract first passes contract admission
    4 to 7 Inway → PDP → Inway PDP input with the BSN The BSN is in the PDP input and in the decision logs, as in the EUDI and ASI routes of demo v0.9.0 (REQ-60, ADR-0043)
    8 to 10 Inway → gateway → source Query with the BSN, then the requested fields The gateway passes a request without a consent token through (ADR-0033). Each controller logs its own processing (ADR-0026)

    What v0.9.0 does¶

    Demo v0.9.0 handles a Gov-to-Gov request as follows:

    Request Result Evidence
    Government peer without an admission for the source Contract refused: PARTY_NOT_IN_REGISTRY or SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED Admission
    Admitted peer, no consent token, a real BSN as subject PID regime, denied: ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED (not a designated issuer) engine_test.rego#L351
    Service without a rule for the field denied: NO_APPLICABLE_RULE engine.rego#L282

    The chain fails closed. Until a rule set with its own evidence exists, a government consumer gets no data.

    Open points¶

    The Gov-to-Gov design has these open points:

    • It is open what form the positive evidence for the legal basis has, and who issues it (REQ-74).
    • It is open where the legal-basis data lives (which consumer, which service, which legal basis, which fields), and who maintains it. ADR-0004 puts it in policy data.
    • The PID actor lists must stay disjoint from the consumers of other regimes. If a Gov-to-Gov consumer omits its evidence, it must not enter the PID regime (F-70).

    SDG-OOTS¶

    A competent authority in another member state requests evidence about a citizen or company through the Once-Only Technical System. The design is an OOTS adapter at the GBO edge (ADR-0020, PSA S08). eDelivery AS4 exists only at the edge. The bronhouder sees a normal FSC request through the standard PEP-PDP chain. It is open who builds the adapter (Q-79).

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) External participant ER as Evidence requester<br/>(other member state) participant EU as OOTS common services<br/>(discovery) participant AP as Dutch access point<br/>(AS4) end box rgb(255,237,213) OOTS participant OA as OOTS adapter<br/>(OOTS-EDM to GraphQL) end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant OUT as FSC Outway<br/>of the adapter participant IN as FSC Inway (PEP) participant PDP as PDP of the source end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant API as Source API end ER->>EU: Find the evidence type and the provider ER->>AP: AS4 message: OOTS-EDM evidence request AP->>OA: Evidence request OA->>OA: Map the evidence type to a source query OA->>OUT: GraphQL query over FSC OUT->>IN: mTLS + access token + body IN->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation Note over PDP: Regime and evidence for OOTS<br/>not designed PDP-->>IN: Allow or deny IN->>API: Query (through the source gateway) API-->>OA: Source data (through Inway and Outway) OA->>OA: Map to OOTS-EDM evidence OA->>AP: Evidence response AP->>ER: AS4 message: evidence

    The OOTS process steps around the request, such as the identification of the user and the preview, stay with the Basisinrichting OOTS. The diagram does not show them.

    Data per hop¶

    Each hop of the OOTS request carries the following data:

    # From → to Data Notes
    1 to 3 Requester → access point → adapter OOTS-EDM evidence request in an AS4 message: evidence type, the subject, the requester Transport, discovery, and the European process stay with the Basisinrichting OOTS (Q-79)
    4 Adapter Evidence type → source query The mapping depends on the canonical semantic models (ADR-0024)
    5 to 10 Adapter → source GraphQL query and FSC token, then source data The same chain as every FSC consumer. The adapter translates the protocol. The decision stays with the PDP of the source (REQ-44, REQ-46)
    11 to 13 Adapter → requester OOTS-EDM evidence The mapping version must be traceable, as for issuance (REQ-124)

    What v0.9.0 does¶

    The demo does not touch OOTS. It has no adapter, no access point, and no rule for OOTS. If an adapter peer sends a request without a consent token, the request enters the PID regime and fails the actor check, as in Gov-to-Gov. The gap is risk R2 in Risks and technical debt.

    Open points¶

    The OOTS design has these open points:

    • It is open who builds the adapter: GBO, or the OOTS-V operator with the GBO interface (Q-79). OOTS-V is the part of the Basisinrichting OOTS that receives evidence requests.
    • The regime and the evidence for an OOTS request are open (REQ-74, ADR-0031). If an OOTS request has no evidence of its own, the PDP denies it.
    • The requirements register has no OOTS requirement.

    Relying-party presentation¶

    The citizen presents a wallet attestation from GBO to a relying party over OpenID4VP, with selective disclosure. No GBO decision component and no source take part at presentation time. This is the purpose of an issuance-based route. The data are fixed at issuance, and the source carries no presentation load. For the issuance itself, see EUDI issuance.

    sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor CIT as Citizen end box rgb(241,239,232) External participant W as EUDI wallet participant RP as Relying party<br/>(verifier) participant TL as Trust list<br/>(open, Q-30) end box rgb(255,237,213) EUDI participant PUB as Publications of the<br/>issuance facility end RP->>W: OpenID4VP request: reader certificate, requested claims W->>CIT: Show who asks for which claims CIT->>W: Approve, or refuse W->>RP: Presentation: dc+sd-jwt, selected disclosures, key binding opt Trust anchor not cached RP->>TL: Get the trust anchor of the issuer end RP->>RP: Verify the issuer signature, the disclosures and the key binding opt Status and type RP->>PUB: GET the token status list (whole list) RP->>PUB: GET the Type Metadata of the vct end RP->>RP: Check the status and the validity

    Data per hop¶

    Each hop of the presentation carries the following data:

    # From → to Data Notes
    1 to 3 Relying party → wallet → citizen Reader certificate of the relying party, the requested claims The approval in the wallet is no legal basis for the relying party (F-83)
    4 Wallet → relying party Selected claims of the attestation, signed by the issuer, with key binding The wallet sends only the claims that the citizen selects
    5 Relying party → trust list Trust anchor of the PuB-EAA issuer It is open which list applies: a List of Trusted Entities or the trusted lists (Q-30)
    7 to 8 Relying party → issuance facility Status list per attestation type, Type Metadata Static publications. The relying party fetches the whole list, so the issuer does not learn which attestation the relying party checks. No PDP, no FSC, and no source take part

    What v0.9.0 does¶

    For this scenario, demo v0.9.0 has these limits:

    • The demo has no relying party for GBO attestations. The ASI wallet verifier asks only for the PID (asi-wallet-verifier/README.md).
    • Trust uses the development CA chain. The test wallet and the demo verifiers trust the development issuer CA.
    • Every attestation is valid for 365 days. A status list exists per type, but revocation on instruction of the bronhouder is not built (REQ-77).

    Open points¶

    The relying-party scenario has these open points:

    • The trust list for PuB-EAA providers (Q-30) and the designation of the Dutch PuB-EAA issuer (Q-28) are open. In production, the relying party verifies the seal of the bronhouder as PuB-EAA provider. GBO operates the technical facility (ADR-0028). ADR-0023 proposes the EUDI certificate roles.
    • Freshness. The attestation shows the source data at issuance. GBO only reads the source on request. If the data change, GBO gets no signal. Long-lived attestations need a change feed and revocation (F-82).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-74, REQ-44, REQ-46, REQ-60, REQ-77, REQ-124
    • Findings: F-70 (open), F-82 (open), F-83 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-79 (open), Q-30 (open), Q-28 (open)
    • Demo increments: none

    Deployment view¶

    The GBO deployment in this chapter follows the infrastructure configuration of gbo-demo v0.9.0: docker-compose.yml, fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml, the Makefile, and the Helm chart. The demo is a reference deployment. It is not a production topology. The availability model lists what changes for production.

    Environments¶

    The demo runs in two environments:

    Environment Platform Purpose
    Local Two Docker Compose projects: the main stack and fsc-infra. Make targets start them: demo-minimal, demo-dvtp (the default make demo), demo-eudi, demo-full, demo-manager, demo-integrator, and demo-asi. Development and demonstration
    Simulation Kubernetes with the generic gbo-app Helm chart. Each application is one release with a Deployment or a Job, a Service, and a Gateway API HTTPRoute. It runs in two tenants: MinEZK (Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy) and MinBZK (Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations). Public demo at gbo.simulatie.datastelsel.nl

    Compose profiles switch on optional parts. The base (no profile) runs the PDP and its databases, the admission register (toelatingsregister), and the consent register (toestemmingsregister). It also runs the BD and BRP sources with their gateways, the BSNk mock, the decryption component, the LDV logbooks, the developer portal, and observability. Each profile adds parts to the base:

    Profile Adds Make target
    dvtp Consent portal (toestemmingsportaal), consumer backends and frontends (Hypotheek-BV, Installatie Register with keyper-mock), and the LVG source and gateway demo-dvtp
    eudi Issuance chain: postgres-eudi, source registry bootstrap and migrations, issuance migrations, configuration materializer, issuance server, and EUDI adapter demo-eudi
    onboarding Source reconciler as the registry writer, with postgres-eudi and the registry jobs onboard-demo-sources
    full dvtp and eudi together demo-full
    integrator Integrator backend and the int-* peer in fsc-infra demo-integrator (after demo-dvtp or demo-full)
    asi ASIP, ASI authorization server, wallet verifier, discovery stub, reference QTSP, and the asip-* peer in fsc-infra demo-asi (after demo-eudi or demo-full)
    manager OpenFTV Manager, its UI, and Keycloak demo-manager

    In demo v0.9.0, the ASI route runs only locally. The chart has no values for the ASI services. Issue #594 covers the deployment to the simulation environment. The simulation uses its own Peer IDs, for example 0000009961MINEZK0000 for the issuance peer.

    Deployment units and network zones¶

    The local stack separates traffic with Docker networks. The isolation of the source gateway is a security control. The gateway acts on the consent token after the PDP allows the request. It does not verify the token again (REQ-81, ADR-0033). The local stack has these networks:

    Network Members Purpose
    frontend Browser-facing UIs UI traffic
    backend Most services Service traffic
    dvtp-onboarding PDP and admission register only Keeps admission data away from other services
    eudi Issuance chain, postgres-eudi, reconciler, ASIP, and reference QTSP Source registry and issuance
    source-gateways Source Inways (bd-inway, brp-inway) and source gateways The only path to a gateway. fsc-infra owns this network.
    sources Source gateways, source APIs, decryption component, source logbooks, and OTel collector Traffic of the components that serve the sources. No consumer is on this network.
    fsc-infra FSC components and the services they reach FSC transport

    The source gateways publish no port and are only on source-gateways and sources (docker-compose.yml). Two limits apply to this isolation:

    • The source APIs are also on backend and fsc-infra. The FSC metadata services of BD and RvIG point at them directly. In the demo, a container on those networks can reach a source API without the PDP. Production must limit a source API to its gateway and its metadata path.
    • The chart has no NetworkPolicy. A Kubernetes deployment needs one, or an equivalent control (F-79).

    The consent register also relies on network placement. Its portal API must serve only the portal backend (REQ-39). The API does not authenticate the caller. It is open whether it must (Q-58).

    The status listener of the register answers only with the FSC peer that cr-inway forwards (REQ-76). In the demo, the listener is also reachable on the compose networks. Production does not accept that exposure.

    The data path runs through these peers and networks:
