      • Behind the FSC Inway, the record does not hold the trace ID or adl.fsc.transaction_id (#369, ADR-0035). The dev portal finds the record through the stored request headers.
      • No pointer leads from the ADL record to the logbook of the consent register (toestemmingsregister) (Q-25).
      • In the EUDI and ASI routes, the record holds the plain BSN (REQ-60, ADR-0043).
    • A replay of a decision from (input, policy, data) is not possible, because the policy fetches the consent status during the evaluation (ADR-0032). A replay needs the non-deterministic built-in cache of OPA, and OpenFTV does not enable this cache.
    • Retention, read access, and tamper evidence are not set (REQ-32, Q-08).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-71, REQ-32, REQ-59, REQ-60, REQ-06
    • Findings: F-07 (closed), F-53 (resolved in demo), F-63 (closed), F-72 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-08 (open), Q-25 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-04 (done), SL-50 (exploration done, build delivered)

    ADR-0037: Authentic Source Interface as an OAuth front door per ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1¶

    • Status: accepted (demo grade)
    • Date: 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: eIDAS article 45e, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569 article 9, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735 Annex IV, GO: verification and retrieval service for QTSPs, S11, S04
    • Supersedes: ADR-0029
    • Deliberation: SL-28, F-80, F-87, and demo epic ICTU/GBO-demo#336
    • Implemented in:
      • services/asi-provider: the ASIP.
      • services/asi-authorization-server and services/asi-wallet-verifier.
      • services/asi-discovery-stub: a stub.
      • services/qtsp-reference: the reference client.
      • asi0001.rego: the rule.
      • The ASIP FSC peer in fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml#L1664-L1669.
      • The conformance matrix and docs/asi-route.md.

    Context and problem statement¶

    Article 45e of eIDAS lets a qualified trust service provider (QTSP) verify attributes of a citizen at an authentic source. The QTSP does this at the request of that citizen. ETSI TS 119 478 V1.1.1 specifies the interfaces.

    Two regulations make clause 6.1.1 (verify) the legal interface: article 9 of Implementing Regulation 2025/1569, and Annex IV of Implementing Regulation 2026/1735. From January 1, 2027, every verification result must be sealed (article 9(4)). The regulations do not designate clause 6.1.3 (authorization) or clause 5 (discovery). For this reason, the design of the authorization part is a national choice (F-80).

    The reference architecture placed the interface "in front of" the FSC and PEP-PDP chain (ADR-0029). The demo showed that this placement is not correct. A QTSP is an EU party with an access certificate and a register entitlement. A QTSP has no FSC peer, no OIN, and no PKIoverheid certificate (F-87). GBO needs two parts:

    • A trust model for the QTSP and the citizen that ends before FSC.
    • A chain behind that trust model that a source can judge like any other consumer.

    Decision¶

    GBO offers the Authentic Source Interface as an OAuth front door with its own trust model. The generic chain starts behind it. The front door works as follows:

    1. Interface. The Authentic Source Interface Provider (ASIP) offers clause 6.1 only: 6.1.1 verify, 6.1.2 retrieve, and 6.1.3 authorization with the scopes verify and retrieve. The ASIP does not offer clause 6.2 (ISO 15000) (REQ-112, Q-64). Each authentic source gets its own data service under /<data service>/authsrc-api (ADR-0038).
    2. Two services with separate keys. The ASIP and the authorization server are separate services. The ASIP gets the token keys of the authorization server from its RFC 8414 metadata.
    3. The QTSP is an OAuth client. It is not an FSC participant. QTSP admission is not a PDP rule. The authorization server admits a QTSP as follows (REQ-88, REQ-89):
      • The QTSP registers through RFC 7591. The QTSP seals the software statement with its certificate (x5c, registryURI).
      • The server verifies the chain against its trust anchors.
      • Then the server looks up the register entry. The entry must carry the entitlement QEAA_Provider and the organizationIdentifier of the certificate.
      • The client key is the certificate key.
      • The server repeats the lookup periodically. It deactivates a client without entitlement.
    4. Login is approval. Before login, the citizen sees one request page (REQ-91). The page shows the legal name of the QTSP from the register, the operation, the source, and the attributes, if they are bound. The citizen approves by logging in, or refuses without login (REQ-90). The approval is one login per request: it is not a stored consent, and it has no relation to the consent register (toestemmingsregister). Approval in a wallet is not a legal basis (F-83).
    5. Token. The authorization server uses the authorization code flow with PKCE S256 and private_key_jwt. It issues a DPoP-bound RFC 9068 JWT (ES256, 10 minutes). The token carries the identification data and the means used (acr, amr) (REQ-86). The resource parameter names exactly one data service (REQ-95). As an option, the token is bound to the attributes (ADR-0042).
    6. The ASIP takes the citizen only from the token. The ASIP verifies the token and the DPoP proof before anything else (REQ-87). Then the ASIP sends one GraphQL query per request through its own FSC Outway, as peer …1200 (REQ-92, REQ-46). The PDP of the source sees the ASIP as actor, and never the QTSP or the citizen. Rule ASI0001 grants the ASIP peer the fields behind the attributes, on service brp only.
    7. Results. Per attribute, the ASIP answers Match, NoMatch, MatchWithVariation, or Unknown:
      • A verify response contains no source value (REQ-85).
      • Unknown means only that the source has no complete value (REQ-84).
      • If the chain does not answer, the result is 503 or 500, and never Unknown (REQ-93).
      • If a retrieve finds no value, the result is 404, with no partial result (REQ-101).
      • If a request has mandate, the result is 501 (REQ-114).
    8. Seal. The ASIP seals every successful response (REQ-83). ADR-0041 sets the format.
    9. Discovery. The ASIP publishes a dataService record per attribute and data service. The contract of the data service names the metadata of the authorization server (REQ-99, REQ-100).
    10. Conformance. A conformance matrix gives every ETSI requirement ID a status and named tests. If an ID or a test is missing, CI fails.

    Consequences¶

    • The ASIP is a channel adapter in the sense of REQ-44. The source decides with its own PDP. The source needs no ASI-specific logic.
    • The source sees only the ASIP. The ASIP passes nothing about the QTSP into the chain, and it writes no LDV record. A citizen cannot see which QTSP verified data (F-87).
    • Rule ASI0001 checks the actor, the service, and the field list. It also checks that the subject is a BSN, and not a placeholder. The rule does not check the token or the QTSP. The BSN is in the PDP input and in the decision log (REQ-60, ADR-0043).
    • EUDI issuance does not replace retrieve, because the QTSP issues the QEAA, and GBO does not.
    • QTSP admission depends on a register and on access certificates that do not exist on November 2, 2026. The demo uses a register file and test certificates (F-85).
    • If a QTSP needs attributes of two sources, it authorizes twice (ADR-0038).
    • The conformance matrix of v0.9.0 has 55 passed, 4 stub, 21 not applicable, and 1 failing. The failing item is REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-10-01: fuzzy matching asks for the value, and the ASIP returns none (F-92, Q-29).
    • The route runs locally only. ICTU/GBO-demo#594 tracks a deployment to the simulation environment with an external QTSP.

    Considered options¶

    The decision considered four other options:

    • Skip retrieve, as ADR-0029 proposed. Not chosen. A QTSP needs the value to issue a QEAA. The EUDI issuance chain does not replace that, because the QTSP issues the attestation, and GBO does not.
    • Make the QTSP an FSC participant. Not chosen. QTSPs are EU parties with access certificates and register entitlements. Clause 6.1 is HTTPS with OAuth.
    • Admit the QTSP in the PDP of the source (a Trusted List check as a rule). Not chosen. The PDP sees only the FSC actor. Admission belongs where the token is issued.
    • Offer clause 6.2 (ISO 15000) as well. Not in demo v0.9.0: Q-64 holds this point open.

    Open points¶

    Security profile of the authorization server¶

    The security profile is open (Q-66). ETSI leaves the profile open and conflicts with FAPI 2.0 on PAR and RS256 (F-84, E8).

    The demo uses private_key_jwt and DPoP. It has no mTLS client authentication, no PAR, and no refresh tokens. The authorization server signs with ES256. The ASIP also accepts RS256, because RFC 9068 requires it. security-considerations.md lists the demo choices.

    These points of the profile are open:

    • The authorization response has no iss (RFC 9207). A QTSP that uses several ASIPs has no mix-up defense (F-96, E9).
    • Tokens stay valid for up to 10 minutes after the withdrawal of the entitlement (Q-41, E10).
    • If the register is unreachable during a re-check, the client stays active (Q-34).
    • Which identifier links the access certificate to the register entry (Q-35)?

    Citizen identification at the authorization server¶

    Citizen identification is open (Q-36). The demo accepts two means:

    • The NL Wallet over OpenID4VP, through the nl-wallet verification_server. It asks only the PID attributes of its registration, and it requires a BSN in urn:eudi:pid:nl:1 (REQ-102). The trusted PID issuers are a fixed list, and not a trusted list. The verifier accepts a PID with an undetermined revocation status.
    • A DigiD mock (stub). DigiD supplies only the BSN (F-88).

    These related points are open:

    • The NL PID has no place of birth, but the implementing regulation makes it mandatory (F-94).
    • The BSN is in plain text in the token, so the QTSP can read it (F-86, E7, ICTU/GBO-demo#595).
    • Nothing links the citizen who logs in at the QTSP to the citizen who logs in at the authorization server (F-93, Q-40, E6).
    • The same-device wallet login did not run on a phone in demo v0.9.0 (ICTU/GBO-demo#596).
    • P-05 decides which means are recognized at the correct assurance level.

    Role, legal basis, and registration¶

    These points are open:

    • Who designates the ASI intermediary, and what is the role of GBO (Q-28, Q-37)? The PSA decision register holds this point as open decision B-14.
    • What is the legal basis to verify for private QTSPs, and does the ASIP return the value on a match (Q-29)?
    • Who registers the data services in the catalogue of attributes and the Discover Interface, and how does the contract name the authorization server (Q-31, Q-67, Q-39, F-91)?
    • How do requests on behalf of another person work (Q-65)?

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-83, REQ-84, REQ-85, REQ-86, REQ-87, REQ-88, REQ-89, REQ-90, REQ-91, REQ-92, REQ-93, REQ-99, REQ-100, REQ-101, REQ-102, REQ-112, REQ-114, REQ-44, REQ-46, REQ-60. Profile: GBO profile on ETSI TS 119 478
    • Findings: F-80 (open), F-83 (open), F-84 (open), F-85 (open), F-86 (open), F-87 (open), F-88 (open), F-91 (open), F-92 (open), F-93 (open), F-94 (open), F-96 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-28, Q-29, Q-31, Q-34, Q-35, Q-36, Q-37, Q-39, Q-40, Q-41, Q-64, Q-65, Q-66, Q-67
    • Standards feedback: E6, E7, E8, E9, E10
    • Demo increments: SL-28

    ADR-0038: One data service per authentic source, one token per data service¶

    • Status: accepted
    • Date: 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569 article 9(4), as replaced by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735 (the result names the body that is responsible for the authentic source), S11, P-10, P-13
    • Deliberation: F-89, and demo PR #529, PR #534, PR #535
    • Implemented in:
      • config/dataservices.json: the data services.
      • handler.go#L99-L105: the routes per data service.
      • main.go#L115-L125 and accesstoken.go#L148: the token audience per data service.
      • service.go#L201-L204: one resource at the authorization server.

    Context and problem statement¶

    ETSI TS 119 478 lets a verify or retrieve response name one authentic source (authenticSource, REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.2-08 and REQ-ASIP-6.1.2.2-04). Article 9(4) requires that the result names the body that is responsible for that source. GBO offers one ASIP for several sources. For this reason, that ASIP must keep every request inside one source (F-89).

    The token has the same problem. The citizen approves a request for one source (REQ-91). If the token is also valid at another source, the QTSP can verify data at a source that the citizen did not see. ETSI does not specify the reach of a token per data service.

    Decision¶

    The decision has four parts:

    1. An ASIP that serves several authentic sources offers one data service per source. Each data service has its own base URL (/<data service>/authsrc-api), its own contract, its own dataService records, and its own token audience (REQ-94, REQ-99).
    2. Every response names the ASIP (provider) and the one authentic source of the data service (authenticSource). Since step 5 of ICTU/GBO-demo#592, the legal name comes from the description of the source (ADR-0039). A data service without an authentic source is not possible.
    3. If an attribute belongs to another data service, the ASIP answers 404. The ASIP then asks no source.
    4. An authorization request names exactly one data service as resource (RFC 8707):
      • If the request has no resource, two, or an unknown one, the result is invalid_target.
      • The token has the base URL of that data service as aud.
      • The ASIP refuses a token for another data service with 401 (REQ-95).

    Consequences¶

    • If a QTSP needs attributes of two sources, it authorizes twice. The citizen logs in twice.
    • The request page can name one source and its legal name (REQ-91).
    • Every data service needs its own records in the Data Service Directory. It is open who registers them (Q-67).
    • The demo has one data service: brp, with source rvig. A second data service exists only in unit tests.
    • The authorization server takes its list of data services from the configuration (AZSP_RESOURCES). It does not take the list from the source descriptions (ADR-0039, an open part of #592).
    • It is open whether an ASIP for several sources makes GBO an intermediary in the sense of article 9(4) (Q-37).

    Considered options¶

    The decision considered three other options:

    • One endpoint for all sources that refuses requests across sources. Not chosen. With this option, the contract, the records, and the token audience do not show which source answers.
    • One authorization for several resources, with a token per resource (RFC 8707 §2.2). Not chosen. This option saves the citizen a login. But the request page then shows several sources at once, and ETSI clients do not expect that.
    • One token for several sources. Not chosen. With this option, the token is valid at a source that the citizen did not see.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-91, REQ-94, REQ-95, REQ-99
    • Findings: F-89 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-37, Q-67
    • Standards feedback: E3
    • Demo increments: SL-28

    ADR-0039: ASI attributes described by the source (asi capability in source metadata)¶

    • Status: accepted, partly implemented. In demo v0.9.0, the authorization server takes its resource list from configuration (ICTU/GBO-demo#592 is open).
    • Date: 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: S10, S07, S11, P-10, P-02
    • Deliberation: Q-38, and demo ICTU/GBO-demo#592 steps 1 to 5, up to PR #624
    • Implemented in:
      • asiCapability in gbo-source-metadata-v1.schema.json#L95.
      • The attribute catalogue schemas/asi-attributes.json.
      • The mapping module services/asi-mapping.
      • The validation by the reconciler in source_registration.go#L396-L406.
      • The release snapshot in services/source-registry/asisnapshot.
      • The query per request in verification/service.go#L238-L268 and plan.go#L22-L35.
      • The BRP description in gbo-source-metadata.json#L204.
      • The rules in docs/source-onboarding.md#L391-L487.

    Context and problem statement¶

    Per data service, the ASIP must know three things:

    • Which attributes the source offers.
    • Which source fields make each attribute.
    • How to ask for these fields.

    The first demo ASIP had this knowledge in code, as a BRP adapter. That breaks REQ-64: a GBO component works only with the description that the source publishes itself. With the adapter, a new source needs a code change in the ASIP.

    Q-38 named three options: code, GBO configuration, or a description that the source publishes. On October 27, the direction became the third option, with a "copy only" mapping. ETSI expects attribute identifiers and value schemas from the EU catalogue of attributes. That catalogue did not exist on November 2, 2026.

    This ADR extends ADR-0016 from EUDI issuance to the ASIP.

    Decision¶

    The decision has seven parts:

    1. The source describes its attributes. Source metadata schema 1.1 adds the capability asi next to eudi. The capability holds these parts:
      • authentic_source: the legal name and country, used in responses and discovery records.
      • graphql: one query document that ends in ...Selected, the subject variable, and the result pointer.
      • attributes: per attribute identifier, the source fields per member of the value.
    2. GBO keeps the shape of each value. GBO keeps a value_schema per attribute identifier in schemas/asi-attributes.json, until the EU catalogue of attributes provides it. The identifiers are provisional. The value schemas use only type, properties, required, items, and format.

    3. The source composes values with four operations. Each member of a value has exactly one operation:

      • pointer: copy a field.
      • join with separator: concatenate fields.
      • const: a fixed value.
      • each with pointer: per list element.

      Pointers are RFC 6901 JSON Pointers over GraphQL field names. This part deviates from the "copy only" direction of October 27. A source cannot always deliver a catalogue value with a copy only. An example is a house number made of three BRP fields.

    4. gbo-simple-v1 stays for the eudi capability only (ADR-0017). The two capabilities have different targets. The eudi target is wallet claims that the source defines. The asi target is values that the catalogue of GBO defines.

    5. The reconciler validates, and the ASIP reads the active release. The reconciler validates asi against the catalogue, as part of the source metadata (ADR-0016). If asi is invalid, the reconciler refuses the whole source. The ASIP reads the active release from the source registry every 5 seconds, with the reader role.
    6. One query per request. The ASIP replaces ...Selected with only the fields of the requested attributes and fragments (REQ-92). If the description does not name an attribute, the ASIP answers 404 and does not ask the source.
    7. Fuzzy matching follows the value schema. A string with a format, such as a date, matches exactly or does not match. Only strings without a format get MatchWithVariation (REQ-113).

    Consequences¶

    • A new source for the ASIP needs a description and a configured data service. It needs no code. The discovery records and the legal name of the source follow the description without a restart.
    • If no current description exists (absent, without asi, or stale), the ASIP answers 503 for verify, retrieve, and discovery (REQ-93).
    • A source with asi gets release snapshot version 4.0. A source without asi stays at 3.0. Onboarding still refuses a document with only asi, because onboarding requires the issuance certificate sets.
    • Onboarding validates the form only. It does not validate against the GraphQL schema of the source. It also does not check whether the policy of the source allows the selection. A difference shows at the first request. A demo test holds the BRP description against rule ASI0001.
    • The ASIP still normalizes a code without a format, such as a nationality or a postal code. For codes, demo v0.9.0 does not meet REQ-113 (Q-70).
    • The shape of name and address is provisional (Q-71).

    Open points¶

    These points are open:

    • The authorization server takes its data services from AZSP_RESOURCES (main.go#L105), and not from the descriptions. This is the open part of ICTU/GBO-demo#592.
    • The identifiers and value schemas move to the EU catalogue of attributes when it exists (Q-31).
    • Which normalization applies per kind of value (Q-70)?
    • The document format is part of the open PSA S10 decision on the source-specific configuration (ADR-0016).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-64, REQ-84, REQ-92, REQ-93, REQ-94, REQ-113, REQ-115
    • Findings: F-57 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-31, Q-38, Q-70, Q-71
    • Demo increments: SL-28, SL-46

    Proposed

    ADR-0024: Canonical semantic models per bronhouder¶

    • Status: proposed
    • Date: 2026-08-24
    • Satisfies: S10, D-14, GO F4
    • Deliberation: reference architecture v0.6.2, gap 3 (archived and unpublished)
    • Implemented in: partially. The GraphQL schemas of the sources come from the gbo-semantiek source profiles. No route serializations other than SD-JWT VC exist.

    Context and problem statement¶

    The same data must appear in three forms:

    • GraphQL responses (DvTP).
    • Attestation claims (EUDI).
    • OOTS-EDM evidence (cross-border).

    If no canonical model per source exists, every route grows its own mapping.

    Proposed decision¶

    The source profile GraphQL schema is the canonical model per source. The GBO-Semantiek track maintains this schema. GBO generates or defines the route serializations from it:

    • Attestation attribute schemas and type metadata. The sources already publish these, as ADR-0016 decides.
    • OOTS-EDM evidence-type mappings for ADR-0020.

    Open points¶

    These points are open:

    • The governance between the schemas of the bronhouders and the central semantics track.
    • The mapping coverage for the evidence types of the OOTS Semantic Repository.
    • Is gbo-simple-v1 (ADR-0017) sufficient as the projection language for richer models?

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-124
    • Open questions: Q-79

    ADR-0025: GraphQL as a recognized FDS data service type¶

    • Status: proposed
    • Date: 2026-08-24
    • Satisfies: D-08, D-13, PSA: REST versus GraphQL note
    • Deliberation: reference architecture v0.6.2, gap 4 (archived and unpublished)
    • Implemented in: not applicable (standardization action)

    Context and problem statement¶

    FDS mandates the REST API Design Rules. GraphQL is not a recognized data service (datadienst) type in FDS. The data access pillar of GBO (ADR-0001) depends on GraphQL. For this reason, GBO must bring the deviation to the standards bodies under the comply-or-explain rule ("pas toe of leg uit").

    Proposed decision¶

    GBO proposes GraphQL as an additional data service type through the FDS and Forum Standaardisatie processes. The proposal includes a Digikoppeling GraphQL profile. The proposal positions GraphQL as follows:

    • GraphQL runs over FSC, and the transport does not change.
    • The iWlz/nID production deployment and gbo-demo are the precedent.
    • The AuthZEN mapping of the query structure to the authorization input is the enforcement story.

    Open points¶

    These points are open:

    • The owner and the timeline of the standardization submission.
    • The scope of a Digikoppeling GraphQL profile (pagination, errors, introspection policy).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: none directly. The data access pillar it supports is ADR-0001.

    ADR-0027: Bronhouder onboarding toolkit¶

    • Status: proposed
    • Date: 2026-08-24, updated on 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: D-06, GO §6: impact on bronhouders
    • Deliberation: reference architecture v0.6.2, gap 6 "bronhouder onboarding toolkit" (archived and unpublished)
    • Implemented in: partially. These parts of the demo are reusable starting points: the Helm chart, the source metadata contract (ADR-0016), the source gateway (ADR-0033), and the contract seed scripts.

    Context and problem statement¶

    GBO has one API and one connectivity stack. Even so, the connection of a bronhouder involves PKI, FSC components, a source gateway, policies, and metadata. Smaller bronhouders, for example municipalities, can lack the capacity for this work.

    Proposed decision¶

    GBO packages the source-side stack as a deployable toolkit. The toolkit has these parts:

    • FSC Inway and Manager.
    • The source gateway (bron-sidecar).
    • Contract seeds.
    • Policy templates per route.
    • A reference onboarding process: certificate, FSC registration, metadata publication, contract, and activation.

    Some sources cannot host their own GraphQL endpoint. For these sources, GBO offers a GBO translation layer (GBO-vertaallaag) as a shared service.

    Open points¶

    These points are open:

    • Who operates the shared instances of the translation layer?
    • The policy templates are guidance. Each bronhouder owns and publishes its own policy (ADR-0021).
    • How does a source get its BSNk decryption keys as an onboarding step (BSNK-09, #467)?
    • Who builds the registration and onboarding facility (Q-74)?
    • The support model and the conformance testing for onboarded sources.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-64, REQ-65, AV-07, AV-09, BSNK-09
    • Findings: F-57 (open), F-71 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-74 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-09 (mostly covered), SL-46 (done)

    ADR-0028: PubEAA Provider productization¶

    • Status: proposed
    • Date: 2026-08-24, rewritten on 2026-11-02. The rewrite made the bronhouder the PuB-EAA provider and GBO the technical issuance facility, and added the regulatory frame of F-81.
    • Satisfies: S11, P-06, GO: PuB-EAA issuance
    • Deliberation: reference architecture v0.6.2, gap 7 (archived and unpublished), F-81, F-82, REQ-77
    • Implemented in: demo grade. The issuance chain of ADR-0018 works end to end with development CAs. issuance_config.go#L166-L168 fixes the validity at 365 days.

    Context and problem statement¶

    The government issues no PuB-EAAs. For this reason, the Netherlands relies on commercial QTSPs for attestations from government sources. The demo proves the issuance chain. Production status needs trust anchoring and governance. The demo leaves these out on purpose.

    The first version of this ADR made the shared GBO facility the PuB-EAA provider that the member state notifies. That choice does not fit the regulation or the GO:

    • eIDAS article 3(46) names two possible issuers. One is the body that is responsible for the authentic source. The other is a public sector body that the member state designates on behalf of that body.
    • The notification specification (EUDI TS2) assumes that the bronhouder is the provider. A party that issues on behalf of the bronhouder goes in the field EEAIssuer.
    • The GO describes GBO as a technical, central, and optional issuance facility. Legally, GBO is not a PuB-EAA provider. The bronhouder stays legally responsible (PSA S11).

    Since August 2026, PuB-EAA issuance also falls under the same standard as QEAA issuance (F-81).

    Proposed decision¶

    The proposal has seven parts:

    1. Roles. Each bronhouder is the PuB-EAA provider of its attestations. GBO operates the technical issuance facility. GBO is probably the EEAIssuer in the notification of each bronhouder. The designation of GBO or the management organization under article 3(46) is an open decision (Q-28).
    2. Conformity. The facility conforms to ETSI TS 119 471 with EN 319 401. Implementing Regulation 2026/1735 requires this for QEAA and PuB-EAA providers. Issuance follows OpenID4VCI as ETSI TS 119 472-3 specifies. The issuance checks the wallet instance attestation and the key attestation.
    3. Certificates per bronhouder:
      • The facility seals the attestation in a QSCD, with a qualified seal certificate as ETSI TS 119 412-6 clause 8 specifies. The certificate names the authentic source and the legal basis (eIDAS article 45f(1)(b)).
      • Each registered service has its own access certificate and registration certificate.
      • The issuer registers as relying party with the entitlement PUB_EAA_Provider.
      • ADR-0023 describes the roles.
    4. Rulebook per type. Each Dutch attestation type gets a rulebook. The rulebook uses the template of the rulebooks catalogue.
    5. Validity and revocation per type. The bronhouder sets them (REQ-77):
      • If an attestation is valid for more than 24 hours, it carries a status reference.
      • The facility revokes the attestation on instruction of the bronhouder, and when the source data changes.
      • GBO only queries and gets no change signal (F-82). For this reason, each type chooses one of two forms: short-lived (less than 24 hours), or long-lived with a change feed from the source and revocation.
    6. The callback gap of ADR-0018 is closed with positive PID evidence and an authenticated callback (REQ-45).
    7. The facility is optional per bronhouder. Sources with capacity can run their own credential issuer.

    Consequences¶

    • The legal responsibility for content, validity, and revocation stays with the bronhouder. GBO revokes technically, on instruction of the bronhouder (AV-12, AV-13).
    • Notification and registration happen per bronhouder. They do not happen once for GBO.
    • Nobody tested the demo against ETSI TS 119 471, the certificate profile, or the checks of ETSI TS 119 472-3.
    • The development CA of the demo stands in for all certificate roles at once. Production separates the roles.
    • The central facility holds the private keys of the issuer and status-list certificates of every source. That needs a decision on key custody (Q-17).

    Open points¶

    These points are open:

    • Who holds and uses the seal and status-list keys of a bronhouder (Q-17)? The options are the central facility, a remote signing service, or an HSM at the bronhouder.
    • Who designates the Dutch PuB-EAA issuer, and who supervises (Q-28)?
    • On which trust list do PuB-EAA providers appear: a List of Trusted Entities or the trusted lists (Q-30)? This point is open, and no fact settles it.
    • Does every source answer get one seal, regardless of the channel (Q-75)?
    • The governance of the attestation schema per attestation type.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-45, REQ-58, REQ-77, AV-12, AV-13
    • Findings: F-66 (closed), F-81 (open), F-82 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-17, Q-28, Q-30, Q-75
    • Demo increments: SL-26

    ADR-0040: Citizen recognition and the BSNk participant: route D¶

    • Status: proposed (waits for Q-49)
    • Date: 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: S01, S02, S03, P-04
    • Deliberation: Open design choice: how does the register find the citizen again?, route D, routes A, B and C, F-75, F-98, and demo PR #469
    • Implemented in: demo, provisionally:
      • subjectref.go: the HMAC reference.
      • portal.go: one activation per citizen.
      • polymorphic.go: PI and PP stored under the reference.

    Context and problem statement¶

    The consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) needs two things from a citizen who logged in:

    1. A stable key for its own administration. With this key, the service shows and revokes the consents of the citizen without a BSN (REQ-20, REQ-40).
    2. A PI and a PP. With these, the service makes the values for the parties at a new consent (BSNK-03).

    A stored PI or PP is not a stable key. BSNk gives other values at every activation, and the service cannot compute these values from a BSN. Every activation goes into the BSNk access register (Inzageregister) (BSNK-10). Only a recognized BSNk participant can activate and transform (BSNK-01).

    Two points are open (Q-49):

    • Are the consent register (toestemmingsregister) and the consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) backend one system?
    • Which of them is the BSNk participant?

    The working assumption puts the BSNk calls at the register. The demo puts them at the backend. The TO removed the earlier requirement on this point (REQ-22) until a decision on Q-49.

    Proposed decision¶

    The proposal is route D, under the working assumption that MijnOverheid passes the BSN:

    • The consent facility recognizes the citizen by an HMAC of the BSN, with a secret, versioned key:
      • The key is in an HSM or KMS.
      • The input has a fixed prefix and nine digits with leading zeros.
      • The result is at least 128 bits.
      • Every record keeps the key version.
    • At the first consent, the service activates once at BSNk. It stores PI and PP under that reference. At a later consent, the service only lets BSNk transform values.
    • To show and revoke consents, the service needs no BSNk call.

    In the demo, the portal backend derives the reference and activates. The register stores PI and PP. This split fits only if both are one BSNk participant (Q-49).

    Considered options¶

    BSNk preconditions describes the routes in full. The design weighed four options:

    1. Route D: an own pseudonym from the BSN (proposed). BSNk is necessary only at the first activation. The route needs the BSN from MijnOverheid and a legal basis (grondslag) for the register.
    2. Route A: an own pseudonym through BSNk. The service activates and transforms at every login, also to show consents. Every login goes into the access register.
    3. Route B: a pseudonym through the login. MijnOverheid passes a VP for the register. The route depends on DigiD and MijnOverheid.
    4. Route C: a reference from MijnOverheid. MijnOverheid must have such a reference and must be allowed to pass it on.

    Consequences¶

    • The register stores PI and PP. It stores no BSN and no value per party (REQ-69, REQ-23). This deviates on purpose from FR-35, criterion 1 (F-98).
    • The service processes the BSN briefly at every login, and that needs a legal basis. For every BSN, the service can compute whether consents exist, without a trace elsewhere.
    • The secret key is the whole protection. Without the key, anyone can compute every reference back from the small BSN space.
    • A new key gives every citizen a new reference. A migration of existing records is not built (Q-56).
    • The consent facility must become a recognized BSNk participant (F-75, Q-26).

    These points are open:

    • Q-49: one system, and which participant.
    • Q-50: how the backend gets the verified identity.
    • Q-57: the protection of the stored PI and PP.
    • Q-58: does the register authenticate the backend?
    • Q-63: retention.

    When Q-49 has a decision, this ADR becomes accepted, or another route replaces it.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-20, REQ-23, REQ-24, REQ-40, REQ-69, BSNK-01, BSNK-02, BSNK-03, BSNK-10
    • Findings: F-75 (open), F-98 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-26 (open), Q-49 (open), Q-50 (open), Q-56 (open), Q-57 (open), Q-58 (open), Q-63 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-51 (done)

    ADR-0041: Seal format of ASI results¶

    • Status: proposed (waits for Q-32)
    • Date: 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569 article 9(4), as replaced by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735, from January 1, 2027, and S11
    • Deliberation: REQ-83, F-80, and demo ICTU/GBO-demo#498, PR #499
    • Implemented in: demo grade, with a development certificate:
      • The seal in seal.go#L18-L57.
      • The seal on successful responses only, in handler.go#L402-L417.
      • The header in the contract, in completions.json#L25-L33.
      • The validation by the reference QTSP, in qtsp-reference/internal/seal/seal.go.

    Context and problem statement¶

    From January 1, 2027, every verification result of an ASIP must be signed or sealed. The seal is at least an advanced electronic seal based on a qualified certificate. The certificate belongs to the responsible public sector body or to the designated intermediary (F-80). ETSI TS 119 478 defines no seal on the response (E4).

    A QTSP that verifies at several ASIPs must validate every seal in the same way. If each ASIP chooses its own format, every QTSP must implement each format. For this reason, the format is an interface agreement. It is not a choice per ASIP (REQ-83). Q-32 asks who decides the format. This ADR stays proposed until that decision.

    Proposed decision¶

    The proposal has five parts:

    1. The ASIP seals the exact response body with a detached JWS (RFC 7515, Appendix F). The JWS goes in the header X-JWS-Signature (<protected header>..<signature>).
    2. The algorithm is ES256. The protected header carries the certificate chain in x5c, leaf first.
    3. The body stays plain JSON, as the ETSI OpenAPI prescribes. The contract of the data service names the header as an addition.
    4. The ASIP seals every successful verify and retrieve response (200). An error response is not a verification result and gets no seal.
    5. The QTSP validates the signature over the received body, and the chain against its trust anchors. The QTSP does not accept a result without a valid seal.

    Consequences¶

    • With only the response and the trusted lists, the QTSP can establish that the response comes unchanged from this ASIP.
    • The format works with any HTTP client. It leaves the ETSI response schema unchanged.
    • The demo seals with a development certificate. Production needs a qualified certificate for electronic seals (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1943, Annex II). The certificate has the registration number of the organization as organizationIdentifier.
    • It is open who holds that certificate: the bronhouder, or the designated intermediary (Q-17, Q-28).

    Considered options¶

    • A detached JWS in a header (proposed). It is simple for a JSON API. The body stays as ETSI specifies.
    • A JAdES baseline signature (ETSI TS 119 182-1). This is the EU format for JSON signatures, with the signing time and the certificate references in the header. It is more work for the QTSP and the ASIP, but it is closer to the eIDAS ecosystem.
    • An enveloping JWS, with the result as the JWS payload. This option changes the response form that the ETSI OpenAPI prescribes.

    Open points¶

    These points are open:

    • Who decides the format for all Dutch ASIPs, and does ETSI ESI add it to TS 119 478 (Q-32, E4)?
    • Does every source response get one seal, regardless of the channel (DvTP, EUDI, ASI) (Q-75)?

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-83, REQ-94
    • Findings: F-80 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-17, Q-28, Q-32, Q-75
    • Standards feedback: E4
    • Demo increments: SL-28

    ADR-0042: Optional per-attribute token binding for ASI tokens¶

    • Status: proposed (waits for Q-33)
    • Date: 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569 article 9(5) (a member state can impose access control), S11, P-02
    • Deliberation: REQ-103, F-95, and demo PR #559, ICTU/GBO-demo#571, PR #572
    • Implemented in:
      • The check at the authorization server in authorization_details.go#L31-L79.
      • The request page in pages.go#L109-L111.
      • The token in tokens.go#L70-L72.
      • The mandatory switch in main.go#L109.
      • The check at the ASIP in accesstoken.go#L177-L197 and handler.go#L346-L356.

    Context and problem statement¶

    ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1.3.2 binds an access token per operation only (verify, retrieve). With one token, the QTSP can ask every attribute of the data service, also when the citizen approved something else (F-95, E5). Article 9(5) of Implementing Regulation 2025/1569 lets a member state impose access control. Q-33 asks whether the Netherlands imposes a binding per attribute. This ADR stays proposed until that decision.

    Proposed decision¶

    The proposal has four parts:

    1. A QTSP can name the attributes in the authorization request as one RFC 9396 authorization_details entry. The entry has the provisional type https://gbo.example/authorization-details/authentic-source-attributes. The entry has these fields:
      • locations, equal to resource.
      • actions, equal to the scope.
      • attribute_identifiers, with 1 to 50 unique https URIs.
    2. The authorization server validates the entry against the data service and the scope. It refuses an invalid entry with invalid_request. It shows the attributes on the request page and puts the entry unchanged in the token.
    3. If the token carries the entry, the ASIP refuses a request for another attribute with 401 insufficient_scope.
    4. By default, the binding is optional, so a QTSP that implements only ETSI can connect. Without the entry, the authorization is per operation, and the description of the data service is the limit. A configuration switch makes the entry mandatory (AZSP_REQUIRE_AUTHORIZATION_DETAILS=true in the demo).

    Consequences¶

    • With the binding, the citizen sees exactly which attributes the QTSP asks (REQ-91). The token is not valid for other attributes.
    • Only parties that know the GBO type can use the binding. The type identifier is provisional.
    • If the Netherlands makes the binding mandatory, QTSPs that implement only ETSI cannot connect. This stays so until ETSI or a national profile defines the extension.

    Considered options¶

    The proposal considered three other options:

    • A binding per operation only, as ETSI specifies. This option is simpler for QTSPs, but the token is wider than the approval.
    • A mandatory binding per attribute. This option is closer to P-02. But it excludes QTSPs that implement only ETSI, until the extension is standard.
    • Attributes in the scope string. Not chosen. ETSI fixes the scopes, and RFC 9396 is the standard place for structured detail.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-91, REQ-95, REQ-103
    • Findings: F-95 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-33
    • Standards feedback: E5
    • Demo increments: SL-28

    ADR-0043: Keep identifiers out of the PDP input instead of masking decision logs¶

    • Status: proposed (waits for demo #368)
    • Date: 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: P-04, P-02, S09
    • Deliberation: REQ-60, F-54, and demo #149, #364, #368, CHANGELOG
    • Implemented in: not implemented. The plain BSN enters the PDP input at eudi-adapter source_metadata.go and asi-provider graphqlsource/source.go.

    Context and problem statement¶

    Logging must hold no BSN that the processing does not need (REQ-60). Two decision logs record the PDP input: the ADL and the console decision log (ADR-0036). The routes differ:

    • In the consent route, the PDP input holds a placeholder and no identifier (ADR-0032). This route meets the requirement.
    • In the EUDI and ASI routes, the query variables hold the plain BSN from the PID or the token. As a result, both decision logs hold the BSN.

    Masking in the policy engine had no effect (F-54). The demo then kept the BSN out through the construction of the input: the request mapper pseudonymized the BSN through BSNk. The demo removed that step when the mapper became a pure mapper (#364). The demo accepts the BSN in both logs until #368 decides between masking and "transform first".

    Proposed decision¶

    The proposal has three parts:

    • A component that builds PDP input leaves out or replaces every identifying value that the decision does not need.
    • If the component cannot do that, the request does not continue.
    • Masking in the engine or in the log pipeline is a second line only, with a continuous test on the real log output.

    Why proposed, not accepted¶

    In demo v0.9.0, the input side gives no guarantee. If the team picks masking in #368, REQ-60 must change, because it says "never rely only on masking".

    Considered options¶

    1. Keep identifiers out of the input (proposed). The PDP never receives the value, so no log can hold it.
    2. Mask the decision logs. The value still reaches the engine. A change in the log shape can leak the value again without notice, as F-54 showed.
    3. Transform the BSN to a pseudonym before the PDP, as the earlier mapper did. This option needs a BSNk call in the decision path, and no rule reads the result.

    Consequences¶

    • If the proposal is accepted, the EUDI adapter and the ASIP must build their PDP input without the BSN. The source still needs the BSN after the allow. For this reason, the value must reach the source another way, as in the consent route (ADR-0033).
    • LDV records never hold a BSN. The logbook refuses any record with a run of nine digits that passes the BSN checksum (elfproef) (ADR-0026). This ADR covers the decision logs only.
    • Until a decision on #368, the BSN in the EUDI and ASI decision logs is a known risk (Risks and technical debt).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-60, REQ-71, REQ-20
    • Findings: F-54 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-08 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-29 (done)

    Deferred

    ADR-0022: Sector-level grants with organizational attribute verification¶

    • Status: deferred
    • Date: 2026-08-24 (proposed), deferred on 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: S04, P-16
    • Deliberation: reference architecture v0.6.2, authorization models analysis §9.5 (archived and unpublished), F-36, SL-05
    • Implemented in: not implemented. gbo-demo removed the sector-pip scaffolding (#378, CHANGELOG).

    Why deferred¶

    In gbo-demo v0.9.0, admission runs through the admission register (toelatingsregister) and the contract decision of the PDP (REQ-61, ADR-0015). No component called the sector PIP, so the demo removed it. A sector grant is not a native FSC concept (F-36). The proposal stays in the log for one case: per-organization admission does not scale. Work on it starts only after a new decision.

    Context and problem statement¶

    PKI proves which organization calls (OIN). PKI does not prove what kind of organization it is. Per-organization contracts do not scale to sectors. For example, 800 notary offices need 800 contracts with each source.

    Proposed decision (deferred)¶

    The proposal extends contract acceptance and token issuance with organizational attributes:

    • Sector PIPs (KvK SBI, KNB, BIG, AFM) verify sector membership.
    • A sector-level grant type expresses "this sector may use this service".
    • The access token carries verified sector claims.

    This proposal builds on contract acceptance by policy (ADR-0015). The autosign input then must carry more than peer IDs.

    Open points¶

    The proposal leaves three points open:

    • An extension of the FSC grant schema, through the Logius standards process.
    • The freshness of sector register data, and the liability for it.
    • The relation with the admission register: admission versus membership.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-61, REQ-62
    • Findings: F-36 (resolved in demo), F-56 (closed)
    • Open questions: none
    • Demo increments: SL-05 (done)

    Superseded

    ADR-0006: Consent register as runtime PIP¶

    • Status: superseded by ADR-0007, which ADR-0032 supersedes in turn
    • Date: 2026-08-24 (ported from reference architecture v0.6.2)
    • Satisfies: S01, P-01
    • Deliberation: Reference architecture v0.6.2, decision 2, and its DvTP PBAC alignment proposal (archived and unpublished)
    • Implemented in: superseded before implementation

    Context and problem statement¶

    DvTP draft v0.1 authorized requests through a custom gateway that checked consent twice. GBO replaces this gateway with the standard PEP-PDP chain. Then the question is how the consent evidence gets to the decision.

    Decision (superseded)¶

    A register records the consent and acts as a Policy Information Point (PIP). For each request, the PDP looks up the consent by consent_id. The consent proof that the service provider (dienstverlener) receives is an opaque reference.

    Why it was superseded¶

    With a pure lookup, the authorization evidence depends only on the availability and integrity of the register. The consumer gives the PDP nothing that the PDP can verify.

    The implemented design keeps the register and its status check for revocation on each request. But the consent itself becomes a signed artifact that the consumer presents and that the PDP can verify. For this design, see ADR-0007.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-68, REQ-18
    • Findings: F-24 (resolved in demo)
    • Open questions: Q-05 (answered), Q-23 (closed)
    • Demo increments: SL-08 (done)

    ADR-0007: Consent as a signed token with a live status check¶

    • Status: superseded by ADR-0032
    • Date: 2026-08-24 (superseded 2026-11-02)
    • Satisfies: S01, S02, P-01
    • Supersedes: ADR-0006
    • Superseded by: ADR-0032
    • Deliberation: signed, actor-bound consent proof (PR #238, SL-47)
    • Implemented in: changed in gbo-demo. Since PR #469, the token does not carry pi. Verification moved from the request mapper into the policy (#330, PR #371). The status goes over FSC (#383).

    Why superseded¶

    The demo changed three parts of this decision:

    • The token carries no PI. It carries an encrypted value for each source (encrypted_subject). The consumer names the citizen with a placeholder (SL-51).
    • The policy verifies the token and gets the status itself. The request mapper only maps.
    • The PDP asks for the status over FSC, through its own Outway, and not directly at the register.

    For this reason, ADR-0032 records the consent proof again. The signed token, the live status check for each request, and the bearer-token consequence stay. The following sections keep the original decision as history.

    Context and problem statement¶

    The PDP needs consent evidence that it can verify and that can be revoked. The evidence must work without exposing the BSN. Also, one consent must cover more than one bronhouder.

    Decision (superseded)¶

    The consent register (toestemmingsregister) issues an ES256-signed JWT of type gbo-consent+jwt with these claims:

    • consent_id
    • pi
    • scopes
    • scope_entries (per bronhouder)
    • dienstverlener_oin
    • valid_until (= exp)

    The service provider (dienstverlener) presents the token in the X-Gbo-Consent-Token header. For each request, the PDP does three things:

    1. It verifies the signature against the JWKS of the register.
    2. It cross-checks the claims.
    3. It gets the live status of exactly that consent_id. Thus a revocation takes effect immediately.

    The register stores no BSN and no PI.

    Consequences (at the time)¶

    • The decision binds to verified claims:
      • actor binding (subject.id == dienstverlener_oin)
      • subject binding (the PI in the query equals the PI in the token)
      • scope and year coverage
    • The token is a bearer token. Actor binding blocks use by another consumer. It does not block replay by the same consumer. Production needs a shorter validity and a proof-of-possession binding to the FSC identity. Risks and technical debt tracks this.
    • The register stays a runtime dependency only for the status check. This check fails closed (CONSENT_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-68, REQ-79
    • Findings: F-04 (closed), F-44 (resolved in demo)
    • Open questions: Q-05 (answered)
    • Demo increments: SL-23 (done), SL-47 (done), SL-51 (done)

    ADR-0008: Service catalog as a data-driven policy ceiling¶

    • Status: superseded by ADR-0009
    • Date: 2026-08-24 (ported from reference architecture v0.6.2)
    • Satisfies: P-02, GO: service catalog
    • Deliberation: Reference architecture v0.6.2, decision 3 (archived and unpublished)
    • Implemented in: superseded before implementation

    Context and problem statement¶

    GBO needs a ceiling that applies to all individual consents. The ceiling limits what a consent screen can ask for and what a query can select.

    Decision (superseded)¶

    GBO keeps a statutory service catalog (dienstencatalogus) as a separate register with a legal anchor. The register maps each scope to its allowed fields (data.dienstencatalogus[scope].allowed_fields). The PDP checks every query against the catalog. The consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) shows only catalog entries.

    Why it was superseded¶

    A separate catalog is a second authorization source. It can drift away from the rules that enforce it. The implemented model puts the ceiling into the rules themselves: the coverage declarations in closed-world rules are the catalog (ADR-0009).

    The question of the legal anchor stays open: a catalog based on a general administrative order (AMvB), with its own governance. Risks and technical debt tracks this question.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-08, REQ-121
    • Findings: F-21 (closed), F-23 (closed), F-38 (closed)
    • Open questions: none
    • Demo increments: SL-14 (done)

    ADR-0010: BSN resolution inside the PEP¶

    • Status: superseded by ADR-0011, which ADR-0033 supersedes in turn
    • Date: 2026-08-24 (ported from reference architecture v0.6.2)
    • Satisfies: P-04
    • Deliberation: Reference architecture v0.6.2, decision 4 (archived and unpublished)
    • Implemented in: superseded before implementation

    Context and problem statement¶

    After the PDP allows a pseudonymous DvTP request, a component must resolve the pseudonym to the BSN. The API of the source requires the BSN.

    Decision (superseded)¶

    The PEP intercepts the query of the consumer. After the policy decision, the PEP resolves consent_id → PI → BSNk Transform → BSN. Then it puts the BSN into the internal query of the bronhouder.

    Why it was superseded¶

    With this decision, the PEP becomes a middlebox that transforms data. Also, a component with BSN authorization sits in shared infrastructure.

    In the implemented design, the PEP (the FSC Inway) only enforces decisions. The source owns the identifier resolution. For this design, see ADR-0011.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-21, BSNK-04
    • Findings: F-30 (resolved in demo), F-37 (resolved in demo)
    • Open questions: none
    • Demo increments: SL-02 (done)

    ADR-0011: Source-owned sidecar resolves pseudonyms, and the PDP never sees a BSN¶

    • Status: superseded by ADR-0033
    • Date: 2026-08-24 (superseded 2026-11-02)
    • Satisfies: P-04, P-10
    • Supersedes: ADR-0010
    • Superseded by: ADR-0033
    • Deliberation: source gateway de-pseudonymization (SL-22, F-30)
    • Implemented in: changed in gbo-demo. The source gateway does not call BSNk and does not read subject_id_type any more (PR #469, #473). The request mapper does not pseudonymize any more (#364). Code in gbo-demo v0.9.0: services/bron-sidecar

    Why superseded¶

    The mechanism changed in three places:

    • The source gateway does not call BSNk Transform at query time. It takes the value for its own OIN from the consent proof. The decryption component of the source reads this value.
    • The source gateway acts when a consent proof is present. The demo removed the subject_id_type grant property (ADR-0031).
    • The PDP request mapper does not pseudonymize a disclosed BSN any more. In the EUDI and ASI routes, the PDP input holds the plain BSN (ADR-0043, proposed). So the claim "the PDP never sees a BSN" in the title is true only for the consent route.

    For this reason, ADR-0033 records the mechanism again. The resolution by the source after the allow stays. The following sections keep the original decision as history.

    Context and problem statement¶

    A component between the allow decision and the source API must resolve the pseudonym to the BSN. Shared infrastructure must not get BSN authorization. The BSN must not leak into policy inputs or logs.

    Decision (superseded)¶

    A source gateway that the source owns sits between the Inway and the GraphQL API. The source gateway does the resolution. It reads the subject_id_type claim from the FSC access token:

    • For pseudonym, it transforms the PI to the BSN through BSNk, with its own OIN. Then it substitutes the query variable.
    • For direct, it passes the request through.

    In addition, the PDP request mapper pseudonymizes any disclosed BSN (EUDI flows) before policy evaluation. So the engine input and the decision log contain only the PI.

    Consequences (at the time)¶

    • Each role stays separate, in line with data sovereignty:
      • The PEP stays a pure enforcement point.
      • The PDP does no data transformation.
      • Only the bronhouder holds BSN authority.
    • The meaning of the identifier is a grant property that both peers countersign (ADR-0030). So a caller cannot choose how the source interprets its subject identifier.
    • A pseudonym that cannot be resolved is a hard error (HTTP 400). The fail-safe default is pass-through (direct).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-21, REQ-60
    • Findings: F-30 (resolved in demo), F-37 (resolved in demo), F-54 (open)
    • Open questions: none
    • Demo increments: SL-02 (done), SL-22 (done), SL-29 (done)

    ADR-0012: Query AST inspection with OPA's graphql.parse_query¶

    • Status: superseded by ADR-0013
    • Date: 2026-08-24 (ported from reference architecture v0.6.2)
    • Satisfies: P-02
    • Deliberation: Reference architecture v0.6.2, component architecture "GraphQL schema registry and scope-driven field authorization", and its GraphQL + PBAC proposal (archived and unpublished)
    • Implemented in: superseded before implementation

    Context and problem statement¶

    For authorization per field, the PDP must read the structure of the incoming GraphQL query, in addition to its metadata.

    Decision (superseded)¶

    Rego parses the query with the built-in OPA function graphql.parse_query(). The policy code then walks the AST. This follows the nID/iWlz production pattern.

    Why it was superseded¶

    If Rego walks a raw AST, the parsing mechanics go into every rule. Rego also cannot resolve parent types, verify consent proofs, or pseudonymize identifiers.

    The implemented design moves the request preparation into a mapper inside the PDP service, before policy evaluation. The rules then use clean facts for each field. For this design, see ADR-0013. The intent stays the same: the query is the authorization object.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-17
    • Findings: F-25 (closed)
    • Open questions: Q-14 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-03a (done)

    ADR-0014: Flow and subject identifier semantics through a provider-side Additional Claims service¶

    • Status: superseded by ADR-0030, which ADR-0031 supersedes in turn
    • Date: 2026-08-24
    • Satisfies: P-01, D-11
    • Deliberation: gbo-demo CHANGELOG, v0.6.11, F-62
    • Implemented in: removed from gbo-demo in v0.6.11 (September 2026)

    Context and problem statement¶

    The PDP selects rules by the flow of the request (dvtp:query, eudi:attestation, gbo:source-metadata). The source gateway interprets the subject identifier (pseudonym or direct). If callers supply these values as headers, a caller can choose the authorization regime that applies to its request.

    Decision (superseded)¶

    An Additional Claims service that the provider owned mapped each validated connection grant (outway peer, service peer, service name) to an add claim object. The FSC Manager of the provider signed this object into the access token. The PDP mapper and the source gateway read only the add claim.

    Why it was superseded¶

    The mechanism was a workaround for a version limit. The simulation environment ran OpenFSC v1.44, which is older than grant properties. The mechanism had two costs:

    • Only the provider signed the regime. The consumer never countersigned it.
    • The mapping file from grants to claims was outside the contracts. People had to maintain it by hand, and it broke twice during the Peer-ID migration.

    When OpenFSC v2.4.0 became available, the regime moved into the contract itself, as FSC-normative grant properties. For this design, see ADR-0030.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-74
    • Findings: F-32 (resolved in demo), F-45 (closed), F-62 (resolved in demo)
    • Open questions: Q-15 (answered)
    • Demo increments: SL-48 (done)

    ADR-0019: FSC transaction ID as the end-to-end correlation key¶

    • Status: superseded by ADR-0035
    • Date: 2026-08-24 (superseded 2026-11-02)
    • Satisfies: P-12, S09
    • Superseded by: ADR-0035
    • Deliberation: OBSERVABILITY.md, FSC txlog observability (SL-38)
    • Implemented in: changed in gbo-demo (PR #366). If no traceparent arrives, entry components still tie the trace to the transaction ID: consumerhttp.go, eudi-adapter/main.go. Txlog viewer: fsctxlog.go

    Why superseded¶

    If the two IDs are equal, the design breaks in three cases (F-67):

    • A caller sends its own traceparent.
    • One processing calls more than one source.
    • The request passes an extra FSC hop.

    LDV and the ADL require that a component takes over the trace ID unchanged. FSC-Logging gives every transaction its own ID. Also, FSC forwards traceparent on the data path. Only the AuthZEN call from the Inway to the PDP drops it (F-41).

    ADR-0035 makes W3C Trace Context the correlation key and records the transaction ID next to it. One part stays: an entry component without an incoming traceparent can tie its trace to the transaction ID that it mints. The following sections keep the original decision as history.

    Context and problem statement¶

    FSC does not propagate W3C trace context across the Inway. As a result, the trace of a consumer and the records on the provider side carry unrelated identifiers.

    Decision (superseded)¶

    Consumers generate a UUIDv7. They use it as the Fsc-Transaction-Id and also as the OpenTelemetry trace ID. The PDP records it in every decision log line. The FSC transaction logs of every hop carry it natively.

    Consequences (at the time)¶

    • One identifier links the consumer request, the policy decision, and the audit record of each hop. A deny reason can be traced to the exact exchange.
    • Debug stores (Jaeger, Loki) keep data only for a short time. The FSC txlog stays the authoritative record. For more information, see Logging and traceability.
    • If a later FSC version supports trace-context propagation, GBO can change this convention without breaking the txlog linkage.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-55
    • Findings: F-39 (resolved in demo), F-41 (resolved in demo), F-67 (resolved in demo)
    • Open questions: none
    • Demo increments: SL-07 (done), SL-38 (done)

    ADR-0029: Authentic Source Interface per ETSI TS 119 478¶

    • Status: superseded by ADR-0037
    • Date: 2026-08-24, superseded on 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: eIDAS Article 45e, GO: verification and retrieval service for QTSPs, PSA open decisions: central verification and retrieval service
    • Superseded by: ADR-0037
    • Deliberation: reference architecture v0.6.2, gap 8 and ASI design (archived and unpublished)
    • Implemented in: not implemented in this form. The built route is ADR-0037.

    Why superseded¶

    The demo built the Authentic Source Interface after this ADR (SL-28). Three core points of this proposal changed:

    • Retrieve is implemented. The ASIP offers clause 6.1.2 next to 6.1.1. EUDI issuance does not replace retrieve, because the QTSP issues the QEAA, and GBO does not (REQ-101, REQ-112).
    • The QTSP is outside FSC. This proposal saw the ASI as a protocol adapter "in front of" the FSC chain. The ASI is an OAuth front door with its own trust model. The authorization server admits the QTSP, and the PDP does not. The generic chain starts behind the ASIP, which is an FSC peer of its own (F-87).

    • Clause numbers replace the labels I1 to I5. The labels came from the reference architecture:

      • I1 is clause 5 (discovery).
      • I2 is 6.1.1 (verify).
      • I3 is 6.1.2 (retrieve).
      • I4 is 6.1.3 (authorization server).
      • I5 is citizen identification inside 6.1.3.

      The TO uses the ETSI clause numbers and roles.

    ADR-0037 records the decision that replaces this ADR. ADR-0038, ADR-0039, ADR-0041, and ADR-0042 record the details. The following sections hold the original proposal as history.

    Context and problem statement¶

    Article 45e of the amended eIDAS regulation obliges member states to let QTSPs verify attributes against authentic sources at the request of the user. ETSI TS 119 478 specifies the interfaces. Without this interface, QTSPs cannot issue QEAAs based on Dutch government registers.

    Proposed decision¶

    The proposal builds the ASI provider as a GBO edge service, in the HTTP/OAuth variant:

    • Implement I2 (Verify). The service translates verification requests into GraphQL queries over FSC, through the standard PEP-PDP chain, and compares the values.
    • Implement I4 and I5: citizen authorization through OAuth, with a wallet or eID.
    • Skip I3 (Retrieve), because the EUDI chain covers direct issuance (ADR-0018).
    • Register the data services in the EU catalogue of attributes (I1).

    Open points¶

    The proposal left these points open:

    • The PDP policy set for QTSP verification (Trusted List check, citizen authorization, attribute scope).
    • The design of the authorization server (I4), and its relation to the consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening).
    • The timeline pressure from the Article 45e deadline. For more information, see Risks and technical debt.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-101, REQ-112
    • Findings: F-80 (open), F-87 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-28

    ADR-0030: Flow and subject identifier semantics as FSC grant properties¶

    • Status: superseded by ADR-0031
    • Date: 2026-09-07, superseded on 2026-11-02
    • Satisfies: P-01, D-11, D-08
    • Supersedes: ADR-0014
    • Superseded by: ADR-0031
    • Deliberation: gbo-demo CHANGELOG, v0.6.11, and issues #244, #277, #279
    • Implemented in: removed from gbo-demo. #334 removed the flow property (PR #363). #473 removed the subject_id_type property (PR #475). In gbo-demo v0.9.0, the seeds create grants without properties (CHANGELOG).

    Why superseded¶

    The regime does not need a declaration. The regime follows from the evidence that the request carries (ADR-0031):

    • A consent proof puts the request in the consent regime.
    • A request without a consent proof is in the PID regime.

    After that change, no component read the flow property. The subject_id_type property also lost its reader. The source gateway takes the subject from the consent proof, and not from the contract (ADR-0033). The demo removed both properties. The following sections hold the original decision as history.

    Context and problem statement¶

    The PDP judges a request under an authorization regime. The regime has two parts: the flow, and the way to read the subject identifier (subject_id_type). The regime must be bound to the connection and signed, and the caller must not control it. ADR-0014 describes the mechanism that this ADR replaced.

    Decision (superseded)¶

    The decision put flow and subject_id_type as properties in the GRANT_TYPE_SERVICE_CONNECTION grant of the FSC contract (fsc-core, section Properties). It worked as follows:

    • The properties are inside the grant, so they are part of the grant hash. Both peers countersign the regime when they sign the contract.
    • The Manager of the provider puts the properties in the access token, as the FSC-normative prp claim.
    • The PDP request mapper reads the flow from prp only. It uses no header and no default.
    • If a token has no prp, the flow is empty. An empty flow matches no rule, so the PDP denies with NO_APPLICABLE_RULE.
    • The source gateway reads subject_id_type from the same claim.

    The demo seeded three property sets:

    Contract Properties
    EDI issuer → data services (bri, brp) {"flow": "eudi:attestation", "subject_id_type": "direct"}
    Mortgage lender (Hypotheek-BV) → bri {"flow": "dvtp:query", "subject_id_type": "pseudonym"}
    EDI issuer → metadata services {"flow": "gbo:source-metadata"} (not subject-bound)

    Consequences (at the time)¶

    The decision had these consequences:

    • The provider needed no mapping file and no extra service. The contract was the single source of truth for the regime.
    • Contracts are immutable, so a regime change meant a new contract. The seed scripts matched on properties and moved the grant link to the new contract.
    • Every peer on a contract needed OpenFSC 2.0 or later. If the contract of a peer carried no properties, the PDP denied the peer until a new seed.
    • If subject_id_type was missing, the fail-safe default of the source gateway was direct (pass-through). If the flow was missing, the default of the PDP was deny. This difference was safe, because the PDP decided first.

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-74
    • Findings: F-32 (resolved in demo), F-43 (superseded), F-62 (resolved in demo), F-70 (open)
    • Open questions: Q-15 (answered)
    • Demo increments: SL-24 (dropped), SL-48 (done)

    Quality requirements¶

    The scenarios on this page refine the quality goals and make them testable. The scenarios use the IDs QS-01 to QS-52. The Q-NN IDs belong to the open questions.

    The column "Pinned by" links the test in gbo-demo v0.9.0 that holds the scenario. "Not pinned" means that no automated test holds the scenario. In that case, the scenario is an acceptance criterion for future work, or it fails in demo v0.9.0. If a scenario fails in demo v0.9.0, its expected outcome says so.

    Reason codes have two layers (Reason codes). The consumer and the ADL get a client code, for example FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED. The operator gets the rule code per field in the console decision log, for example YEAR_NOT_COVERED. Each scenario names the code at the layer where the test checks it.

    Data minimization and authorization¶

    The following scenarios test data minimization and authorization:

    # Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by
    QS-01 A consumer asks for a field that no rule covers, for example box2Inkomen next to permitted income fields Deny. Rule code NO_APPLICABLE_RULE for that field. No data leaves the source. engine_test.rego#L210
    QS-02 A query asks for a year that the citizen did not give consent for Deny. Rule code YEAR_NOT_COVERED. dvt0001_test.rego#L167
    QS-03 A query has no year filter Deny (fail closed). dvt0001_test.rego#L172
    QS-04 The mapper cannot prove the field list because of a parse error, an exceeded limit (depth 64, 100 fragments, 1 MiB body), or an unknown schema Deny. Client code COVERAGE_UNVERIFIABLE with a subcode. A mutation or subscription gives OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED. engine_test.rego#L117
    QS-05 A request carries a consent proof, or carries none With a consent proof, only consent-regime rules judge the request. Without one, only PID-regime rules judge it (REQ-74). engine_test.rego#L227, #L234
    QS-06 The actor list of a PID rule contains a consent consumer The test fails. The lists stay disjoint. The test knows only the local consumers (F-70, R21). engine_test.rego#L371 (local consumers only)
    QS-07 A rule for service brp meets a request on service bri The rule does not bind, and the field gets NO_APPLICABLE_RULE. Every rule names its services (REQ-97). engine_test.rego#L397, #L497
    QS-08 The PDP gets a schema for a service whose digest the bundle does not pin Deny. engine_test.rego#L108
    QS-09 A consumer gets a deny The consumer sees only the client code. This code names no field and no rule code (REQ-06). engine_test.rego#L29

    Consent integrity¶

    The following scenarios test the integrity of consent:

    # Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by
    QS-10 The citizen revokes a consent between grant and use The PDP denies the next request. Rule code CONSENT_WITHDRAWN (REQ-14). consent_test.rego#L202
    QS-11 A forged or tampered consent token reaches the PDP Deny. Rule code CONSENT_SIGNATURE_INVALID. consent_test.rego#L318, #L324
    QS-12 A consumer other than the one in the consent presents a valid consent proof Deny. Rule code CONSENT_ACTOR_MISMATCH. dvt0001_test.rego#L84
    QS-13 The status service of the register does not answer Deny (fail closed). Rule code CONSENT_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE, and the consumer sees ACCESS_DENIED. consent_test.rego#L303
    QS-14 A consumer puts a literal BSN in the query under a valid consent Deny. Rule code CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH (REQ-79). dvt0001_test.rego#L131
    QS-15 A request carries two consent proofs Deny. The PDP picks neither proof. Rule code CONSENT_CONTEXT_INVALID. consent_test.rego#L438
    QS-16 A citizen revokes an expired or already revoked consent The backend refuses the revocation with CONSENT_NOT_REVOCABLE (REQ-109). Fails in demo v0.9.0: the backend answers 200 (#600, R31). Not pinned

    Admission and integrators¶

    The following scenarios test admission and integrators:

    # Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by
    QS-17 A suspended participant submits an FSC contract The contract stays proposed. Reason PARTY_NOT_ACTIVE. autosign_test.rego#L138
    QS-18 A participant asks for a source outside its allowed_source_peer_ids The contract stays proposed. Reason SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED. autosign_test.rego#L109
    QS-19 The admission register is missing from the PDP data The contract stays proposed. Reason ADMISSION_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE. The reason is not "party unknown". autosign_test.rego#L86
    QS-20 An integrator proposes a delegated contract for a provider for which it has no registered integration The contract stays proposed. Reason DELEGATION_NOT_REGISTERED. autosign_test.rego#L176
    QS-21 An integrator calls for a provider without a mandate, or the register is unavailable Deny. Rule code INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED, or INTEGRATOR_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE (REQ-106). engine_test.rego#L621, #L631
    QS-22 A suspended consumer with an existing contract sends a query under a valid consent Deny (REQ-110). Fails in demo v0.9.0: the request passes until the contract is revoked. Not pinned

    Privacy¶

    The following scenarios test privacy:

    # Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by
    QS-23 A DvTP consumer asks for income data under a consent The consumer request names the subject with the placeholder consent:identity. The request, the PDP input, and the ADL hold no citizen identifier (REQ-20). consumer_test.go#L86
    QS-24 The proof carries a value made for another OIN The source gateway refuses the value and does not forward the request (REQ-80). substitution_test.go#L112
    QS-25 A consumer tries to reach a source gateway or a source API directly Unreachable (REQ-81). Partly met in demo v0.9.0: Docker Compose isolates the gateways, but the source APIs share networks with consumers (R25). Not pinned (manual check of the gateways, October 5, 2026)
    QS-26 A consent record is read from the register The record holds no BSN and no per-party value. The register keeps PI and PP under the subject_ref of the portal, and no consent answer carries them (REQ-69). polymorphic_test.go#L39, #L85
    QS-27 Two sources get values for the same citizen The values differ per recipient and cannot be linked. Not demonstrated in demo v0.9.0: the BSNk mock does not encrypt, and the demo sources share one OIN. Not pinned
    QS-28 An EUDI or ASI request reaches the PDP The PDP input and both decision logs hold no BSN (REQ-60). Fails in demo v0.9.0 (#368, R22). Not pinned
    QS-29 A component writes an LDV record that contains a valid BSN anywhere The logbook refuses the record. validate_test.go#L94

    Traceability and audit¶

    The following scenarios test traceability and audit:

    # Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by
    QS-30 A caller sends both traceparent and Fsc-Transaction-Id The component takes the trace ID from traceparent. The transaction ID is recorded next to it (REQ-55). tracecontext_test.go#L100
    QS-31 An auditor reads all processing records of one request Each logbook returns the records of that trace (REQ-72). logbook_test.go#L180
    QS-32 The logbook is unavailable while a request runs The request is served. Later, the outbox delivers the record once (REQ-72). outbox_test.go#L86, #L119
    QS-33 An auditor holds a transaction ID and looks for the ADL record The ADL record carries the trace ID and the transaction ID (REQ-71). Partly met in demo v0.9.0: behind the FSC Inway, the record has neither. The reader finds the record through the stored request header (#369, R23). Not pinned (code: adl.go#L49-L66)
    QS-34 An auditor asks which policy version made the decision The ADL record names the policy version (REQ-59). Fails in demo v0.9.0. Not pinned
    QS-35 A citizen asks which parties processed data under one consent The answer is available per consent. Partly met in demo v0.9.0: each controller can answer from its logbook, but the citizen view per consent is not built (R19). Not pinned

    EUDI issuance¶

    The following scenarios test EUDI issuance:

    # Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by
    QS-36 A caller outside the designated issuers asks for an attestation Deny. Rule code ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED. eud0001_test.rego#L65
    QS-37 A caller posts a BSN to the adapter callback without the issuance server Refused (REQ-45). Fails in demo v0.9.0: the callback is unauthenticated (#133, R5). Not pinned
    QS-38 A source has no certificate set Only that source is blocked. Other sources keep working (REQ-58). service_test.go#L130
