    QS-40 A published Type Metadata version is fetched twice The responses are byte-identical, and vct#integrity matches. type_metadata_test.go#L17

    Authentic Source Interface¶

    The following scenarios test the Authentic Source Interface:

    # Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by
    QS-41 A QTSP uses a token issued for another data service 401. A token is valid for one data service only (REQ-95). dataservices_test.go#L16
    QS-42 A request has no DPoP proof, or replays one 401. token_test.go#L158, #L200
    QS-43 A request asks for an attribute outside the approved authorization_details 401 insufficient_scope (REQ-103). token_test.go#L217
    QS-44 A verify or retrieve succeeds The body is sealed with a detached JWS in X-JWS-Signature. Errors are not sealed (REQ-83). handler_test.go#L238
    QS-45 A verify gives Match The response carries no value from the source (REQ-85). handler_test.go#L108
    QS-46 The source holds no value, or the chain fails No value gives Unknown. A failed chain gives an error, never Unknown (REQ-84, REQ-93). handler_test.go#L140, source_test.go#L141
    QS-47 A retrieve asks for an attribute for which the source has no value 404. No partial result (REQ-101). handler_test.go#L291
    QS-48 A QTSP reads the discovery records of the ASIP Each record leads to the data service endpoint, its contract, and the authorization server metadata (REQ-99, REQ-100). discovery_test.go#L66, #L105
    QS-49 A QTSP without QEAA_Provider in the register registers, or loses the entitlement later Registration refused (unapproved_software_statement). After a withdrawal, the next re-check deactivates the client (REQ-88, REQ-89). If the register is unreachable, the client stays active (R27). registration_test.go#L152, #L276, #L306
    QS-50 The wallet returns on the same device but in another browser Refused before the verifier is asked. wallet_test.go#L123
    QS-51 An FSC peer other than the ASIP asks for BRP personal data under the PID regime Deny. Rule code ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED. ASI0001 judges service brp only. asi0001_test.rego#L29, #L56
    QS-52 The QTSP holds the access token The QTSP cannot read the BSN (F-86). Fails in demo v0.9.0 (#595, R26). Not pinned

    The ETSI conformance matrix etsi-ts-119478.yaml gives each ETSI TS 119 478 requirement a status and the tests that hold it. The CI check fails in each of these cases:

    • A requirement ID has no entry.
    • A status lacks what it requires.
    • A named test does not exist.

    One entry has the status failing: fuzzy matching against a response without a value (R30).

    Open quality targets¶

    Availability, capacity, and performance targets have no scenarios in this version of the TO. By design, the demo runs one instance of each component. For more information, see the availability model. Two targets are open:

    • The volumes that the chain must handle (Q-47).
    • The propagation time, availability, and latency of the consent status (REQ-75). The register is a dependency of every DvTP decision (R10).

    Traceability¶

    • Requirements: REQ-06, REQ-14, REQ-20, REQ-45, REQ-55, REQ-58, REQ-59, REQ-60, REQ-66, REQ-69, REQ-71, REQ-72, REQ-74, REQ-75, REQ-79, REQ-80, REQ-81, REQ-83 to REQ-89, REQ-93, REQ-95, REQ-97, REQ-99 to REQ-103, REQ-106, REQ-109, REQ-110
    • Findings: F-70 (open), F-79 (open), F-86 (open), F-90 (resolved in demo)
    • Open questions: Q-47 (open)
    • Demo increments: SL-28 (done), SL-45 (done), SL-47 (done), SL-50 (done), SL-51 (done)

    Risks and technical debt¶

    The design and gbo-demo v0.9.0 have known risks and technical debt. The risk list carries forward the gap analysis of the archived reference architecture v0.6.2, with updates from the demo findings. Every entry names its follow-up: a decision, a hardening action, a demo issue, or an open question. Each entry links the findings (F), open questions (Q), requirements (REQ), and decisions (ADR) that it rests on.

    Overview¶

    Each risk belongs to one group:

    ID Risk Group
    R1 The ASI exists at demo grade only Routes
    R2 The SDG-OOTS bridge is design-level only Routes
    R3 No Gov-to-Gov regime and no positive evidence for it Routes

    R5 The EUDI adapter accepts unauthenticated issuance callbacks Security
    R6 No rate limiting or quota Security

    R8 Contract acceptance sees the parties but not the service Security
    R9 Demo-grade shared services Production readiness
    R10 The consent register (toestemmingsregister) is a dependency of every DvTP decision Production readiness
    R11 The demo runs one PDP for all providers Production readiness
    R12 Policy distribution has no integrity chain and no visible fallback Production readiness
    R13 The PDP mapper is a patch on OpenFTV Production readiness
    R14 New sources need a restart of the issuance server Production readiness
    R15 The legal ceiling of the service catalog (dienstencatalogus) has no technical counterpart Governance
    R16 Rego instead of ODRL Governance
    R17 GraphQL is not a recognized data service (datadienst) type of the Federatief Datastelsel (FDS) Governance

    R28 No link between the QTSP login and the source login ASI
    R29 The NL PID has no place of birth ASI
    R30 Fuzzy matching without returning a value ASI

    R33 A suspended consumer keeps access DvTP
    R34 Any connected peer can read any consent status Security

    Routes¶

    R1: The ASI exists at demo grade only¶

    • Risk: The Authentic Source Interface is built (ADR-0037), but only as a local demo stack. From January 1, 2027, the interface of CIR 2026/1735 Annex IV and the seal obligation apply (F-80).
    • Impact: Production needs these parts, which the demo does not have:
      • a qualified seal certificate and its holder (Q-17, Q-28, Q-32)
      • the national register of relying parties and access certificates (R27)
      • real identification means: the DigiD route is a mock, and the wallet verifier also trusts the development issuer CA (Q-36)
      • a decision on the role of GBO (Q-37) and on catalog registration (Q-31, Q-67)
      • a simulation deployment (#594)
    • Follow-up: Three items track this risk:
      • the proposed ADRs 0041 and 0042
      • the ASI risks R26 to R30
      • the standards feedback E1 to E10, which is not sent.
    • Related: F-80, F-84, F-87, REQ-112, SL-28.

    R2: The SDG-OOTS bridge is design-level only¶

    • Risk: The AS4 bridge for SDG-OOTS has no implementation.
    • Impact: Until the bridge is built, the EU obligation is not met.
    • Follow-up: ADR-0020, ADR-0024. It is open who builds the adapter (Q-79).
    • Related: SDG-OOTS scenario.

    R3: No Gov-to-Gov regime and no positive evidence for it¶

    • Risk: The PDP knows two regimes: consent and PID. No legal-basis regime, rule set, or legal basis (grondslag) data exists. A request without a consent proof falls in the PID regime (ADR-0031).
    • Impact: The two-path access-basis model of ADR-0004 is only half proven. A Gov-to-Gov regime cannot reuse "absence of a token" as its evidence, because the PID regime already uses it (R21).
    • Follow-up: Define the positive evidence for a legal basis. Then add a regime and a rule set.
    • Related: REQ-74, Gov-to-Gov scenario.

    Security hardening¶

    R4: The consent proof is a bearer token¶

    • Risk: The actor binding stops another consumer from using a proof. It does not stop replay by the same consumer within the validity period.
    • Impact: A stolen proof gives data access for its remaining life.
    • Follow-up: Make the validity period shorter. Bind the proof to the FSC identity with proof of possession (ADR-0032).
    • Related: REQ-68, Bearer token.

    R5: The EUDI adapter accepts unauthenticated issuance callbacks¶

    • Risk: The issuance server verifies the PID disclosure. The gap is behind it: the adapter route POST /attestations/{source}/{type} has no caller authentication (source_release_runtime.go#L69-L81, plain ListenAndServe at main.go#L700). The developer portal shows the gap: its playground posts a typed BSN straight to the adapter through /eudi-api/ (EudiQrPanel.tsx#L36-L51, nginx.conf#L36-L42).
    • Impact: Any caller that reaches the adapter can post an arbitrary BSN. The adapter calls the source over FSC as the designated issuer. As a result, the PDP allows the request, and the adapter returns the claims without any wallet. Two more gaps add to this risk:
      • nothing binds the BSN in the source query to the verified disclosure
      • the PID trust list of the issuance server also holds non-PID anchors, including the GBO development issuer CA.
    • Follow-up: Authenticate the callback (mTLS or a signed request from the issuance server), or let the adapter verify the SD-JWT itself. Bind the disclosure to the request. Restrict the PID trust list to PID issuers (REQ-45, #133). The QTSP callback already uses a secret path and CA-pinned TLS.
    • Related: F-70, Q-18, ADR-0018, SL-25 (dropped), the callback gap.

    R6: No rate limiting or quota¶

    • Risk: Authorization concern ⑤ exists only as structural checks: parse, depth, size, and coverage. Rate limiting and quota are not built.
    • Impact: Only the FSC contracts limit enumeration and abuse.
    • Follow-up: Define limits per grant. Enforce them at the Inway or the PDP (ADR-0004).
    • Related: REQ-17.

    R7: Data-chain responses are not sealed¶

    • Risk: DvTP and EUDI source responses carry no qualified electronic seal. ASI verification results carry a seal: a detached JWS (ES256, x5c) over the exact body. The ASI certificate is a development certificate and is not qualified (REQ-83).
    • Impact: Non-repudiation of a data-chain response rests on the FSC transaction log and the ADL. No seal supports it.
    • Follow-up: Decide whether every source response gets one seal, whatever the channel (Q-75). The ASI seal format waits for Q-32 (ADR-0041). The BSN in the decision logs is a separate risk (R22).
    • Related: F-80, E4.

    R8: Contract acceptance sees the parties but not the service¶

    • Risk: The autosign input carries peer IDs and grant types only.
    • Impact: At contract time, the policy cannot enforce admission per service.
    • Follow-up: An upstream FSC change. Until that change, request-time rules compensate (ADR-0015).
    • Related: F-56 (closed), REQ-62.

    R21: The absence of a consent proof selects the PID regime¶

    • Risk: A request without a consent proof is in the PID regime (engine.rego#L168-L181). The only control is the list of designated issuers per EUDI rule. A consumer on that list can skip consent: it leaves out the consent proof.
    • Impact: The PID regime rests on an identifier whose origin no one in the chain checks. A test keeps the issuer list disjoint from the DvTP consumers, but the test knows only the local consumers. For the simulation consumer, only an inspection shows that it is disjoint.
    • Follow-up: Make positive PID evidence at the point where the wallet presentation is verified. Bind this evidence to the subject of the query (REQ-45, #133, #381). Until then, test the disjointness per environment.
    • Related: F-70, REQ-74, Q-18, Q-22, ADR-0031.

    R25: Source isolation is incomplete¶

    • Risk: The rule "Decrypt only after the allow" depends on one condition: only the FSC Inway reaches the source gateway (REQ-81). In Docker Compose, the gateways publish no port and are only on source-gateways and sources. However, the source APIs (graphql-server, brp-graphql-server, lvg-graphql-server) are also on backend and fsc-infra (docker-compose.yml#L631-L636), together with the consumer backend (#L1080-L1082).
    • Impact: A party on those networks can reach a source API without the Inway, the PDP, and the gateway. The Helm chart has no NetworkPolicy. The decrypted value is not bound to one consent (no nonce).
    • Follow-up: Take the source APIs off the shared networks. Outside Compose, add a NetworkPolicy or an equal control. Add the nonce as a second safeguard (BSNk preconditions).
    • Related: F-79, REQ-21, ADR-0033, network isolation.

    R32: Only the network protects the register listener¶

    • Risk: The register listener for create, list, read, and revoke has no caller authentication. The consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) backend is its only intended caller (REQ-39). In Compose, the register is on backend (docker-compose.yml#L737-L740).
    • Impact: Any party that reaches the register directly can create or revoke consents for every citizen.
    • Follow-up: Decide between authentication of the backend and network isolation (Q-58). Isolation alone works only under one condition: the register and the backend run at one participant (Q-49).
    • Related: REQ-76 (the status listener goes over FSC).

    R34: Any connected peer can read any consent status¶

    • Risk: The status service over FSC answers every peer that has a contract for it. It does not check that the caller is the PDP of a source in the consent.
    • Impact: A connected peer with a consent_id learns its status.
    • Follow-up: Restrict the status answer to the PDPs of the sources in the consent (REQ-76, #382).
    • Related: ADR-0032.

    Privacy and audit¶

    R22: BSN in the decision logs of the EUDI and ASI routes¶

    • Risk: In the EUDI and ASI routes, the query names the citizen with the plain BSN. The PDP input, the ADL, and the console decision log hold it. Nothing masks the BSN, and the mapper stopped pseudonymizing it.
    • Impact: REQ-60 is not met for these routes. Masking alone also does not meet the requirement.
    • Follow-up: Keep identifiers out of the PDP input (ADR-0043, proposed). The decision is made in #368.
    • Related: F-54, SL-29 (reversed by PR #370), the BSN exception.

    R23: The ADL record is incomplete behind the FSC Inway¶

    • Risk: The ADL is the authoritative decision record (ADR-0036). Three parts are missing:
      • Behind the FSC Inway, the record has its own random trace and no transaction ID. The Inway passes neither to the PDP (#369).
      • The record does not name the policy version (REQ-59).
      • The record holds only the allow and the reason. It does not hold the consent status answer (F-72).
    • Impact: An auditor finds the record only through the stored request header. The auditor cannot replay the decision against a known policy.
    • Follow-up: Fix the trace headers upstream in open-fsc (ADR-0035). Record the bundle revision in the ADL.
    • Related: F-41, REQ-71, Q-25.

    R26: The QTSP can read the BSN in the ASI token¶

    • Risk: ETSI requires the identification data in the access token. In the demo, a token claim holds the BSN in readable form (tokens.go#L29).
    • Impact: The QTSP holds the token. It can read a BSN that it is not allowed to process (P-04).
    • Follow-up: Encrypt the identification data for the ASIP (#595). Send the gap to ETSI (E7).
    • Related: F-86, REQ-86, Q-36.

    ASI production gaps¶

    R27: No national register for QTSP admission¶

    • Risk: The authorization server admits a QTSP on the entitlement QEAA_Provider in the national register of relying parties. That register and its API do not exist. It is not fixed which identifier links the QTSP certificate to its entry. The demo uses a stub register file.
    • Impact: QTSPs cannot be admitted in production. If the register is unreachable during a re-check, the demo keeps the client active (fail-open). Issued tokens stay valid up to 10 minutes after a withdrawal.
    • Follow-up: Q-34 (outage behavior), Q-35 (identifier), Q-41 (tokens after withdrawal).
    • Related: F-85, REQ-88, REQ-89, E10.

    R28: No link between the QTSP login and the source login¶

    • Risk: The QTSP identifies the citizen, and the ASI authorization server identifies the citizen again. Nothing links the two. The QR route can be completed on another phone.
    • Impact: A QTSP can attest the data of person B to person A.
    • Follow-up: Add a check under CIR 2025/1569 art. 9(5). In this check, the QTSP sends its identification data for verification. As an alternative, the QTSP gives this data to the authorization server as a hint (Q-40). Send the gap to ETSI (E6).
    • Related: F-93, REQ-90, REQ-102.

    R29: The NL PID has no place of birth¶

    • Risk: CIR 2024/2977 makes the place of birth a mandatory PID attribute. The NL PID type metadata has no place of birth. As a result, the authorization server asks for four of the five mandatory attributes.
    • Impact: If the Netherlands reads "identification data" as the mandatory PID attributes, a token from the NL Wallet cannot meet that reading. DigiD gives a BSN only (F-88).
    • Follow-up: Ask the NL Wallet team. Fix the minimum identification data in the PSA (Q-36).
    • Related: F-94, REQ-86.

    R30: Fuzzy matching without returning a value¶

    • Risk: The ASIP gives MatchWithVariation and never returns the stored value. Annex IV of CIR 2026/1735 makes the value optional but keeps the fuzzy-matching requirement. The conformance matrix marks that requirement failing.
    • Impact: In a literal reading of the annex, the ASIP does not conform.
    • Follow-up: Decide whether the ASIP returns the value on a match (Q-29). Send the gap to ETSI (E2).
    • Related: F-92, REQ-85, REQ-113.

    DvTP consent¶

    R24: The consent proof freezes at consent¶

    • Risk: BSNk transforms only while the citizen is logged in (BSNK-04). As a result, the proof fixes the parties, the key versions, the BSN authorization, and the proof form for its whole validity period. The proof has no version.
    • Impact: A new source needs a new consent. A re-keyed source must keep its old keys (AV-09). A new proof form makes all outstanding proofs fail with CONSENT_CONTEXT_INVALID.
    • Follow-up: Give the proof a version. Extend the service catalog with OIN, key version, and BSN authorization per party (REQ-82, Q-77).
    • Related: F-78, ADR-0032, the proof freezes at consent.

    R31: The backend revokes a revoked consent again¶

    • Risk: A direct revoke of an expired or already revoked consent returns HTTP 200, sets REVOKED again, and writes a new LDV record (main.go#L282-L299).
    • Impact: The status history and the logbook get false entries.
    • Follow-up: Refuse the revoke with CONSENT_NOT_REVOCABLE (REQ-109, #600).
    • Related: F-97.

    R33: A suspended consumer keeps access¶

    • Risk: The request policy does not read the admission status of a direct consumer. A suspended consumer with an existing contract can still send queries under a valid consent.
    • Impact: Suspension takes effect only at the revocation of the contract.
    • Follow-up: REQ-110. Q-53 covers the time until the suspension takes effect.
    • Related: ADR-0015.

    R35: The consumer sets the consent validity¶

    • Risk: The consumer sends the validity period. The default is one year, with no upper limit. The citizen cannot change it.
    • Impact: A proof can live longer than the purpose needs. This makes R4 and R24 worse.
    • Follow-up: Decide who sets the validity period (Q-13, Q-76).
    • Related: F-11, REQ-19.

    R37: BSNk recognition of the consent facility is not settled¶

    • Risk: Only a recognized party can activate and transform (BSNK-01). It is open whether the consent facility can be that party, and in which role. The demo assumes route D: the backend derives and activates, and the register stores PI and PP.
    • Impact: Route D works only under one condition: the backend and the register are one BSNk participant. The rotation of the reference key (Q-56) and the protection of stored PI and PP (Q-57) are open.
    • Follow-up: Q-26, Q-49, and ADR-0040 (proposed).
    • Related: F-75, REQ-69.

    EUDI issuance¶

    R36: Attestations are valid 365 days without a change feed¶

    • Risk: Every attestation type gets a fixed validity of 365 days. GBO only queries sources and has no change feed.
    • Impact: If the source data changes, an issuer must revoke an attestation that is valid for 24 hours or more. GBO cannot do that.
    • Follow-up: Per type, choose short-lived attestations or a change feed with revocation (REQ-77).
    • Related: F-82, AV-12, AV-13, ADR-0028.

    Production readiness¶

    R9: Demo-grade shared services¶

    • Risk: The shared services are demo grade: the consent register runs in memory by default, DigiD is a mock, and the PKI is self-generated. The BSNk mock follows the BSNk interface (as JSON), but it encrypts nothing. The three demo sources share one OIN and one decryption component.
    • Impact: None of these services carries production trust or availability. The demo does not demonstrate unlinkability per source.
    • Follow-up: ADR-0023, ADR-0005, a replicated register store (SL-12), and a DigiD connection.
    • Related: Q-54, demo mock and production BSNk.

    R10: The consent register is a dependency of every DvTP decision¶

    • Risk: For every request, the policy asks for the consent status online, without a cache.
    • Impact: A register outage stops all consent-based traffic (fail closed).
    • Follow-up: Set the availability, latency, and propagation targets (REQ-75, Q-47). Replicate the register.
    • Related: F-61, ADR-0032.

    R11: The demo runs one PDP for all providers¶

    • Risk: The target model has a PAP and a PDP at each bronhouder (ADR-0021). The demo runs one shared PDP.
    • Impact: The demo does not show policy separation between bronhouders.
    • Follow-up: Run a PDP per provider in the simulation deployment.
    • Related: Q-21 (answered).

    R12: Policy distribution has no integrity chain and no visible fallback¶

    • Risk: By default, the PDP loads policies from a bind mount. Bundle distribution through the OpenFTV Manager is opt-in. Bundles are not signed. Signing is not planned while bundles stay inside one organization (#426). The policy store is cumulative, and one broken module stops every decision.
    • Impact: There is no integrity chain from author to runtime. There is no visible fallback to the last valid policy set.
    • Follow-up: Guidelines RL-01 and RL-05. If a bundle crosses an organization boundary, signing becomes a requirement.
    • Related: F-09, F-51, F-52, Q-21.

    R13: The PDP mapper is a patch on OpenFTV¶

    • Risk: The PDP is built from OpenFTV tag v0.1.0, with the FTV GraphQL mapper patched in.
    • Impact: Upstream changes can break the build. The patch steps fail loudly, but the maintenance cost stays.
    • Follow-up: Contribute the mapper extension point to OpenFTV upstream (ADR-0013).
    • Related: REQ-42.

    R14: New sources need a restart of the issuance server¶

    • Risk: The issuance server reads its configuration at startup.
    • Impact: Source activation needs a controlled restart.
    • Follow-up: Accepted in demo v0.9.0 (ADR-0016). If the issuance server supports reload, revisit this decision.
    • Related: REQ-64.

    Governance and standards¶

    R15: The legal ceiling of the service catalog has no technical counterpart¶

    • Risk: Rule coverage replaced the catalog artifact. The legally anchored ceiling and its governance (the Bureau DvTP process) are not defined.
    • Impact: The legal ceiling of what a consumer can ask for is not inspectable on its own.
    • Follow-up: A legal anchoring decision (ADR-0008, ADR-0009). The data-set description is one input (REQ-121).
    • Related: F-74.

    R16: Rego instead of ODRL¶

    • Risk: The PSA lists ODRL for S06. The design uses Rego, and Cedar inside the OpenFTV Manager.
    • Impact: The comply-or-explain duty is open.
    • Follow-up: Bring the deviation to the standards bodies, in line with D-13. For more information, see Policy lifecycle and Q-78.

    R17: GraphQL is not a recognized FDS data service type¶

    • Risk: The data access pillar rests on a deviation that no standard covers.
    • Follow-up: ADR-0025.

    R18: Integrator mandates have no validity and no governance¶

    • Risk: Three points of the integrator route are open. A mandate has no validity period, and the integrator is not in the proof (Q-46). The upstream act.sub deviates from RFC 8693. The route itself is built (opt-in) and has three parts (ADR-0034):
      • an FSC delegated grant
      • a mandate per integrator, provider, and rule in the admission register
      • a consent that binds the represented party.
    • Impact: A mandate stays valid until someone removes it. It is not set who admits integrators and on which terms (AV-06).
    • Follow-up: Three items are open: mandate validity, the governance of admission (Q-74), and a change log for admissions (REQ-123).
    • Related: F-73 (closed), REQ-106, Q-12.

    R19: LDV gaps: citizen view, activity register, ASIP¶

    • Risk: LDV is built: each controller logs its own processings in its own logbook (ADR-0026). These gaps remain:
      • the citizen view of processings per consent is not built (P-13)
      • the register of processing activities is a stand-in (Q-08)
      • the local dpl.gbo.* extension is not agreed (Q-72)
      • the ASIP writes no LDV records
      • no pointer leads from the ADL to the consent logbook (Q-25)
      • no retention, access model, or tamper evidence exists for the ADL the logbooks, and the FSC transaction logs (REQ-32).
    • Impact: A citizen cannot see QTSP verifications. A chain read stops at a party that does not log under LDV (F-68).
    • Follow-up: The open points of ADR-0026, and the consumer obligation (AV-02).
    • Related: REQ-72, F-64, SL-50.

    R20: Onboarding cost for small bronhouders¶

    • Risk: The cost to connect a source stays high for small organizations.
    • Impact: There is an adoption risk for municipalities and small sources.
    • Follow-up: ADR-0027.

    Accepted technical debt¶

    The design accepts the following technical debt on purpose:

    • Monetary amounts in attestations are integers, because the pinned wallet stack cannot represent non-integral values (ADR-0017).
    • Attestations have no nested claims (REQ-78).
    • The unsecured source transport exists for local development. The mount policy excludes it from deployments. The code does not exclude it.
    • The demo works around OpenFTV upstream quirks and documents them: the policy language flag, the missing policy-data APIs, and the broken policy DELETE (the demo retires a policy instead).

    Glossary¶

    The TO is written in English. Each concept has one English term. On its first use on a page, the term gets the Dutch name of the Globaal Ontwerp in parentheses, for example "consent register (toestemmingsregister)". After that, the page uses the English term only. Proper names stay as they are: Gemeenschappelijke Bronontsluiting, Delen van gegevens via Toestemming met Private dienstverleners, Globaal Ontwerp, Projectstartarchitectuur, Technisch Ontwerp, MijnOverheid, DigiD, Logius, BSN, Autorisatielijst BSN, Basisinrichting OOTS, Logboek Dataverwerkingen. One Dutch government term also stays as it is, without a translation: bronhouder.

    The following tables give each term, the Dutch name, its meaning, and the words that the TO does not use for the same concept. The style linter (scripts/style_lint.py) reports every word from a "Do not use" column in running text. A Dutch name directly inside parentheses is allowed. Code names, quotes from sources, and IDs are exempt. For the full begrippenlijst of the GBO stelsel, see the GO begrippenlijst.

    Building blocks and channels¶

    These terms follow the building block view:

    Term Dutch (GO) Meaning Do not use
    GBO Basis GBO Basis The part of GBO at every bronhouder: FSC, the PEP and the PDP, the source gateway, source configuration, and the records. It feeds every channel (GBO Basis). —
    Channel kanaal A way in which GBO serves one kind of consumer. The three channels are DvTP, EUDI wallet, and OOTS. trajectory
    Route — One end-to-end flow through a channel: the DvTP route, the PuB-EAA route, the ASI route, the SDG-OOTS route, and the Gov-to-Gov route. trajectory
    Facility voorziening A shared function that GBO or another party provides, for example the consent facility. voorziening
    Consent facility toestemmingsvoorziening The GBO facility of the DvTP channel where the citizen gives, views, and revokes consent. It consists of the consent portal and the consent register (Consent facility). toestemmingsvoorziening, consent service
    Consent portal toestemmingsportaal The citizen-facing application of the consent facility (PSA S02). It has a frontend and a backend. The short form "portal backend" is allowed. toestemmingsportaal
    Consent register toestemmingsregister The register of consents (PSA S01). It signs the consent proof and answers the consent status. toestemmingsregister
    Pseudonymization facility pseudonimiseervoorziening BSNk PP: the Logius facility that the DvTP channel uses at consent time. pseudonimiseervoorziening
    PuB-EAA provider PubEAA-voorziening The GBO block of the EUDI wallet channel that issues an attestation from source data to the wallet (PuB-EAA provider). Legally, the bronhouder is the provider. PubEAA
    Issuance facility — The technical part of the PuB-EAA provider that GBO runs: the issuance server and the EUDI adapter (ADR-0028). —
    ASI — Authentic Source Interface: the interface of ETSI TS 119 478 through which a QTSP verifies or retrieves attributes at an authentic source (eIDAS article 45e). —
    ASI provider ASI-provider The GBO block of the EUDI wallet channel that offers the ASI. It consists of the ASIP and the ASI authorization server (ASI provider). —
    OOTS adapter OOTS-adapter The GBO block of the OOTS channel that answers EU evidence requests. Design only (OOTS channel). —
    Source gateway — The component in front of a source API (code name bron-sidecar). After the allow decision, it decrypts the value for its own OIN (ADR-0033). sidecar
    Decryption component — The component of a source that reads the VI or VP for that source with its own keys. The source gateway calls it after the allow decision. —
    Admission register toelatingsregister The register of admitted participants and integrator mandates. The PDP pulls it as a PIP (code name dvtp-onboarding-register). onboarding register
    Source registry — The store of source descriptions: candidates, immutable releases, and the active release. —
    Source metadata — The description that a source publishes of its own services, at /.well-known/gbo (Source configuration). —
    EUDI adapter — The component between the issuance server and the FSC chain. In the demo, its FSC peer is called "EDI issuer" (edi-…). —
    Wallet verifier — The nl-wallet verification server that the ASI authorization server uses for a login with the NL Wallet. —
    Integrator integrator A software party that calls a source on behalf of a consumer, under an FSC delegated grant and a registered mandate (ADR-0034). —

    Domain terms¶

    Term Dutch (GO) Meaning Do not use
    Bronhouder bronhouder The government organization responsible for an authentic register and the access to it. The TO keeps this Dutch government term, also in English text, without translation. source holder
    Source bron A system of a bronhouder that answers queries. —
    Source access bronontsluiting The provision of register data through a standard interface. bronontsluiting
    Citizen burger The data subject in GBO flows. —
    Consent toestemming The informed agreement of the citizen to a specific data exchange. —
    Consumer afnemer An organization that asks a bronhouder for data, in any channel. afnemer
    Service provider dienstverlener The private party that is the consumer in the DvTP channel. dienstverlener
    Controller Verantwoordelijke The party that decides on a processing (AVG). Under LDV, each controller keeps its own logbook. —
    Data subject Betrokkene The person whom a processing is about (AVG and LDV term). —
    Data set gegevensset A named group of fields that a consent covers as a whole (REQ-10). gegevensset
    Service catalog dienstencatalogus The legally anchored register of the maximum scope that a consumer can ask for per use case. See ADR-0008. dienstencatalogus
    Purpose limitation doelbinding Processing of data is allowed only for the stated purpose. —
    Legal basis grondslag The legal ground for a processing or a provision of data. A legal basis set directly by law is a statutory basis (wettelijke grondslag). grondslag
    Interface koppelvlak A specified technical interface between parties or components. koppelvlak
    Interaction pattern interactiepatroon One of the patterns of the GO: A (EUDI wallet), B (OOTS), C (DvTP). interactiepatronen
    Processing verwerking Any operation on personal data (AVG term). —

    Consent, identity, and pseudonyms¶

    Term Meaning Do not use
    Consent proof The signed gbo-consent+jwt that the toestemmingsregister issues. It carries an encrypted value per source (encrypted_subject), the scopes, and the consumer (ADR-0032). —
    Consent token The same JWT as it travels in X-GBO-Consent-Token, before the PDP verified it. The evidence that selects the consent regime is a consent token. —
    Placeholder The value that a dienstverlener puts in the query in place of the citizen: consent:identity or consent:pseudonym. The source gateway replaces it after the allow decision (REQ-79). —
    Regime The basis on which the PDP judges a request. The evidence in the request selects it (ADR-0031). With a consent token, the consent regime applies. Without one, the PID regime applies. —
    Designated issuer An FSC peer on the actor list of the EUDI rules. Only a designated issuer can ask for source data under the PID regime. —
    Mandate (acts_for) The registration in the admission register that an integrator acts for a consumer and a rule. The PDP reads it at request time. —
    BSN authorization list The BSNk list (Autorisatielijst BSN) of the parties that are allowed to receive the BSN. A source on the list gets a VI in the consent proof. Other sources get only a VP. —
    PI Polymorphic identity. A BSNk value made for the requester (the toestemmingsportaal) from the BSN. The toestemmingsregister stores it under the subject_ref. Recipients get a VI made from it. —
    PP Polymorphic pseudonym. Like the PI, but for pseudonyms. Recipients get a VP made from it. —
    VI Encrypted identity. A BSN that BSNk encrypted for one recipient OIN and one key version. Only that recipient can read it. —
    VP Encrypted pseudonym. A pseudonym that BSNk encrypted for one recipient OIN and one key version. The BSNk specification calls it EP. —
    subject_ref The reference under which the toestemmingsvoorziening knows a citizen: a keyed HMAC of the BSN (route D). It is not a BSNk value. —
    Peer ID The identifier of an FSC peer. It is different from the OIN of the organization (REQ-67). —

    Records and tracing¶

    Term Meaning Do not use
    Decision record One ADL record: the authoritative record of a PDP decision (ADR-0036). —
    Console decision log The log of the policy engine that goes to Loki. It holds the detail per field, but it is observability, not audit. —
    LDV logbook The logbook of one controller, with one record per processing (ADR-0026). —
    FSC txlog The transaction log of an FSC peer (FSC-Logging): the authoritative record of transport. —
    W3C Trace Context The traceparent and tracestate headers. The trace ID in traceparent is the correlation key of the chain (ADR-0035). —

    Abbreviations¶

    Term Meaning
    ADL Authorization Decision Log. The Logius standard for the record of an authorization decision. In GBO, the ADL is the authoritative record of every PDP decision.
    ASIP Authentic Source Interface Provider. The GBO service that offers verify and retrieve as specified in ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1. It calls the source over FSC (ADR-0037).
    AuthZEN The OpenID standard for the evaluation interface from PEP to PDP.
    AVG Algemene verordening gegevensbescherming (GDPR).
    AZSP The ASI authorization server. It registers QTSPs, lets the citizen approve by logging in, and issues DPoP-bound access tokens.
    BSN Burgerservicenummer. The citizen identification number, restricted to authorized parties.
    BSNk PP BSN-koppelregister polymorphic pseudonymization. The Logius facility that turns a BSN into encrypted values per recipient. GBO uses it only at consent time (ADR-0005).
    DIP Discover Interface Provider. The party that publishes the data service records of ASIPs. The demo has a stub.
    DPoP Demonstrating Proof of Possession (RFC 9449). It binds an access token to a key of the client.
    DvTP Delen van gegevens via Toestemming met Private dienstverleners. The consent-based channel.
    EUDI wallet European Digital Identity wallet (eIDAS2).
    FSC Federated Service Connectivity. The connectivity standard, with Inway, Outway, Manager, directory, and contracts.
    FSC Manager The FSC component of each peer that negotiates contracts and signs access tokens. It is different from the OpenFTV Manager.
    FTV, OpenFTV Federatieve Toegangsverlening. The authorization framework that hosts the PDP.
    GBO Gemeenschappelijke Bronontsluiting.
    Gov-to-Gov The route in which a government consumer gets data on a legal basis, without consent. Design only.
    LDV Logboek Dataverwerkingen. The Logius standard (v1.0.0) that records each processing in the logbook of its controller.
    OIN Organisatie-identificatienummer. The organization identifier, bound to PKI certificates.
    OOTS Once-Only Technical System. The EU cross-border evidence exchange under the SDG-verordening.
    OpenFTV Manager The policy administration component of OpenFTV. It stores policies and serves bundles to the PDP. It is different from the FSC Manager.
    OpenID4VCI, OpenID4VP Protocols for credential issuance and presentation.
    PAP Policy Administration Point. It authors and distributes policies.
    PBAC Policy-based access control.
    PDP Policy Decision Point. It evaluates authorization requests.
    PEP Policy Enforcement Point. It enforces PDP decisions. In this design, the FSC Inway is the PEP.
    PID Person Identification Data. The identity attestation in the EUDI wallet.
    PIP Policy Information Point. It supplies data to the PDP: the consent status and the admission register.
    PuB-EAA Public Body Electronic Attestation of Attributes.
    QEAA Qualified Electronic Attestation of Attributes.
    QTSP Qualified Trust Service Provider. In the ASI route, the QTSP is an OAuth client of the AZSP, not an FSC participant.
    QEAA_Provider The entitlement in the national register of relying parties that a QTSP needs to become an ASI client.
    SD-JWT VC The selective-disclosure JWT verifiable credential format (dc+sd-jwt).
    VCT Verifiable credential type identifier. It is published with vct#integrity over immutable Type Metadata.

    Traceability terms¶

    Term Meaning
    BSNk precondition (BSNK-NN) A fact about BSNk PP that the design must respect. It is not a requirement on GBO (BSNk preconditions).
    Connection condition (AV-NN) A demand on a party that connects to GBO, not on GBO. The TO holds candidates for the management organization (connection conditions).
    Demo increment (SL-NN) A bounded piece of demo work with its result (increments). The ID keeps the old prefix SL.
    Finding (F-NN) An observation from building the demo: a design gap, an exposed design choice, an implicit requirement, or an erratum (findings).
    Guideline (RL-NN) A recommendation to bronhouders, for example on policy management. Not a demand on GBO (policy management).
    Open question (Q-NN) A question that the demo cannot answer, with the forum that must answer it and the working assumption until then (open questions).
    Quality scenario (QS-NN) A testable scenario for a quality goal (quality requirements).
    Requirement (REQ-NN) A testable demand on what GBO builds or on its interfaces (requirements).
